Twelve thousand years ago, Eldre'Thalas served as a wondrous bastion for Queen Azshara's favored sorcerers, the Shen'dralar. When the Well of Eternity collapsed during the Great Sundering, Prince Tortheldrin wove a magical barrier that shielded the city from ruin. Severed from their source of magic, the surviving Highborne trapped a colossal demon named Immol'thar beneath their sanctum, siphoning its fel essence to sustain their immortality and arcane powers for millennia.

subzone:direforge-hill.text: Direforge Hill. Hostile Dark Iron dwarves hold Direforge Hill in the northeastern Wetlands, southeast of Dun Modr and northeast of the Green Belt. Dark Iron dwarves hold the northeastern Wetlands hill under Balgaras the Foul, a Dark Iron dwarf warlock. Their encampment lies southeast of Dun Modr. Travelers crossing the northeastern Wetlands face the hostile Dark Iron encampment on Direforge Hill. Balgaras the Foul commands the dwarves there.

subzone:dragonmaw-gates.text: Dragonmaw Gates. At the Dragonmaw Gates, heavy fortifications bar the road climbing from the eastern Wetlands. They guard the ascent to Grim Batol, a mountain fortress in the cursed dwarven ruins. Carved into rugged peaks along the eastern Wetlands, the Dragonmaw Gates seal the winding road to Grim Batol. The barriers take their name from the Dragonmaw orcs, who held the dwarven mountain city during the Second War. The road remains a fortified checkpoint, and the ascent still brings danger. Powerful drakes haunt the pass, while grim reminders of the clan's dark history linger in the mountains. The Dragonmaw orcs were broken and scattered after the Demon Soul was destroyed, but the mountain path remains dangerous. Powerful red dragons have been seen watching the winding slopes and perches around the gates. Monstrous drakes and Dragonmaw remnants still lurk in the nearby hills, and the gates remain a firm barrier against travelers bold enough to venture into the heights.

subzone:dragonmurk.text: Dragonmurk. Dragonmurk is a sprawling, hazardous tract of southern Dustwallow Marsh swarming with black dragonspawn and hatchlings. Flanked by ancient ogre ruins and scorched caverns, it serves as the hostile outer perimeter for the brood of Onyxia. Spanning the southern interior of Dustwallow Marsh, the Dragonmurk marks the threshold where damp wetlands give way to the dominion of the black dragonflight. The waterways and thick mud here crawl with black wyrmkins, dragonspawn, and ravenous whelps. The surrounding landscape has suffered deeply from their presence; adjacent territories such as the ruined village of Stonemaul and the scorched cavern known as the Den of Flame have both fallen completely under the flight's territorial grip.

subzone:dreadmaul-post.text: Dreadmaul Post. Dreadmaul Post is an entrenched ogre settlement situated in the scorched wastes of the Blasted Lands. Established by the Dreadmaul clan, this mound serves as a fortified redoubt near the Dark Portal where ogres have lingered since their arrival from Draenor. Travelers passing through the region must contend with these fierce brutes and the treacherous terrain surrounding their encampment. When the Horde surged through the Dark Portal in decades past, clans of ogres marched alongside them into Azeroth. The Dreadmaul clan chose to dig in near the gateway itself, raising crude stone mounds and earthworks across the red wastes of the Blasted Lands. Dreadmaul Post stands as one of their primary outposts, maintaining a firm grip over the badlands and clashing with wandering beasts and any travelers foolish enough to draw near their territory.

subzone:dreadmaul-rock.text: Dreadmaul Rock. Dreadmaul Rock is a towering crag and cave complex rising out of the fiery wastes of the Burning Steppes. It serves as the primary base of operations for the Firegut ogres, who make their home within its winding, subterranean mounds. Towering above the scorched plains of the Burning Steppes, Dreadmaul Rock is a massive stone formation carved out by a labyrinthine cave system. Though its name hints at a possible connection to the Dreadmaul ogres of the Blasted Lands, the rock is held firmly by the Firegut clan. These brutish ogres use the elevated paths, crags, and interior earthen mounds as a defended encampment, dominating the surrounding wasteland and menacing anyone attempting to traverse the northern slopes toward Blackrock Spire.

subzone:dreadmurk-shore.text: Dreadmurk Shore. Dreadmurk Shore encompasses the foggy coastline and scattered islands of Dustwallow Marsh running north toward the Barrens. Dominated by aggressive Mirefin murlocs and sea beasts, these treacherous waters have recently become the hiding ground for shipwrecked Defias Brotherhood outlaws. Stretching along the northeastern edge of Dustwallow Marsh between Theramore Isle and Northwatch Hold, Dreadmurk Shore is a dismal expanse of muddy shoals, tide pools, and misty islands. The coast is overrun by the Mirefin tribe, a territorial clan of murlocs that aggressively attacks any travelers nearing their coastal villages. Sea turtles and aquatic predators prowl the shallows, making the shoreline dangerous to navigate even without factoring in the surrounding swamplands.

subzone:dream-bough.text: Dream Bough. Dream Bough is a colossal Great Tree nestled on an island in the center of Jademir Lake in northern Feralas. The ancient tree shelters a mysterious gateway connecting Azeroth directly to the Emerald Dream. Green dragons loyally watch over the sanctuary, keeping unwanted intruders away from its verdant boughs. Rising high above the canopy of northern Feralas, the Dream Bough stands as the largest tree in the region. Situated in the tranquil waters of Jademir Lake, the towering sentinel houses a natural portal carved into its trunk, providing a direct threshold into the untamed Emerald Dream. Because of its connection to the Emerald Dream, the tree is under the vigilant protection of the Green Dragonflight. Dragonkin and drakes patrol the banks of Jademir Lake and the approaches to the great trunk. While primarily a place of contemplation and slumber for druids wandering between realms, travelers should approach with care, as the green dragons tolerate few uninvited visitors near such an important threshold.

subzone:drowned-reef.text: Drowned Reef. The Drowned Reef is a treacherous stretch of coastal waters off the southern cliffs of the Arathi Highlands. Beneath the waves lie ancient sunken ruins, claimed by hostile Daggerspine naga who appear able to control the bay's tides, endangering passing vessels. Just outside the hidden entrance to Faldir's Cove, the Drowned Reef forms a watery graveyard for navigators. Shattered ships, including the Maiden's Folly and the Spirit of Silverpine, lie submerged beneath the waves. Daggerspine naga led by Prince Nazjak inhabit the reef and appear able to control the bay's tides, dooming crews seeking refuge in the cove. Those brave or foolish enough to dive into the deep water will discover the submerged architecture of an ancient elven city. Calcified elven gems remain among its drowned ruins.

subzone:drowned-sacellum.text: Drowned Sacellum. At Blackfathom Deeps' entrance, the Drowned Sacellum lies submerged beneath the coast. Brackish saltwater and cavern roots surround its broken stones, now occupied by murlocs and makrura. You enter the Drowned Sacellum just beyond Blackfathom Deeps' threshold. The chapel once offered quiet worship to Elune, but it has long since collapsed into the sea-swept abyss beneath Ashenvale's coast. Brackish pools swallow its ancient marble flagstones, where starfish cling beneath the cavern ceiling's massive roots. Dark wisps flicker dimly through the gloom, lighting a broken stone path. Careful steps along it lead deeper into the temple complex, toward the Pool of Ask'ar. Night elf caretakers left the Drowned Sacellum long ago, and shoreline scavengers now hold the ruins. Packs of aggressive murlocs and heavily armored makrura share the murky waters and attack anyone who disturbs their nesting grounds. Darker cultic threats lie deeper in the temple, but these predators guard the first stretch of the underground ruins.

subzone:drywhisker-gorge.text: Drywhisker Gorge. Drywhisker Gorge is a rugged cleft in the eastern mountains of the Arathi Highlands, situated northeast of the Horde outpost of Hammerfall. The gorge and its inner cavern are held by a hostile clan of kobolds, who fiercely guard rich mineral deposits and ancient elemental relics buried deep underground. Tucked away in the mountainous folds east of Hammerfall, Drywhisker Gorge serves as the primary redoubt of the Drywhisker clan of kobolds. While kobolds are often dismissed as simple mine pests, the Drywhiskers in Arathi are heavily entrenched. They guard their subterranean passages with fierce territorial tenacity, working veins of rare Lesser Bloodstone Ore and defending the deep recesses of the earth. Their proximity makes them a persistent nuisance to the nearby orcs of Hammerfall.

subzone:dun-mandarr.text: Dun Mandarr. Dun Mandarr is an abandoned dwarven camp situated before an icy cavern in south-eastern Winterspring. Established by the dwarf Jaron Stoneshaper, the site now sits in ruins after its occupants fled an onslaught of enraged local moonkin. Bearing the traditional dwarven prefix 'Dun', Dun Mandarr was established by the explorer Jaron Stoneshaper as a base of operations in the frozen reaches of southeastern Winterspring. Stoneshaper's curiosity proved his undoing when he uncovered a relic known as the Blue-Feathered Amulet. The artifact's disturbance provoked the fury of the native wildkin, who descended upon the encampment in an uncontrollable rage. Overwhelmed and driven out, the dwarves abandoned the camp entirely. Today, no friendly souls remain among the snowbanks; ferocious, territorial moonkin guard the cavern and prowl the broken shelters.

subzone:dunemaul-compound.text: Dunemaul Compound. Dunemaul Compound serves as the central settlement and ogre mound for the Dunemaul clan in Tanaris. Tucked into the rocky ridges bordering the desert wastes, it houses the clan's brute enforcers and spellcasters. Carved into the rugged desert rock of western Tanaris, the Dunemaul Compound is the primary stronghold of the Dunemaul ogres. These hulking desert dwellers have adapted to the harsh arid climate, scratching out an existence through brute force and opportunism. The compound itself centers on an ogre mound and cave network. Though primitive, the clan fields a dangerous mix of warriors, enforcers, and twisted spellcasters practicing dark warlock and mage magics. For travelers journeying across the dunes, the settlement is a treacherous den of aggressive giants who violently reject uninvited guests.

subzone:dustbowl.text: Dustbowl. The Dustbowl is a sprawling, arid expanse in the northwestern Badlands, lying between the Horde outpost of Kargath and the central Valley of Fangs. Swept by scouring desert winds, it is a harsh wilderness populated by scavengers, prowling beasts, and wandering elementals. It is also the site of Camp Wurg, making it a frequent crossing point for travelers braving the wasteland. Stretching across the northwest of the Badlands, the Dustbowl is characterized by dry gulches, cracked clay, and relentless winds that stir up choking plumes of grit. Despite the barren landscape, tough desert flora persists in the form of hardy cacti and scattered, gnarled trees. The open flatland presents constant danger to unguided wayfarers, who must contend with predatory coyotes, circling buzzards, and living rock elementals born of the rugged earth. Tucked within this scrubland lies Camp Wurg, providing a recognizable landmark amidst the otherwise desolate expanse.

subzone:dustfire-valley.text: Dustfire Valley. Dustfire Valley is a dry, windswept gulch nestled along the northern edge of the Searing Gorge. It serves as the scorched threshold leading directly to the fortified gate of Stonewrought Pass, which bars the mountain route into Loch Modan. Tucked away in northern Searing Gorge, Dustfire Valley is defined by choking ash, brittle rock, and barren canyon walls. Its most notable feature is the imposing, locked dwarven gateway sealing Stonewrought Pass. Because of these locked iron doors, direct travel north into the Valley of Kings and Loch Modan remains entirely barred to ordinary wanderers, leaving the valley an isolated cul-de-sac amidst the sulfurous wastes.

subzone:dustwallow-bay.text: Dustwallow Bay. Dustwallow Bay is an inlet of the Great Sea tucked between the sodden coast of Dustwallow Marsh and the fortified port of Theramore Isle. Its brackish coastal shallows teem with marine life, treacherous shoals, and secluded coves just off the main maritime routes of eastern Kalimdor. Dustwallow Bay defines the coastal boundary where the stagnant, murky wetlands of Dustwallow Marsh meet the open waters of the Great Sea. Flanked to the east by Theramore Isle, the bay serves as an oceanic approach for vessels arriving at Lady Jaina Proudmoore's island haven. Despite heavy maritime traffic running to and from the docks, the surrounding coastline remains wild and hazardous, pocked with rocky outcrops, murloc encampments, and tucked-away inlets like Tidefury Cove. While the marsh itself is infested with crocolisks and hostile beasts, the bay's islands and inlets draw those who seek isolation and rich catches. The small islets dotting the waters near Tidefury Cove provide a secluded retreat for anglers, most notably the legendary fisherman Nat Pagle, who can often be found angling off the rocks away from the bustling city of Theramore.

subzone:eastern-strand.text: Eastern Strand. Daggerspine naga hold the Eastern Strand along Hillsbrad's southeastern coast. The beaches and shallows reach toward the Arathi Highlands border. The Daggerspine naga hold the Eastern Strand on Hillsbrad's southeastern edge. Across the bay lies the Western Strand. Southshore and Tarren Mill clash over the region's human farms, while the naga dominate these sandy flats and tidelines. They come from the Great Sea, crossing the sandbars and settling among rocky outcrops. From there, they watch the mainland.

subzone:eastmoon-ruins.text: Eastmoon Ruins. The Eastmoon Ruins are an ancient troll archaeological site situated in eastern Tanaris, perched just west of the Gaping Chasm. Once built by the desert empires of old, the crumbling stone masonry is now occupied by Dunemaul ogres using the remnants as a desert encampment. Rising out of the blistering desert floor just west of the insect-infested Gaping Chasm, the Eastmoon Ruins preserve the crumbling architecture of ancient troll civilization. Decaying pillars, weathered stone plazas, and sun-bleached monuments hint at a time long before the sands swallowed this region. Rather than scholars or troll descendants tending the shrines, the site is firmly held by the Dunemaul ogres, who rely on the broken walls for shelter and vantage over nearby trade routes.

subzone:eastwall-gate.text: Eastwall Gate. Eastwall Gate is a fortified side entrance set into the perimeter wall of the fallen city of Stratholme. Located in the northern reaches of the Eastern Plaguelands, it offers a direct secondary access point into Stratholme's interior ruins, bypassing the chaos of the city's main gates. While the grand main entrance of Stratholme opens directly onto King's Square, the Eastwall Gate pierces the city's eastern fortifications. Barred securely against intruders, this gateway leads straight into Elders' Square, close by the steps of Alonsus Chapel. For those venturing into the burning heart of the Scourge stronghold, bypassing the front barricades can mean the difference between a swift strike into the city's depths and a meatgrinder assault through the forward undead lines. Gaining entry through the Eastwall Gate is no simple matter. It is sealed tightly by heavy ironwork that requires the Key to the City, recovered from inside Stratholme itself, or an exceptionally skilled infiltrator capable of picking masterwork locks. Once past the threshold, a heavy mechanical lever mounted on the inner wall allows travelers to raise the portcullis from the inside, opening a reliable path for allies to follow.

subzone:eastwall-tower.text: Eastwall Tower. Eastwall Tower is a ruined Lordaeron scout tower situated in the Eastern Plaguelands near the eastern road. Sacked during the Third War when the Scourge swept across the kingdom, its remains overlook the Scourge-infested wilderness. Built as a border sentinel for the kingdom of Lordaeron, Eastwall Tower once watched over travelers heading toward the far reaches of the realm. When the Scourge invaded during the Third War, the outpost was crushed along with the surrounding settlements, leaving shattered stone arches and burnt timber behind. Now, with the Lich King's armies still infesting the region, the tower's elevated position makes it an indispensable forward post. Its ruined ramparts overlook roads through the Scourge-infested countryside.

subzone:eldreth-row.text: Eldreth Row. Eldreth Row comprises the soaring, ruined outer halls forming the western entrance to Dire Maul in Feralas. Once a grand threshold of ancient Eldre'Thalas, the area is now choked with overgrowth and fiercely patrolled by Gordunni ogres. Standing as the outermost perimeter of ancient Eldre'Thalas, Eldreth Row is an imposing avenue of high-arched elven architecture that sits just outside the deeper quarters and the Broken Commons. Centuries of neglect have cracked its stonework, allowing the creeping flora of Feralas to reclaim its colonnades. Today, the pristine majesty of the Highborne has been replaced by the crude dominance of the Gordunni ogres, who use the halls as an outer staging ground, guarding the paths leading east toward the Warpwood Quarter and west past the Dire Pool.

subzone:emerald-sanctuary.text: Emerald Sanctuary. The Emerald Sanctuary is an outpost of the Cenarion Circle situated at the southern entrance of Felwood. Here, night elven and tauren druids unite to study the pervasive demonic taint and attempt the arduous task of healing the corrupted woodland. Perched on the southern edge of Felwood near the Ashenvale border, the Emerald Sanctuary serves as the primary base of operations for the Cenarion Circle in this blighted wilderness. Unlike the bitter factional conflicts burning across Kalimdor, this sanctuary offers a neutral foothold where druids look past politics to focus entirely on ecological restoration. From here, researchers track corrupted flora and direct investigations toward Jaedenar, seeking any viable method to cleanse the poisoned soil.

subzone:ethel-rethor.text: Ethel Rethor. Ethel Rethor is an ancient night elven ruin situated along the rugged northwestern coast of Desolace. While a solitary, sealed tower still rises above the waves, the majority of the sunken settlement now lies submerged in the sea and overrun by hostile naga. Perched on the desolate coast of western Kalimdor, Ethel Rethor stands as a haunting reminder of the ancient night elven civilization that flourished before the Great Sundering. Much of the grand architecture has collapsed into the ocean depths, leaving only shattered foundations and a lone, weathered tower protruding from the surf. A small bridge extends toward the tower's sealed portal, but the structure remains shut tight against the elements and intruders alike. The submerged chambers and surrounding shallows have become a stronghold for coastal naga, making the waters treacherous for any who wander near. Despite its remote location and serpentine infestation, Ethel Rethor draws travelers interested in Kalimdor's forgotten histories and ongoing threats. An agent of the Argent Dawn, Azore Aldamort, maintains a watchful presence near the ruins, monitoring the naga menace and offering aid to intrepid adventurers willing to dive into the sunken passages. Between the aquatic dangers offshore and the barren wastes inland, the ruins serve as a lonely coastal crossroads.

subzone:everlook.text: Everlook. Everlook is a snow-swept trading outpost in central Winterspring established by the Steamwheedle Cartel. Situated at the crossroads of the snowy valley's routes, it serves as a neutral haven for merchants, prospectors, and researchers braving the high-altitude cold. Everlook represents the Steamwheedle Cartel's northernmost endeavor, mirroring outposts like Gadgetzan and Booty Bay under a blanket of permafrost. The walled settlement perches at the intersection of Winterspring's snowdrifts, operating under strictly enforced neutrality. It hosts the only operational bank and shared auction house services in the region, drawing both Alliance and Horde travelers in search of warmth and shelter. Guarded by hired bruisers, the town offers refuge from ferocious frostsabers and yetis. Beneath its icy wooden roofs and whimsical penguin wallpaper, Everlook is a hotbed of technological curiosity. It houses specialized engineering workshops and advanced alchemical laboratories where goblin tinkerers push the boundaries of their craft away from prying eyes. Outside diplomacy has also begun knocking on the frost-rimmed gates; the Argent Dawn recently dispatched Gregor Greystone here to negotiate directly with town leadership, keeping a wary watch on the region's ancient ruins and gathering northern threats.

subzone:faldir-s-cove.text: Faldir's Cove. Faldir's Cove is a secluded natural harbor nestled along the southern coastline of the Arathi Highlands. Steeped in human history, it is traditionally remembered as the departure point from which early settlers sailed south to found Stormwind. Today, it serves as an emergency shelter for stranded Blackwater Raiders whose fleet ran afoul of local hazards. Tucked away behind the rugged bluffs south of Stromgarde Keep, Faldir's Cove is linked to the mainland by a concealed cave tunnel. The cove honors the memory of Faldir, the ancient Arathor explorer whose expedition set sail from these very shores to cross the Great Sea and establish the southern kingdom of Stormwind. In the present day, however, its quiet waters house a very different crowd: an expedition of Blackwater Raiders from Booty Bay, led by Captains Steelgut and O'Breen, who sailed north pursuing ancient elven treasures only to end up trapped in the bay. The Blackwater venture turned catastrophic upon reaching the Arathi coast. Strange and unnatural tides conjured by the territorial naga dwelling on the offshore Drowned Reef shattered two of their three vessels. Only the Harbinger survived intact, limping into Faldir's Cove. With the naga prowling the waters and their navigation charts resting beneath the waves, the surviving pirates and their gnomish researchers find themselves marooned, reliant on neutral travelers to battle the aquatic horrors and recover sunken salvage.

subzone:fallow-sanctuary.text: Fallow Sanctuary. The Fallow Sanctuary is a secluded village hidden deep within the bogs of the Swamp of Sorrows. It serves as home to an isolated tribe of mutated draenei known as the Lost Ones, whose severe grief and homesickness have driven them feral. Tucked away among the sunken trees of the Swamp of Sorrows, the Fallow Sanctuary was established by stranded Lost Ones seeking a place of their own. Severed from their ancestral world and deformed by dark energies, these wretched outcasts found no peace in the marshland. Over time, relentless sorrow and isolation shattered their sanity, reducing the tribe to a hostile, feral state where they fiercely attack any outsiders who trespass into their village. The settlement was once guided by figures like Ongeku and Noboru the Cudgel, though the village's leadership crumbled following their absence and demise.

subzone:feathermoon-stronghold.text: Feathermoon Stronghold. Feathermoon Stronghold is the premier night elf military base in southern Kalimdor, situated securely on Sardor Isle off the Forgotten Coast of Feralas. Commanded by General Shandris Feathermoon, this fortified outpost projects Sentinel strength across the wild forest and keeps watch over regional threats. Perched on Sardor Isle across the channel from Feralas's mainland, Feathermoon Stronghold serves as the primary strategic base for the Sentinels in southern Kalimdor. Built among ancient elven groves and supplied with a sacred moonwell, the fortress houses archers, huntresses, and support staff under the direct supervision of General Shandris Feathermoon. From this insular sanctuary, the night elves project their influence over the verdant interior of Feralas, guarding against demonic corruption, hostile wildlife, and encroaching Horde expeditions. Because the mainland of Feralas is thick with savage beasts, Gordunni ogres, and the tainted shadows of Dire Maul, Sardor Isle provides an essential defensive buffer. Alliance travelers rely on the ferry crossing from the Forgotten Coast to reach its fortified docks, repair their gear, and gather intelligence. The presence of Shandris Feathermoon—General of the Sentinels and High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind's trusted right hand—ensures that the stronghold remains an unassailable redoubt against all enemies of the kaldorei.

subzone:feathermoon-stronghold-classic.text: Feathermoon Stronghold (Classic). Feathermoon Stronghold is a fortified night elf bastion situated on Sardor Isle off the western shores of Feralas. Established by General Shandris Feathermoon, it serves as the Alliance's primary staging ground and military anchor in southern Kalimdor. Perched on Sardor Isle just off the Forgotten Coast, Feathermoon Stronghold stands as a crucial bulwark for the Night Elves and the broader Alliance. Built under the direction of General Shandris Feathermoon—Tyrande Whisperwind's trusted lieutenant for ten millennia—the fortress projects Sentinel power deep into southern Kalimdor. Its isolated island geography shields it from the beasts, ogres, and Horde interlopers prowling the primeval jungles of mainland Feralas. Given its insular position, Feathermoon relies heavily on sea and air links to maintain logistics. A small passenger boat regularly shuttles travellers across the channel between Sardor Isle and the Forgotten Coast dock. For distant travel, a dedicated hippogryph roost ties the stronghold directly to major Alliance hubs, including Thalanaar on the Thousand Needles border, Nijel's Point in the Desolace highlands, and Auberdine in the north.

subzone:felpaw-village.text: Felpaw Village. Felpaw Village is a corrupted furbolg settlement nestled in the far northern reaches of Felwood, guarding the mountain path leading directly to Timbermaw Hold. Inhabited by the fallen Deadwood tribe, its huts and gathering grounds are tainted by demonic influence and hostile to all outsiders. Situated at the northern edge of Felwood, Felpaw Village serves as the primary northern redoubt for the fallen Deadwood furbolgs. Once gentle forest wardens, the tribe fell victim to the demonic blight unleashed during the Third War, driving them into a state of feral madness. Now, the village stands as a blighted enclave filled with crude huts, ritual totems, and hostile warriors who attack anyone wandering near the tunnel entrance to Timbermaw Hold. The proximity of Felpaw Village to the sacred entrance of Timbermaw Hold makes it a critical threat to the few uncorrupted furbolgs remaining in the region. The Timbermaw guards posted at the northern mouth of Felwood view their fallen cousins with a mixture of mourning and vigilance, frequently calling upon travelers to cull the Deadwood ranks, seize their ritual fetishes, and keep the corruption from spilling through the gates into Moonglade and Winterspring.

subzone:felstone-field.text: Felstone Field. Felstone Field is a blighted farmstead located in the northwestern Western Plaguelands. Once a thriving piece of Lordaeron agricultural land, it has been claimed by the Scourge and anchored by a plague cauldron spewing toxic fumes across the ruined soil. Before the Third War, Felstone Field was a peaceful, productive family farm feeding the citizens of Lordaeron. When the plague swept through the north, the homestead fell swiftly to the Cult of the Damned and the Scourge. Today, the fields sprout dead weeds and creeping rot instead of grain. At the heart of the farmland sits an enormous plague cauldron, continuously churning foul vapors into the sky under the watch of Cauldron Lord Bilemaw and legions of skeletal flayers, sorcerers, and ravenous ghouls.

subzone:feral-scar-vale.text: Feral Scar Vale. Feral Scar Vale is a rocky gorge tucked within the High Wilderness of western Feralas. Overrun by territorial Feral Scar yetis, its cavernous tunnels are notoriously perilous to travelers who venture off the overgrown forest trails. Situated amid the thick foliage and sheer cliffs of the High Wilderness, Feral Scar Vale serves as the primary den for the savage Feral Scar yetis. While yetis are common in the snowy peaks of Alterac and Dun Morogh, these primal brutes have adapted completely to the wild, humid climate of Feralas. They fiercely defend the vale's cave network, hoarding bone trophies and aggressively driving off any intruders who wander into their hunting grounds. Beyond the primal danger of the yetis, the deeper recesses of Feral Scar Vale hide unexpected oddities. Gnomish engineering distress signals have occasionally been tracked into these dark caverns, where lost exploratory devices—such as stranded robotic survey chickens—have ended up trapped by the ferocious beasts, awaiting activation and extraction.

subzone:fire-plume-ridge.text: Fire Plume Ridge. Fire Plume Ridge is the active volcano rising directly from the center of Un'Goro Crater. Its searing slopes and subterranean magma channels fuel the crater's geysers and steam pools while playing host to fierce fire elementals. Towering over the primeval basin of Un'Goro, Fire Plume Ridge stands in sharp contrast to the surrounding lush jungle. Lava steadily cascades down its scorched rock faces, carving a landscape of ash and basalt. Subterranean magma arteries spiderweb outward beneath the soil from the ridge, fueling the bubbling geysers and hot springs scattered across the basin. The oppressive heat here is legendary—far exceeding ordinary volcanic temperatures according to goblin measuring devices—making it perilous for ill-prepared explorers to wander without ample water and shade. The volcano is an elemental furnace teeming with living flame. Living flares and roving fire elementals patrol the glowing flows, drawn to the concentration of pure subterranean heat. Deep within a cavern near the volcanic summit resides Blazerunner, the undisputed master among Un'Goro's elemental denizens. Venturing high up the ridge means navigating both lethal heat and volatile elemental spirits that aggressively defend their fiery domain.

subzone:firewatch-ridge.text: Firewatch Ridge. Firewatch Ridge is a high volcanic bluff in the northern reaches of Searing Gorge, serving as a primary encampment for the Dark Iron dwarves. Looming directly above the vast excavation known as the Cauldron, the ridge is heavily fortified by dwarven sentries, mechanical golems, and nesting fire spiders. To the northwest, an ominous cave system reveals an entrenched presence of the Twilight's Hammer cult. Perched above the industrial devastation of the Cauldron, Firewatch Ridge functions as a critical staging ground for the Dark Iron clan's operations in Searing Gorge. Dwarven guards, engineers, and molten golem creations patrol the crags, fiercely defending their foothold alongside venomous flame spiders native to the smoldering rocks. Its elevation provides the Dark Irons an unobstructed view of the surrounding ash plains, ensuring early warning against rival incursions from Ironforge or the Thorium Brotherhood. Tucked away in the northwestern reaches of the ridge lies an underground cave network claimed by the Twilight's Hammer. These cultists operate in the shadows of the Dark Iron encampment, conducting dark rituals and harboring powerful elite zealots beneath the rock. Their proximity to both the Dark Iron infrastructure and Blackrock Mountain reflects the pervasive, insidious reach of elemental and apocalyptic cults within the fiery heart of the Searing Gorge.

subzone:flame-crest.text: Flame Crest. Flame Crest watches the volcanic wastes from a rocky ledge in the Burning Steppes. The neutral camp shelters scouts, beast collectors, and strategists, while wind riders carry travelers across the Redridge range and beyond. Flame Crest clings to a stone ledge above the ash and lava plains. You cross a narrow wooden bridge to reach the camp. Its height helps keep prowling beasts and roaming orc warbands at bay. Wind riders carry travelers across the Redridge range to Kargath, Stonard, Thorium Point, and Rog'mar in the Riverglades. Scouts at Flame Crest watch the Blackrock clan entrenched in Blackrock Spire. They gather intelligence and plan how to break the renegade Dark Horde. The camp also trades with eccentric loners, including Kibler, a pet master who lives in a nearby cave.

subzone:foothold-citadel.text: Foothold Citadel. At Foothold Citadel, Theramore's guards prepare to defend the island. The fortress holds the Alliance command and barracks on Theramore Isle, overlooking the settlement. Foothold Citadel holds the Alliance defense within Theramore Isle's stone walls. Captain Garran Vimes and Commander Samaul lead the Theramore Guard from its halls. Field medics, logistics officers and quartermasters work beside them. Guards patrol and drill, preparing Lady Jaina Proudmoore's forces for threats from the surrounding swamplands. Foothold Citadel recalls the early days of Theramore. Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore seized the city to wage his personal crusade against the Horde, and the fortress became the place of his final stand. Thrall's allied force broke through the citadel under Rexxar, a half-ogre warrior, and struck down the Admiral. The fortress has been repaired, though the bloody conflict is remembered.

subzone:forgotten-coast.text: Forgotten Coast. The Forgotten Coast forms the wild western shore of Feralas, where the ancient rainforest meets the Veiled Sea. Lumbering sea giants and water elementals roam this battered strand. Stretching along the western edge of Feralas, the Forgotten Coast is a windswept shoreline confronting the expanse of the Veiled Sea. Unlike the dense canopy inland, this frontier is exposed to the elements and dominated by towering sea giants and roving water elementals pacing the surf. Travelers emerging from the forest canopy must contend with these primeval coastal guardians while navigating access to the sea, where ferry connections link to the night elven bastion of Sardor Isle.

subzone:forgotten-pool.text: Forgotten Pool. Past the Moonshrine Ruins, Forgotten Pool lies beneath the flooded halls of Blackfathom Deeps. Its dark waters hide monstrous deep-sea predators. You reach Forgotten Pool by diving through the sunken waterways beyond the Moonshrine Ruins. Dark water fills this isolated cavern, cut off from dry ground. Twilight's Hammer cultists chant nearby, and naga patrol the flooded halls, but the pool lies apart from them. Old Serra'kis, an ancient aquatic terror, lairs in its depths, hidden by the water.

subzone:forlorn-cloister.text: Forlorn Cloister. The Forlorn Cloister is the haunted graveyard wing of the Scarlet Monastery. Here, members of the Scarlet Crusade desperately torch the bodies of fallen brothers to prevent them from rising into undeath, while restless spirits and shambling corpses roam among the tombs. Once a peaceful sanctuary where the priests and paladins of Lordaeron laid their honoured dead to rest, the Forlorn Cloister has become a grim charnel ground. Despite the Scarlet Crusade's fanatical vigilance, the taint of the plague has seeped deep into the earth. crusaders patrol the fog-shrouded cemetery with torches, frantically burning remains to stave off the rot. Even so, spectres glide between crypts and the dead pull free from their graves, ruled over by dark magic deep within the grounds. Deep within the cloister lurks Bloodmage Thalnos, a skeletal sorcerer whose undeath embodies the tragedy of the Monastery. Hungering for vengeance, Thalnos wields dark magic, binding the souls of the deceased and slaughtering any who dare intrude upon his blighted graveyard.

subzone:forlorn-ridge.text: Forlorn Ridge. Forlorn Ridge is a towering mountain ridge looming over southwestern Azshara. Its strategic elevation and commanding views over the coast have drawn the attention of both the Alliance and the Horde, who have each carved out fortifications along its slopes. Rising sharply above the autumnal forests of western Azshara, Forlorn Ridge dominates the surrounding terrain. Resembling an ancient, long-dormant volcano, its high vantage point offers a sweeping view over the coastal approaches and the ruined elven estates below. Because control over these heights dictates military dominance in the sector, both Alliance and Horde forces have established encampments and outposts along its mountain flanks, watching each other warily across the rugged bluffs.

subzone:frayfeather-highlands.text: Frayfeather Highlands. The Frayfeather Highlands form an elevated wilderness in the dense forests of Feralas. This remote plateau is the ancestral roost and nesting ground of the wild Frayfeather hippogryphs. Intrepid scavengers and naturalists often brave its territorial flocks in search of intact hippogryph eggs. Rising above the surrounding forest floor of Feralas, the Frayfeather Highlands are dominated by steep slopes and crags where wild hippogryphs raise their broods. The local flocks are notoriously aggressive toward intruders, fiercely defending the scattered nests tucked among the rock shelves. Because these beasts are so well adapted to the rugged cliffs, their nesting grounds have drawn significant interest from outsiders—most notably goblin entrepreneurs in distant Gadgetzan who seek unhatched eggs for study and profit.

subzone:frostfire-hot-springs.text: Frostfire Hot Springs. Frostfire Hot Springs are a curious series of steaming pools nestled amidst the western snowdrifts of Winterspring. Despite the bitter sub-zero temperatures all around them, these waters bubble constantly, attracting curious scholars, hardy fishers, and hostile furbolgs alike. Situated near the tunnel leading to Timbermaw Hold, Frostfire Hot Springs represent one of the strangest natural anomalies in northern Kalimdor. The pools remain hot amid the surrounding snow, although the source of their heat is uncertain. The local Winterfall furbolgs maintain a presence near the water, though their aggressive territorial nature makes approaching the warm banks hazardous for unwary travelers. For those able to navigate the hostile wildlife and winter chill, the unfrozen waters provide a rare haven for fish. The uncanny existence of such intense heat in an otherwise frozen wasteland has drawn the attention of curious observers. Nearby, an inquisitive dwarf named Donova Snowden keeps a lonely vigil over the springs, studying their origin and composition. Snowden suspects that these geothermal anomalies might not be entirely natural, hypothesizing that dark magical corruption seeping northward from the demonic stronghold of Darkwhisper Gorge could be responsible for roiling the subterranean waters.

subzone:frostsaber-rock.text: Frostsaber Rock. Frostsaber Rock is a towering stone promontory rising above the snowy northern reaches of Winterspring. It serves as the primary sanctuary and training grounds for the noble frostsaber cats of the region. Rising high above the frozen wastes of northern Winterspring, Frostsaber Rock commands a sweeping view of the snowbound wild. The crag is named for the fierce, majestic frostsaber predators that prowl the slopes and valleys below. At its highest apex resides Rivern Frostwind, a solitary night elf dedicated to raising and tending these beasts. For champions loyal to the Alliance willing to brave the harsh conditions and prove their devotion, Rivern offers the rare privilege of learning to raise, tame, and ride one of these legendary snowy mounts.

subzone:frostwhisper-gorge.text: Frostwhisper Gorge. Frostwhisper Gorge is a frigid canyon carved into the southern highlands of Winterspring, lying directly north of the sinister Darkwhisper Gorge. Ancient night elven ruins litter its icy floor and surrounding cliffs, while towering Frostmaul giants dominate the chasm. High above the eastern rim, a solitary dwarf camp looks out over the precipice toward the ocean below. Carved into the southern mountains of Winterspring, Frostwhisper Gorge serves as a threshold just before the demon-infested depths of Darkwhisper Gorge. Its snowy floor and cliffside ridges are strewn with the forgotten stonework of ancient night elven settlements. In the present day, the gorge is claimed by immense Frostmaul giants and their preservers. Travel down into the ravine is perilous, as the giants fiercely defend the frozen crags against any wandering intruders. Hidden along a narrow, quiet track at the top of the gorge's eastern cliffs lies a curious outpost. Flying travelers on wyverns or gryphons passing between Azshara, Orgrimmar, and Winterspring often glimpse it from above: a solitary dwarven encampment perched at the very edge of the world. Planted with the banner of Ironforge, the camp features crates of provisions, barrels of ale, a comfortable chair, and a rifle leaning against the rest, providing an unmatched view across the drop to the Great Sea below.

subzone:fungal-rock.text: Fungal Rock. Fungal Rock is a damp, cavernous hollow carved into the northeastern cliff walls of Un'Goro Crater. Dominated by aggressive primates and thick growths of Ghost Mushrooms, it is one of the crater's most dangerous ape dens. Tucked behind a small waterfall and pool along Un'Goro Crater's northeastern edge, Fungal Rock serves as the primary den for the region's massive gorillas. Inside the damp, subterranean corridors, towering Un'Goro Stompers and Thunderers patrol among clusters of rare Ghost Mushrooms. The deepest recesses house territorial behemoths, including the mighty silverback U'cha and the elusive albino gorilla Uhk'loc. Beyond its primal inhabitants, curious travelers may stumble upon artificial oddities near the cave mouth, such as A-Me 01, a damaged mechanical ape abandoned by gnome researchers.

subzone:fungal-vale.text: Fungal Vale. The Fungal Vale is a deeply blighted depression located in the south-central Eastern Plaguelands, just north of the Crown Guard Tower and Marris Stead. Choked in a murky haze and blanketed with dark purple earth, the valley showcases the raw, mutating power of the Plague of Undeath. It swarms with roaming Scourge horrors and mortal acolytes serving the Cult of the Damned. Situated north of Marris Stead, the Fungal Vale represents one of the most thoroughly corrupted pockets in Lordaeron. The ground here has turned a sickly purple, swollen with alien fungal growths and drowning under a perpetual, murky haze produced by necrotic spores. Rather than simply killing the ecosystem, the Plague of Undeath has warped the soil to cultivate unholy flora, feeding monstrous carrion beasts and shambling undead. Cult of the Damned members frequent the area, tending to the blighted blooms and conducting foul rites amidst the unnatural decay.

subzone:gadgetzan.text: Gadgetzan. Gadgetzan is the walled desert hub of the Steamwheedle Cartel, standing as an island of commerce in northern Tanaris. Open to both Horde and Alliance travelers, the town operates under strictly enforced goblin neutrality, welcoming anyone with coin to spend or odd jobs to undertake. Surrounded by scorching sands, Gadgetzan serves as the regional heart for the Steamwheedle Cartel's ventures in southern Kalimdor. Built with characteristic goblin ingenuity and haphazard architecture, the town boasts an independent auction house, bank, inn, and specialized crafting facilities for engineers, blacksmiths, and alchemists. It also houses flight masters catering to both major factions, ensuring steady traffic of adventurers heading toward Tanaris, Feralas, and the untamed basin of Un'Goro. Above all, commerce rules supreme: as long as visitors keep their weapons sheathed and their purses open, they are safe within its gates. Peace in Gadgetzan is maintained not by good will, but by heavily armed goblin bruisers who swiftly pummel anyone who threatens trade or instigates faction brawls. Beyond the gates, however, life is precarious. The Gadgetzan Water Company constantly battles the Wastewander bandits, a ruthless gang occupying the vital Waterspring Field. Water is liquid gold in Tanaris, and the cartel frequently hires outside mercenaries to eliminate bandit leadership and reclaim vital water pouches to keep the town's reservoirs functional.

subzone:gahrron-s-withering.text: Gahrron's Withering. Gahrron's Withering is a corrupted farmstead nestled along the eastern border of the Western Plaguelands near the path to the Eastern Plaguelands. Once a thriving piece of Lordaeron farmland, it is now occupied by the Scourge and anchored by a massive cauldron pumping virulent plague vapors into the air. Before the Third War ruined the kingdom of Lordaeron, this estate was a working farm. Its fertile fields yielded grain for the realm until the Cult of the Damned and the Scourge swept across the land. Now called Gahrron's Withering, the homestead stands broken and derelict. Haunting visions, wailing wraiths, and restless spirits wander the ruined outbuildings, overseen by Scourge overseers sworn to the Lich King.

subzone:gallery-of-treasures.text: Gallery of Treasures. The Gallery of Treasures is an ornate, heavily guarded corridor inside the Scarlet Monastery's halls, connecting the Huntsman's Cloister to the Athenaeum. Lined with recovered paintings, relics, and illuminated texts, it showcases the wealth and Lordaeron heritage preserved by the Scarlet Crusade amidst their zealous war against the undead. Situated deep within the Library wing of the Scarlet Monastery, the Gallery of Treasures serves as a grand hall connecting the kennels of the Huntsman's Cloister to the sacred archives of the Athenaeum. Unlike the hound pens of the cloister, this corridor is lined with fine paintings, historical artifacts, and small chambers filled with books salvaged from across the fallen kingdom of Lordaeron. To the Scarlet Crusade, these relics represent the untainted legacy of humanity they have sworn to protect, fiercely guarded against all outsiders who dare intrude upon their sanctuary.

subzone:gaping-chasm.text: Gaping Chasm. The Gaping Chasm is a sprawling silithid hive carved deep into the sands of southeastern Tanaris. Infested by aggressive insectoid horrors of the Hazzali brood, it serves as a grim warning of the growing silithid menace spreading beyond the western deserts. Breaking the rolling expanses of Tanaris, the Gaping Chasm plunges down into a teeming subterranean warren of tunnels, resinous mounds, and twitching carapaces. This hive belongs to the Hazzali, an aggressive brood of silithid that have burrowed beneath the desert wastes. Between subterranean stingers, swarmers, and hulking sandreavers, any travelers or treasure-hunters foolish enough to descend into the chasm quickly find themselves hunted as prey or preserved in sticky cocoons. The expanding hive caught the attention of Gadgetzan's enterprising minds, prompting Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser to dispatch his junior surveyor, Scrimshank, into the pit to map and measure the geological shifts caused by the insect tunnels. Unsurprisingly, the expedition ended in disaster. Scrimshank met a grim end amidst the chittering broods, leaving behind scattered gear and measuring instruments that caution anyone against underestimating the silithid threat.

subzone:garrison-armory.text: Garrison Armory. The Garrison Armory is an Alliance mining operation carved into the hills southwest of Nethergarde Keep in the Blasted Lands. Miners and engineers work the underground veins to harvest valuable minerals, sustaining the lonely fortress and shipping raw wealth back to Stormwind. It forms a crucial industrial lifeline in an otherwise blasted, barren wilderness. Maintaining a permanent military garrison in the arid wastes of the Blasted Lands requires constant supply, and Nethergarde Keep cannot rely purely on long supply trains from Stormwind. The Garrison Armory serves as the keep's primary industrial excavation. Nethergarde miners, overseen by foremen and assisted by engineers, work these subterranean shafts to pull valuable minerals from the earth. The ore extracted here is utilized directly by Nethergarde's smiths and fortifications or hauled back to the capital in exchange for the foodstuffs, tools, and provisions the fortress needs to maintain its vigil over the Dark Portal. Because the armory sits away from the main walls of Nethergarde Keep, the excavation remains exposed to the harsh perils of the red desert. Dreadmaul ogres and wild beasts prowl the surrounding crags. The workforce within the tunnels operates under armed guard, knowing that any disruption to the armory directly threatens Nethergarde's ability to maintain its watch over the blasted frontier.

subzone:gelkis-village.text: Gelkis Village. Gelkis Village is the primary stronghold of the earth-aligned Gelkis centaur clan in southwestern Desolace. Built around a rugged ravine connected by wooden spans and cliffside paths, the settlement guards the southern route toward Feralas. Its vantage directly overlooks the main north-south road, making it a perilous crossing for any traveler who has not earned the clan's favor. Gelkis Village sits in a deep, craggy gorge framed by precarious bluffs and rope bridges. Unlike the nomadic raiders of the Barrens, the Gelkis have fortified their ancestral grounds into a permanent settlement, complete with outposts spreading toward the border of Feralas. The heart of the clan's leadership lies within Bolgan's Hole, a cavern carved into the southern cliff face where Khan Shaka oversees his warriors. Travelers trekking south through Desolace must either cut a bloody path through the gorge or tread carefully, as the Gelkis view uninvited wanderers as fair game in their eternal war against their rival centaur brethren.

subzone:ghost-walker-post.text: Ghost Walker Post. Ghost Walker Post is a modest tauren settlement situated in the heart of Desolace right beside the ancient Kodo Graveyard. Far more exposed to regional dangers than Shadowprey Village on the western coast, it serves as a frontline Horde staging ground against centaur clans and the Burning Blade. Perched on the dusty flats of central Desolace, Ghost Walker Post provides the Horde with an austere foothold in a hostile territory. Unlike the sheltered coastal fishing haven of Shadowprey Village, this post directly faces roaming centaur marauders and demon-worshiping cultists of the Burning Blade. Facilities are spartan, offering only the bare essentials for travelers, with no inn or flight master in sight. Despite the harsh conditions, a garrison of tauren and an orcish detachment sent by Warchief Thrall keep vigilant watch over the badlands. Led by the tauren shaman Gurda Wildmane, the spiritual heart of the outpost is closely entwined with the neighboring Kodo Graveyard. Shamans stationed here tend to the dying beasts that wander in to perish, helping ease them into the next life and communing with their lingering spirits. Between spiritual communion and constant military readiness, the defenders of the post honor the ancient bond between the tauren and the mighty kodo amid the ashes of Desolace.

subzone:gnomeregan.text:
Gnomeregan. Troggs and leper gnomes roam Gnomeregan’s poisoned halls among the broken defenses. The city was once the gnomes’ underground capital, until a desperate defense ended in catastrophe. Gnomeregan’s halls once rang with the work of gnomish engineers. Ironforge dwarves helped build the city centuries ago, carving it into the snowy crags of western Dun Morogh. Steam-driven gears, copper pipes, and vast assembly halls made it the heart of gnomish industry and invention. During the Second War, its designs, flying machines, and complex weapons supplied the Alliance. Even Orgrim Doomhammer’s Horde could not break the city during its siege. During the Third War, troggs surged up from deep underground and broke into Gnomeregan’s lowest chambers. High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque chose to face the invasion alone, unwilling to draw Alliance armies away from the slaughter in Lordaeron.

On the advice of chief engineer Mekgineer Thermaplugg, he ordered radioactive gas released through the lower chambers to wipe out the troggs. Instead, the gas empowered many troggs and killed nearly eighty percent of the gnomish people. Survivors exposed to it became twisted leper gnomes, and Thermaplugg took control of the poisoned ruins.

subzone:go-shek-farm.text: Go'Shek Farm. Go'Shek Farm is an agricultural outpost in the eastern Arathi Highlands, occupied by the Horde and guarded by orcs from Hammerfall. Behind its mundane rural facade, Forsaken apothecaries conduct secretive alchemical experiments far from prying eyes. Go'Shek Farm is held by the Horde. Positioned south of Hammerfall and just north of the hostile Witherbark troll territory, the farmstead nominally serves as a vital supply and staging hub for the orcish settlement. Hammerfall Grunts patrol the fields and stables, securing food and livestock to sustain the Horde's embattled foothold in the Arathi Highlands.

subzone:golakka-hot-springs.text: Golakka Hot Springs. Golakka Hot Springs is a geothermal basin in western Un'Goro Crater, nestled just north of Terror Run. Its bubbling pools and erupting geysers are fueled by the intense volcanic activity of nearby Fire Plume Ridge. The mineral-rich waters attract eccentric researchers, alchemists in search of exotic reagents, and wandering water elementals known as Steaming Furies. Situated in the western reaches of Un'Goro Crater, the Golakka Hot Springs are a direct product of the subterranean heat radiating from Fire Plume Ridge. Scalding water bubbles continuously to the surface, shaping tiered mineral terraces and violently erupting geysers. The environment is heavily prowled by Steaming Furies, elemental manifestations born from the convergence of subterranean groundwater and volcanic heat. Despite the danger, the springs frequently draw explorers, herbalists, and researchers fascinated by the crater's unique geology. The unique properties of Golakka's waters have drawn interest beyond simple sightseeing. Alchemists value the geothermally enriched spring water as a potent catalytic reagent, even utilizing it in delicate concotions such as love potions. The geothermal vent also hosts quirky visitors, such as Spark Nilminer perched atop the central geyser vent, and draws the researcher Krakle, who seeks to decipher how the hot springs directly tap into the volcanic heart of the crater.

subzone:gordok-commons.text: Gordok Commons. The Gordok Commons comprise the fortified northern quarter of the ancient Highborne ruins of Dire Maul. Under the rule of King Gordok, this sprawling stone complex serves as the seat of power for the elite warrior caste of the Gordunni ogres. Occupying what was once an aristocratic wing of Eldre'Thalas, the Gordok Commons have been thoroughly desecrated and refitted for ogre tastes. Grand night elven pillars and arched passageways now house armories, crude barricades, and training grounds for the Gordok—the fiercest, most disciplined fighters among the Gordunni clan. At the deepest end of the wing lies Gordok's Seat, where King Gordok presides over his brutes through sheer force and intimidation. Gordok culture operates entirely on brutal precedent: might makes right. According to clan tradition, whoever slays the sitting monarch claims the title of King Gordok, earning immediate obedience from any surviving captains and guards. Astute intruders exploit this custom by sneaking or scheming past the king's lieutenants rather than slaying them outright. If a challenger executes only the king, the surviving guards will recognize the victor's authority and present lavish tributes rather than fight to avenge their former ruler.

subzone:gordunni-outpost.text: Gordunni Outpost. Tucked into the rugged cliffs north of Lariss Pavilion, the Gordunni Outpost serves as a fortified camp for the brutish Gordunni ogres of Feralas. The clan's corrupting influence has choked the once-vibrant wilderness here, leaving the surrounding earth dry, withered, and brown. Carved into the northern mountains above the Lariss Pavilion, the Gordunni Outpost stands out as a stark scar against the lush canopy of Feralas. Wherever the Gordunni ogres settle, their reckless magical channeling and destructive habits sap the vitality of the wild, leaving the local flora dead and the hillsides barren. The outpost consists of dirt trails, a shallow entrance cave, and a larger ogre mound burrowed deep into the rear cliffs. Patrolled by heavily armed hillguards, cunning channelers, and ogre tamers, the camp also holds dangerous trophies—including a captured sasquatch named Bigfist kept in crude confinement near the deeper den.

subzone:green-belt.text: Green Belt. In eastern Wetlands, Green Belt lies below the ridges of Grim Batol. Bog beasts, crocolisks, and toxic oozes roam its marshes, while Rethiel the Greenwarden keeps watch alone. Green Belt fills the eastern interior of Wetlands, where mossy waters make travel hazardous. Massive crocolisks, shifting oozes, and shambling bog beasts roam the fen. Deep within it, a solitary watch post is manned by Rethiel the Greenwarden, a night elf who studies the fen's ecology and keeps its hostile creatures in check. Wreckage from a Dragonmaw clan caravan lies scattered in the muck, left behind after the catastrophic battle at nearby Grim Batol. Crimson whelplings linger around the broken carts and crushed cages, reminders of the clan's past enslavement of Alexstrasza and her red dragon brood.

subzone:grimesilt-dig-site.text: Grimesilt Dig Site. Grimesilt Dig Site is an archaeological excavation in the Searing Gorge originally broken ground by Ironforge dwarves. Overrun by hostile Dark Iron dwarves, the pit is now firmly under enemy control while surviving members of the original expedition struggle to endure in hiding. Situated within the soot-choked badlands of the Searing Gorge, the Grimesilt Dig Site began as an expedition sanctioned by Ironforge scholars seeking relics beneath the crags. That venture met a violent end when the native Dark Iron dwarves drove out the excavators and claimed the equipment for themselves. Today, the trench swarms with Dark Iron sentries, leaving the wounded and scattered survivors of the original Ironforge crew trapped in and around the pit.

subzone:grimtotem-compound.text: Grimtotem Compound. The Grimtotem Compound is a fortified tribal settlement nestled in the central wilds of Feralas, just east of the elven ruins of Dire Maul. Occupied by the aggressive and insular Grimtotem clan, the encampment serves as a base for their mysterious and destructive operations in the region. Spanning two encampments east of Dire Maul, the Grimtotem Compound establishes a firm foothold for the Grimtotem clan in Feralas. Unlike the tauren aligned with Cairne Bloodhoof in Thunder Bluff, the Grimtotem here operate independently and with hostility toward outsiders. In the southern half of the settlement, they keep captive sprite darters locked inside a large wooden cage for reasons of their own, while rogue gnolls stalk the fringes of their northern perimeter.

subzone:grom-gol-base-camp.text: Grom'gol Base Camp. Grom'gol Base Camp is the Horde's primary fortified outpost in Stranglethorn Vale, situated along the western coast of northern Stranglethorn. Commanded by Commander Aggro'gosh, the settlement secures a critical foothold and supply chain in the southern Eastern Kingdoms. With direct zeppelin towers linking to Orgrimmar and the Undercity, it stands as an armed staging ground against local jungle troll tribes and hostile Alliance forces. Carved into the dense jungle of northwestern Stranglethorn Vale, Grom'gol Base Camp is a fortified military bastion commanded by Commander Aggro'gosh. Ringed by defensive palisades and heavily armed grunts, the base camp endures non-stop harassment from Bloodscalp headhunters, lurking naga, and prowling beasts. Despite these threats, its vital strategic location secures safe supply routes north toward Stonard in the Swamp of Sorrows while keeping a watchful eye on Alliance traffic descending from Duskwood or traveling up from Booty Bay. Grom'gol's prominent wooden zeppelin towers serve as one of the most vital logistical hubs in the Eastern Kingdoms. Goblin skycraft tethered here maintain regular routes directly to the capital cities of Orgrimmar and the Undercity. This uninterrupted airbridge allows Horde forces to rapidly deploy reinforcements and resources straight into the heart of Stranglethorn without braving Alliance-dominated highways or the deep sea.

subzone:growless-cave.text: Growless Cave. In frigid Growless Cave, mountain yetis roam the cavern in the Alterac Mountains. The cave also holds the Flame of Uzel, a ceremonial pyre tied to Helcular's dark necromancy. Territorial mountain yetis roam Growless Cave in the crags above Alterac's foothills. Travelers on the treacherous slopes avoid its entrance, especially when Skhowl, a notorious yeti, prowls outside. The cave holds more than danger from the beasts. Within it stands the Flame of Uzel, an arcane brazier left by the human mage Helcular. Before his death, Helcular meant to use the pyre in a dark ritual to become a lich. Its foul warmth once drew Frostmaw, a massive predator, from the frozen wastes.

subzone:gurubashi-arena.text: Gurubashi Arena. Gurubashi Arena is an ancient stone colosseum standing in southern Stranglethorn Vale, originally built by the mighty Gurubashi Empire. In the present day, it serves as a chaotic free-for-all proving ground where pirates and wandering brawlers shed blood over locked chests of treasure. Long before human or orc set foot in Stranglethorn Vale, the Gurubashi Arena—known also as the Great Arena—was built as a monument to martial strength by the sprawling Gurubashi troll empire. In ancient days, champions fought to the death upon its sands until the earth was slick with troll blood. Though the empire has long since fractured into warring tribes, the arena's floor never stays clean for long. Today, lawless buccaneers and ruffians oversee a different sort of bloody spectacle. A pirate named Short John Mithril oversees the grounds, where every few hours a chest of plundered booty is hauled into the center of the ring. Anyone who steps onto the floor is fair game—faction allegiances vanish, and combatants must butcher their way to the prize against all comers.

subzone:haldarr-encampment.text: Haldarr Encampment. The Haldarr Encampment is a corrupted satyr outpost nestled in western Azshara, situated northeast of the Shadowsong Shrine and southwest of Valormok. Densely inhabited by the vicious Haldarr satyrs, it stands as a dangerous blight among the ancient elven ruins. It is also where an injured Night Elf Sentinel, Keldara Sunblade, can be found. Perched among the broken stones of western Azshara, the Haldarr Encampment serves as a gathering ground for the Haldarr clan of satyrs. These twisted creatures, ancient remnants of the Highborne cursed by demonic corruption during the Sundering, actively hunt and harass any who traverse the autumn forests. The dense settlement poses an ongoing threat to both the Horde forces stationed at nearby Valormok and the dwindling Night Elf sentinels trying to monitor the region.

subzone:hall-of-arms-tyr-s-hand.text: Hall of Arms (Tyr's Hand). The Hall of Arms is a heavily guarded wing within Tyr's Hand Abbey in southeastern Eastern Plaguelands. It serves as a staging ground and barracks for the martial vanguard of the Scarlet Crusade garrisoned at the stronghold. Positioned across the abbey from the library, it houses some of the crusade's most zealous and well-armored fighters. Situated to the south of the abbey's main hall, the Hall of Arms functions as an armory and quarters for the militant forces of Tyr's Hand. While the opposing wing holds archives and holy texts, this wing is dedicated purely to the discipline of war. Clad in heavy armor and sworn to eradicate the undead and anyone deemed impure, the Scarlet defenders stationed here maintain a tireless watch over their eastern bastion, keeping weapons sharpened and shields polished against the surrounding horrors of the Plaguelands.

subzone:hall-of-champions.text: Hall of Champions. The Hall of Champions is the inner sanctum of the Scarlet Monastery's armory wing. It serves as the seat of Herod, the Scarlet Champion, and a proving ground for the Scarlet Crusade's elite. Situated past the Footman's Armory, the Hall of Champions lies at the heart of the monastery's armory wing. Here Herod, the Scarlet Champion, holds sway over the Crusade's fiercest fighters, and Scarlet trainees harden their resolve to purge Lordaeron of all undead and outsiders.

subzone:hall-of-masks.text: Hall of Masks. The Hall of Masks is an ominous chamber inside the sunken Temple of Atal'Hakkar in the Swamp of Sorrows. Lined with giant skull masks and marred by a bone-strewn trench, it marks one of the early thresholds deeper into the Atal'ai stronghold. Located just past the staircase descending from the Broken Hall, the Hall of Masks serves as a central junction within the Sunken Temple. The chamber earns its name from the imposing, stylized skull masks mounted along its stone walls. Below them runs a deep trench choked with discarded bones, suggesting a macabre purpose whose exact nature is unknown. Beyond this eerie hall lie passages branching out to the Butchery, the Chamber of Blood, and the Den of the Caller.

subzone:hammerfall.text: Hammerfall. Hammerfall is the Horde's primary fortified outpost in the Arathi Highlands, built upon the ruins of a notorious Alliance internment camp. It honors the legendary former Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer, who fell nearby while fighting to liberate his captive people. Today, orcs and Forsaken garrison the settlement against hostile Boulderfist ogres, Witherbark trolls, and the League of Arathor. Following the Second War, the human Alliance built vast internment camps across Lordaeron to contain the defeated orcs. The compound that once stood here was among the largest. Years later, Thrall and Orgrim Doomhammer assaulted the camp to liberate the lethargic captives. During the chaos of their retreat, a charging Alliance knight drove a lance through Doomhammer's backplate, mortally wounding the legendary Warchief. Following the Third War, the new Horde reclaimed the ruined ground and established an outpost here, naming it Hammerfall in memory of their fallen leader. Today, Hammerfall serves as the Horde's lifeline in Arathi. Positioned against hostile surroundings, the garrison contends with aggressive Boulderfist ogres from Boulder'gor and Boulderfist Hall, as well as the native Witherbark trolls. Furthermore, Forsaken Defilers have made the outpost their staging ground to claim the contested resources of the Arathi Basin against the Alliance's League of Arathor.

subzone:harborage.text: Harborage. The Harborage is a quiet settlement of exiled Draenor natives situated in the northern reaches of the Swamp of Sorrows. While many of their afflicted kin wandering the surrounding bogs have succumbed to madness and primal hostility, the inhabitants here have managed to hold onto their sanity and wits. They live cautiously along the waterline, seeking peace amidst a harsh and unforgiving wilderness. Tucked away against the northern mountains of the Swamp of Sorrows, the Harborage stands in stark contrast to the feral tribes wandering the nearby waters. Constructed of rugged leather shelters and adorned with mysterious hanging crystals, this small encampment provides sanctuary to exiled Draenor survivors who have refused to surrender their minds. Under the guidance of elders like Magtoor, they maintain a fragile, civilized enclave while remaining watchful of the hostile wilderness, native predators, and the feral tribes of their fallen brothers lurking just beyond their perimeter.

subzone:hearthglen.text: Hearthglen. Tucked away in the northern hills of the Western Plaguelands, Hearthglen is a fortified settlement that remarkably escaped complete physical destruction during the fall of Lordaeron. Today, its sturdy stone walls, towers, and surrounding farmlands serve as the primary northern stronghold and training ground for the fanatical Scarlet Crusade. While neighboring Andorhal lies shattered in skeletal ruin, Hearthglen still resembles a living town of Lordaeron, complete with a lumber mill, scout towers, stables, and a functioning mine. Historically governed from Mardenholde Keep by Lord Tirion Fordring, Hearthglen was renowned for its prosperity and staunch defense during the Second War. When the Plague of Undeath swept Lordaeron during the Third War, Prince Arthas Menethil intercepted tainted grain here, purging the infected townsfolk and repelling a massive Scourge siege alongside Uther the Lightbringer. Through that desperate intervention, Hearthglen's formidable walls survived intact. After the Silver Hand fell into disarray following the kingdom's collapse, Tirion's son, Taelan Fordring, renounced the order and joined the Scarlet Crusade, and the grief and zealotry that birthed the Crusade soon consumed the fortress. Now, Hearthglen is a fortress of religious extremism. Scarlet crusaders patrol its approaches and man its ramparts, violently executing any outsider, living or undead, who trespasses on their land. Highlord Taelan Fordring rules from Mardenholde Keep, a devout servant to the Crusade's uncompromising war against the Plaguelands.

subzone:hetaera-s-clutch.text: Hetaera's Clutch. Hetaera's Clutch is a sunken night elven temple dedicated to Elune, nestled deep beneath the churning waters of Azshara's Bay of Storms. Once a sacred site of devotion, the submerged ruins are now overrun by deadly hydras hatched by their broodmother, Hetaera. Adventurers braving the depths will find ancient stonework claimed by vicious aquatic predators. Before the Great Sundering tore ancient Kalimdor apart, this structure served as a grand temple dedicated to the moon goddess Elune. Cast into the depths of the Bay of Storms, its stone pillars and sacred halls have spent ten thousand years beneath the sea. Today, all signs of holy veneration have been swallowed by the tides, leaving behind a solemn monument to the lost Kaldorei empire. The submerged sanctuary has taken on a far deadlier identity as the nesting ground of Hetaera, a massive multi-headed hydra who stalks the nearby coastal waters and rocky isles. Her numerous offspring, the Spawn of Hetaera, prowl through the ruined arches and corridors of the drowned temple, attacking any surface-dweller bold enough to dive into the bay.

subzone:hidden-grove.text: Hidden Grove. Tucked away behind towering cliffs in northeastern Winterspring, the Hidden Grove is a secluded crater basin. Once an untroubled haven for Arctic hares, the basin has fallen under the domain of fiercely territorial wild moonkin. Walled off from the bitter howling winds of Winterspring, the Hidden Grove forms a sunken, snow-dusted forest crater that is nearly impossible to access from the outside cliffs. Travelers who discover its concealed rim must brave a sheer, dangerous drop or navigate a narrow cavern passage tucked into the southeastern ridge. Though the valley was long the undisturbed home of harmless white hares, aggressive wild moonkin have seized the glade, turning an isolated natural paradise into an ambush for unwary wanderers.

subzone:high-wilderness.text: High Wilderness. The High Wilderness is an expansive, untamed stretch of primordial forest covering much of western Feralas. Bordered by the Verdantis River to the east and the Forgotten Coast to the west, it shelters a wide array of wildlife, wandering treants, and dangerous beasts beneath its towering emerald canopy. Stretching across the western half of Feralas, the High Wilderness represents the quintessential untamed wilderness of southern Kalimdor. Thick foliage and colossal trees block out much of the sky, creating a lush expanse teeming with wolves, bears, hippogryphs, and yetis. Ancient treants wander among the roots, while aggressive ogre clans establish footholds in the shaded clearings. Navigating this vast green expanse requires vigilance, as the dense brush hides both natural predators and lingering primeval hazards.

subzone:hive-ashi.text: Hive'Ashi. Hive'Ashi is a sprawling silithid colony dominating the northern sands of Silithus. As one of three major insectoid hives in the region, its creeping tunnels and towering mounds churn with countless hostile workers, defenders, and stingers. Situated in northern Silithus, Hive'Ashi serves as a prime hive-complex for the re-emerging silithid swarms. Its chitinous spires carve out a distinct territory among the dunes, sending foraging workers and venomous defenders south and east toward the Swarming Pillar. Anyone seeking to understand the strange, coordinated intelligence stirring within the desert wastes inevitably finds their path leading directly into the dangerous, buzzing tunnels beneath these mounds. Cenarion scouts stationed across Silithus monitor Hive'Ashi closely, commissioning brave combatants to thin its ranks and retrieve reconnaissance reports from deep within the colony. The glyphs and coordinated behavior documented within Ashi suggest that these mindless-looking insects share an eerie, singular will. As their numbers swell, the hive threatens to spill beyond northern Silithus entirely, making the eradication of its brood a top priority for those watching the southern borders.

subzone:hive-regal.text: Hive'Regal. Hive'Regal is a massive silithid hive burrowed into the southern reaches of Silithus. As one of the three primary insectoid colonies dominating the arid wastes, it teems with aggressive silithid castes that threaten to overrun the surrounding desert. Sprawling across southern Silithus, Hive'Regal represents one of the greatest concentrations of silithid activity in Kalimdor. Its towering resin spires and cavernous underground tunnels churn with dangerous insectoid broods, from venomous spitfires and burrowers to predatory slavemakers. The hive acts as a coordinated warren, aggressively defending its perimeter and harvesting organic material from any unfortunate travelers who wander too close to its borders. Beneath the red sands, Hive'Regal's labyrinthine passages delve deep into the earth. Strange glyphs etched near its entrance and deep inside the tunnels suggest an organized intelligence directing the swarm rather than mere feral instinct. Scholars and scouts studying the silithid threat believe that Hive'Regal, along with its sister hives, functions as part of a larger emergent power stirring beneath the wastes of Silithus.

subzone:hive-zora.text: Hive'Zora. Hive'Zora is one of the three major silithid colony mounds dominating the arid expanse of Silithus. Located along the western edge of the desert, this teeming subterranean hive crawls with aggressive insectoid castes serving the greater swarm. Rising out of the barren sand dunes of western Silithus, Hive'Zora serves as a bustling hub of insectoid activity. Great, porous stone spires and mounds mark the entrances into deep subterranean tunnels dug out by silithid burrowers. Waywatchers and reavers patrol the perimeter relentlessly, while tunneling castes and hive sisters brood within the depths below. For the Cenarion Circle and other scouts keeping watch over the desert, the hive represents a terrifying sign of the insectoid menace steadily reclaiming the ancient frontier.

subzone:horizon-scout.text: Horizon Scout. The Horizon Scout is a sunken vessel resting on the ocean floor in the Ruined Reaches off the southern coast of Azshara. While its captain remains stranded ashore, several crew members remain trapped in the submerged hull, kept alive beneath the waves by an arcane water-breathing enchantment. Resting beneath the waves among the treacherous shoals of the Ruined Reaches, the Horizon Scout met a violent end off Azshara's jagged coast. While Captain Vanessa Beltis managed to reach land on a nearby peninsula, a portion of the crew went down with the hull. Miraculously, the survivors inside have not drowned; a gnome named Roland Geardabbler maintains a sustained magical bubble of water breathing that preserves them within the wreckage. Surrounded by hostile aquatic predators and predatory naga, the remaining sailors wait in the dark forward compartments, unable to surface on their own. Evidence aboard the ship hints at the sinister forces behind its destruction. In the forward stairwell lies a small shard of raw Azsharite, a mysterious mineral unique to these shores. The Spitelash naga prowling the waters around the Ruined Reaches likely struck the Horizon Scout to plunder whatever artifacts or resources the expedition carried, dragging the vessel down to ensure no survivors could escape with secrets or treasures of the coast.

subzone:ice-thistle-hills.text: Ice Thistle Hills. The Ice Thistle Hills are a snow-covered highland rise lying just southeast of the goblin outpost of Everlook. Dominated by a rugged cavern system, the area is claimed by ferocious Ice Thistle yetis that threaten any travelers venturing off the main road. Rising sharply out of the central drifts of Winterspring, the Ice Thistle Hills serve as the primary hunting grounds and nesting territory for the valley's aggressive Ice Thistle yetis. Centered around a prominent cave dug deep into the rockface, these hulking beasts roam both the rocky slopes and the winding tunnels within. Because of their proximity to Everlook, the yetis present a constant nuisance and danger to goblin commerce and visiting prospectors, who regularly commission intrepid hunters to cull the beasts for their valuable thick pelts and pristine horns.

subzone:infectis-scar.text: Infectis Scar. The Infectis Scar is a deep, unnatural chasm carved into the blighted terrain of the Eastern Plaguelands near Corin's Crossing. Unlike natural ravines, this wound in the earth was ripped open by necromantic power when a cursed runeblade shattered against a dwarven shield. The blight festering at the bottom of the fissure remains an enduring testament to the Scourge's dark sorcery. While neighboring gorges like the Pestilent Scar originated as natural terrain features poisoned by the plague, the Infectis Scar is entirely artificial. It was created during the third war's violent clashes near Corin's Crossing. When the notorious death knight Marduk Blackpool clashed with a stalwart dwarf captain, Marduk's cursed runesword shattered against the captain's shield. Discarding the broken weapon, Marduk kept the hilt, but the severed runeblade sank deep into the soil.
