Named for the sickly fog that rolls down from the north, it provides a quiet and desolate route across the mountain range. Tucked away in the mountains northwest of Quel'Danil Lodge, Plaguemist Ravine acts as a geographic threshold between two radically different realms. To the south lies the lush, untamed highland forest of the Hinterlands, while to the north the pass opens directly upon Caer Darrow and the blighted expanse of the Western Plaguelands. The ravine earned its name from the foul, unnatural vapors that creep southward out of the Plaguelands, creating a jarring contrast with the crisp mountain air of the neighboring wilderness. Despite cutting directly into the edge of Scourge-ravaged territory, the ravine itself remains remarkably deserted. Travelers find neither wild beasts nor wandering undead lingering within the gorge itself. Because of this eerie stillness, the winding path serves as a convenient, albeit ominous, back road for daring couriers and adventurers wishing to bypass the heavily fortified highways and border checkpoints leading into Lordaeron.

subzone:plaguewood.text: Plaguewood. Once a peaceful woodland known as Greenwood, the Plaguewood is now a blighted, fungus-choked expanse stretching south of Stratholme. Crawling with Scourge infrastructure and patrolling Scarlet Crusaders, it stands as one of the most corrupt corners of the Eastern Plaguelands. Before the Third War, this region was Greenwood, a vibrant forest that mirrored the lush woods of Elwynn. A modest village sat near its entrance, and its roads were traveled by farmers and soldiers alike. All of that collapsed when tainted grain arrived from Andorhal. Today, spongy, corrupted soil has taken the place of rich earth, and titanic mushrooms dwarf the dead trees, constantly spewing noxious brown vapors across the woodland floor. Now completely claimed by the Scourge, the Plaguewood serves as a grim staging ground for the undead surrounding Stratholme. Ziggurats and slaughterhouses dot the decayed landscape, churning out abominations and cultists. To make matters worse for travelers, fanatic Scarlet Crusaders relentlessly patrol the road toward Stratholme's gates, eager to purge the Scourge and brutally slaughter any living wanderers they encounter.

subzone:plaguewood-tower.text: Plaguewood Tower. Plaguewood Tower is a ruined Lordaeron scout tower situated in the northern reaches of the Plaguewood near Terrordale. Shattered during the Scourge invasion, it now stands as a broken ruin amid the blighted forest. Standing on the edge of the blight-choked Plaguewood and the blighted town of Terrordale, Plaguewood Tower once served the Kingdom of Lordaeron as a vital northern watchpost. When the Scourge swept across the land, the fortification was battered into crumbling masonry and left in ruins amid corrupted fungal canopies. Today the fractured stones still overlook the northern trails, a silent reminder of the watch Lordaeron once kept over this land.

subzone:pool-of-tears.text: Pool of Tears. The Pool of Tears is a large, murky lake dominating the eastern reaches of the Swamp of Sorrows. Deep beneath its surface lies the sunken Temple of Atal'Hakkar, brought low by the Green Dragonflight to contain the horrors within. Today, vicious frenzies patrol the turbid waters, and ancient troll ruins litter its drowned banks. Long ago, fanatical Atal'ai trolls raised a monumental ziggurat to their bloodthirsty god, Hakkar the Soulflayer. Horrified by the blasphemies taking place within, the Dragon Aspect Ysera shattered the ground beneath the structure, submerging the massive temple into the depths of the marsh. The existing lake flooded over the temple ruins. While the dragons sought to bury the evil forever, the ziggurat still stands beneath the silt and waves, and green drakes remain vigilant in the area to keep its corruption sealed. Navigating the murky lake is treacherous for any adventurer heading toward the sunken halls. Flesh-eating frenzies infest the waters, while Atal'ai artifacts and drowned stonework remain scattered across the muddy floor. Travelers must brave these hostile shallows to access the upper passages of the submerged temple, where cultists and lingering dragon guardians vie for control of the dark sanctuary.

subzone:purgation-isle.text: Purgation Isle. Condemned spirits haunt Purgation Isle, off Hillsbrad’s southern coast. Tombstones and a ruined watchtower mark its winding paths, where fallen humans and dwarves wander without peace. Purgation Isle rises from the sea south of Hillsbrad, its winding paths passing tombstones and an abandoned watchtower. No living nation claims the isle. Condemned souls roam among the graves. They were paladins, priests, mages, and judges, and death has brought them no peace. Dark spellcasters have taken an interest in the condemned souls of Purgation Isle. The ogre necromancer Kormok and others are said to delight in calling upon the anguished dead. They summon the spirits to do their bidding.

subzone:quagmire.text: Quagmire. The Quagmire comprises the sprawling, treacherous heart of central Dustwallow Marsh. Bound by Brackenwall Village to the north and the Dragonmurk to the south, its waterlogged flats are notoriously difficult to navigate. Hostile beasts and ravenous oozes make any journey through this central fen perilous. Occupying the wide expanse between Lost Point in the west and Dustwallow Bay in the east, the Quagmire represents the wild core of the marsh. Footing is unreliable at best, with solid earth constantly giving way to murky water and clinging mud. Travelers must contend with predatory crocolisks lurking beneath the scum, aggressive spiders nesting in the dead brush, and strange oozes that seep through the muck. Beyond its natural hazards, the Quagmire serves as an unpredictable crossroads for the sentient powers contesting the swamp. Tucked away within the bog lies Tabetha's Farm, a lonely refuge for practitioners seeking hermit wisdom amid the dangers of the swamp.

subzone:quel-lithien-lodge.text: Quel'Lithien Lodge. Quel'Lithien Lodge is an isolated high elven hunting lodge nestled in the forested northern hills of the Eastern Plaguelands near the entrance to Quel'Thalas. Its Farstrider rangers hold out among the blighted woods, surrounded by the Scourge and hunted by Forsaken agents, while guarding old elven archives. Before the Third War, Quel'Lithien was a Farstrider camp on the road toward Quel'Thalas, and it housed elven records of the ranger order. The lodge fell on hard times after the Scourge swept through Lordaeron and into the elven kingdom. Today its rangers keep their vigil in the corrupted forest, one of only two major concentrations of high elves left in Lordaeron.

subzone:rage-scar-hold.text: Rage Scar Hold. Rage Scar Hold is a cavern carved into the wilderness of Feralas, situated on the mainland not far from Feathermoon Stronghold. It is notorious for housing some of the most vicious yetis in the region. Strangely, scattered books, symbols, and traces of night elven architecture deeper within suggest the den once served a far more civil purpose before the beasts claimed it. Carved into the rugged wilds of Feralas, Rage Scar Hold is dominated by savage yetis that attack anyone venturing near their lair. The creatures make the surrounding forest trails hazardous for both Alliance sentinels and passing travelers. While yetis are common to the untamed reaches of Kalimdor, the denizens of Rage Scar Hold stand out for their raw aggression and territorial ferocity. Deeper in the dark corridors of the cave lie subtle clues of an older occupancy. Carved stonework and night elven architecture suggest the cavern was once a barrow den or an arcane sanctuary. Forgotten tomes and mystic markings remain among the dirt and bone, leaving travelers to wonder whether unfortunate scholars were slaughtered by the beasts or if the yetis somehow gravitate toward the lingering magic of the site.

subzone:ragefire-chasm.text: Ragefire Chasm. Beneath Orgrimmar, Ragefire Chasm threatens the Horde from below. Its magma-lit tunnels hold savage troggs, and the Cleft of Shadow gives access to the caverns. Beneath Orgrimmar, dangers threaten the capital from below. While Thrall works to secure Durotar above, Ragefire troggs infest the chasm’s unstable vents and magma rivers. They rose from unknown depths and violently rejected Magatha Grimtotem’s attempts at diplomacy. Left unchecked, their numbers could undermine the city and overrun it.

subzone:raptor-ridge.text: Raptor Ridge. Raptor Ridge rises above the eastern Wetlands, northwest of the Dragonmaw Gates. Razormaw raptors hunt and nest among its crags, with a vicious matriarch deep in the caverns. Razormaw raptors hunt in packs across Raptor Ridge, where rocky trails climb above the eastern Wetlands. Travelers near the foothills of Khaz Modan risk meeting these predators. In a cavern at the ridge's heart, the Razormaw Matriarch guards her brood and nests from intruders. The Dragonmaw Gates lie close by.

subzone:ravaged-twilight-camp.text: Ravaged Twilight Camp. Tucked away in the secluded Crystal Vale of northwestern Silithus, the Ravaged Twilight Camp sits ruined among towering mineral formations. It serves as an isolated redoubt for the eccentric hermit Highlord Demitrian, a devotee of the Windseeker. While the Twilight's Hammer maintains numerous active outposts across the sands of Silithus, this broken encampment in the Crystal Vale tells a different story. Nestled far from the primary cult fortresses, the camp lies largely ruined and deserted, save for Highlord Demitrian. A servant of Thunderaan, Demitrian lingers amidst the stones, seemingly abandoned by or detached from the wider Twilight hierarchy while brooding over elemental bindings and the lost power of the Windseeker.

subzone:ravencrest-monument.text: Ravencrest Monument. Perched upon the windswept cliffs of southern Azshara, the Ravencrest Monument marks the shattered remnant of an ancient night elven colossus. Once a towering tribute overlooking the Great Sea, the statue has long since broken apart, leaving only towering legs and scattered stone ruins now stalked by hostile Spitelash naga. Standing high above the ocean southeast of the Ruins of Eldarath, the Ravencrest Monument was once an awe-inspiring marvel of Kaldorei stonework. Today, little remains of the majestic colossus beyond its pair of gigantic broken legs rooted to the stone plinth, with the shattered fragments of its torso and head either buried in the cliffside dirt or lost beneath the waves below. Reaching this remote coastal promontory requires trekking across the mainland bridges of Azshara, as sheer, rocky drops prevent any approach from the sea. Scholars often speculate that the monument commemorates Lord Kur'talos Ravencrest, the famed noble who rallied and led the night elven host during the War of the Ancients after the fall of Zin-Azshari. However, its close proximity to the pre-Sundering city of Eldarath and ambiguous surviving stonework leave its true origins debated. Rather than pilgrims or night elven caretakers, the surrounding cliff is currently claimed by the serpentine Spitelash naga, who defend the fallen monument with vicious territorial aggression.

subzone:rebel-camp.text: Rebel Camp. Tucked just off the road in northern Stranglethorn Vale, the Rebel Camp serves as a fortified refuge for Alliance soldiers who broke away from Colonel Kurzen. Led by Lieutenant Doren, these troops refused to surrender to the madness gripping their commander's expedition and now fight to survive and undo his descent into tyranny. When Colonel Kurzen's expedition pushed deep into the jungles of Stranglethorn Vale on behalf of Stormwind, things rapidly fell apart. Afflicted by the dark jungle magic and the curse of the ogre mage Mai'Zoth, the Colonel and his core loyalists succumbed to madness, turning rogue and terrorizing the wilds. A handful of sound-minded soldiers led by Lieutenant Doren refused to participate in the atrocities. Breaking away from Kurzen's Compound, they established this hidden camp in the north to stage a desperate guerrilla campaign against their former comrades. Perched precariously near the Duskwood border, the Rebel Camp operates under constant threat. Cut off from regular Stormwind relief, Doren relies on covert supplies and defensive armaments—including goblin explosives brokered through Booty Bay—to hold the perimeter against Kurzen's raiding parties. For Alliance travelers venturing south into the savage jungle, the encampment provides a vital first foothold of sanity.

subzone:refuge-pointe.text: Refuge Pointe. Refuge Pointe is the primary redoubt for the Alliance and the surviving remnants of Stromgarde within the Arathi Highlands. Perched centrally along the highlands' trade road, it serves as a staging ground to reclaim the shattered capital of Stromgarde Keep and hold back rival forces across the region. Following the devastation of the Third War and the catastrophic fall of Stromgarde Keep, the bulk of Stromgarde's surviving populace fled south toward friendlier lands. Those who remained formed a resolute vanguard, digging in at Refuge Pointe under Captain Nials. Composed of battle-hardened Stromgarde soldiers, League of Arathor forces, and supporting Alliance specialists, the encampment represents the kingdom's last organized stand in its ancestral homeland. Refuge Pointe is constantly on the brink of being overwhelmed. Hemmed in by the Forsaken and the Horde based out of Hammerfall, Witherbark trolls, Syndicate rogues, and Boulderfist ogres, the garrison has zero reserves to spare. When dwarven commanders at the battered Thandol Span desperately requested reinforcements to fight off the Dark Iron clan, Captain Nials had to refuse. Every sword, shield, and scrap of supply stationed at Refuge Pointe must remain dedicated to defending the highlands and preparing a counteroffensive to retake Stromgarde Keep.

subzone:roguefeather-den.text: Roguefeather Den. Roguefeather Den is a cavern nestled in the south-central reaches of Thousand Needles. Infested with ferocious screeching harpies, the cave serves as a fortified roost where the flock hoards scavenged provisions deep within its shadowed recesses. Carved into the sheer sandstone bluffs of southern Thousand Needles, Roguefeather Den is the foul nesting ground of local harpies. Known for their feral screeching and aggressive territorialism, the harpies treat the cavern as both a secure haven and a storehouse, vigilantly guarding the gathered food and stolen supplies they pile in the dark recesses at the back of the cave.

subzone:ruined-reaches.text: Ruined Reaches. The Ruined Reaches comprise the treacherous southern coastline of Azshara near the border with Durotar. Marked by crumbling ancient ruins, shattered shipwrecks, and jagged shallows, these beaches are overrun by aggressive shoreline predators. Amid the desolation, a small gnomish outpost perches high on a cliffside above the surf. Stretching along the southern borders of Azshara just north of Durotar, the Ruined Reaches are a maze of rocky inlets, cliff faces, and debris-strewn sand. Like the Jagged Reef further north, hidden shallows make maritime travel extremely hazardous, leaving numerous ruined vessels broken along the shore. The waters and beaches teem with hostile wildlife, including territorial murlocs, vicious hydras, and armored makrura, making overland transit just as dangerous as navigating the surf. Perched upon a western cliff overlooking the beaches sits an unexpected pocket of tinker civilization: a gnomish workshop accessible via a steep trail from Azshara's mainland. Run by Blimo and Jubie Gadgetspring, this outpost offers engineering components and general trade goods to passing adventurers. The interior features an elevator ascending to private quarters with three beds, though who—if anyone—claims the third bunk remains a quiet domestic mystery.

subzone:ruins-of-aboraz.text: Ruins of Aboraz. The Ruins of Aboraz are ancient Gurubashi stone ruins nestled along the southeastern cliffs of Stranglethorn Vale. Once part of the sprawling jungle troll empire, the crumbling terraces now serve as the secluded redoubt for the renegade witch doctor Zanzil the Outcast and his mind-addled thralls. Perched on the bluffs southeast of the Ruins of Jubuwal and south of the Crystalvein Mine, the weathered masonry of Aboraz has been transformed into an alchemical testing ground. Zanzil the Outcast was banished by the local tribes and the mainlanders alike, retreating here to brew potent mind-altering concoctions and toxic elixirs. Within the stone courtyards, Zanzil exerts total control over an unsettling menagerie of servitors, including shambling undead ghouls, corrupted troll thralls, and even co-opted coastal naga.

subzone:ruins-of-alterac.text: Ruins of Alterac. The snow-covered Ruins of Alterac are all that remain of Alterac City, once the proud mountain capital of the Kingdom of Alterac. Cast out of the Alliance and put under martial law after King Aiden Perenolde's treason during the Second War, the shattered stronghold is now overrun by the brutish Crushridge ogres. Alterac was once an independent human realm carved out of the old Arathor empire, perched high on the trade routes through the mountains. During the Second War, fearing destruction at the hands of the invading Old Horde, King Aiden Perenolde secretly struck a pact with the orcs. When the betrayal was uncovered following the fighting at Caer Darrow, the Alliance of Lordaeron retaliated swiftly. King Terenas Menethil II put the city under martial law and deposed Perenolde. The grand fortifications, church, and palace fell into disrepair as the populace fled or turned to outlawry. While surviving Alteraci nobles and rogue soldiers formed the Syndicate to wage guerrilla campaigns from towns like Strahnbrad, they lost their ancestral capital entirely. Today, the Crushridge ogres under Mug'thol dwell among the broken ramparts, palace halls, and wrecked ballistae. Neither the Syndicate nor the human defenders of Southshore have managed to reclaim the fallen city, leaving its crumbling towers and abandoned vaults as dangerous territory for treasure hunters and scavengers.

subzone:ruins-of-andorhal.text: Ruins of Andorhal. Once the agricultural hub and grain distribution center of northern Lordaeron, the Ruins of Andorhal now lie at the heart of the Western Plaguelands as a devastated Necropolis stronghold. Under the dominion of the lich Araj the Summoner, the shattered township crawls with legions of undead abominations, ghouls, and wraiths. Andorhal was the initial staging ground for the plague of undeath in Lordaeron, where grain tainted by the Cult of the Damned was packed and distributed across the human kingdom. Today, the ruined city serves as a sprawling bastion of the Scourge in the Western Plaguelands. Araj the Summoner presides over the center of the ruins, flanked by ghouls, skeletal horrors, and towering flesh golems. Scouting parties of the Scarlet Crusade periodically probe the city's outskirts, but the Scourge maintains iron control over the shattered streets.

subzone:ruins-of-constellas.text: Ruins of Constellas. The Ruins of Constellas are the shattered remnants of an ancient night elf settlement in Felwood, nestled near the roots of Mount Hyjal. Today, the once-sacred grounds are overrun by the Jadefire satyrs, who have violently profaned the settlement's moonwell with demonic fel magic. The classical stone arches and crumbling plazas of Constellas reveal that this was once an idyllic night elven community. During the Third War, the Burning Legion's march through Felwood shattered the haven, leaving it exposed to lingering demonic corruption. Now, the foul Jadefire satyrs hold dominion over the stones. Led by Xavathras, they actively tend to a defiled moonwell, transforming pure waters into a font of noxious fel power on behalf of their master, Lord Xavaric. The defilement of Constellas weighs heavily on all who would heal Felwood. To those working to cleanse the forest, Xavathras and his Jadefire are among its foulest corrupters, and the satyrs fiercely guard their tents among the ruins and the tainted moonwell at their heart against any who come to end their work.

subzone:ruins-of-eldarath.text: Ruins of Eldarath. The Ruins of Eldarath are the shattered remains of a pre-Sundering Highborne city perched along the rocky bluffs of Azshara. Once a bastion of Kaldorei arcane scholarship, its fallen plazas and crumbling temples are now overrun by hostile naga. Scholars and adventurers brave the dangerous coastal ruins searching for inscribed tablets and forgotten relics of the ancient past. Before the Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor ten thousand years ago, Eldarath was a flourishing night elven city. Renowned Highborne mages gathered here, carving their deepest arcane insights and fundamental magical rules into grand stone tablets left in public squares for their peers to study. The Sundering dropped much of Eldarath into the Bay of Storms. The portions that survived along the eastern cliffs have sat shunned by modern night elves for millennia, slowly claimed by creeping salt spray and ivy. In recent times, vicious naga have emerged from the sea to seize the shattered streets of Eldarath, commanded by warlords lurking within nearby sanctuaries like the Temple of Zin-Malor. Despite the danger posed by the serpents, the ruins remain an irresistible lure for outsiders. The Explorers' League has dispatched Alliance adventurers into the broken courtyards to take rubbings of Eldarath's ancient arcane tablets. Whispers of lost treasures and lingering magical energy also drew the blue dragon Azuregos to the surrounding wilderness, further confirming that secrets of immense power still sleep beneath the ruins' cracked flagstones.

subzone:ruins-of-isildien.text: Ruins of Isildien. The Ruins of Isildien are the sprawling remains of an ancient night elven city in southwestern Feralas, destroyed ten millennia ago during the Great Sundering. Today, the overgrown stonework and cracked temple courtyards are occupied by brutish Gordunni ogres. Ten thousand years ago, before the world shattered, Isildien was a grand night elven settlement nestled in the primordial forests of ancient Kalimdor. Its graceful marble arches and grand terraces stood as monuments to kaldorei civilization and devotion. When the Well of Eternity imploded and tore the continents apart, Isildien fell into ruined desolation, smothered under millennia of untamed jungle growth. Dominating the upper terrace is a colossal domed structure remarkably reminiscent of Darnassus's Temple of the Moon, suggesting the city was once a significant sanctuary dedicated to Elune. In the modern era, the elegant stonework of Isildien serves a far cruder purpose. The Gordunni ogres of Feralas have claimed the sprawling terraces and outcroppings as one of their primary settlements. The ogres have fortified the crumbling walkways, desecrating ancient plazas with crude bonfires, primitive barricades, and war banners, fiercely defending their stolen home against any outsiders who venture too close to the southern hills.

subzone:ruins-of-jubuwal.text: Ruins of Jubuwal. The Ruins of Jubuwal are the crumbling remnants of an ancient Gurubashi settlement located just east of the Gurubashi Arena in Stranglethorn Vale. Once a place of empire and ritual, the ruins have fallen under the sway of the rogue witch doctor Zanzil the Outcast and his bizarre retinue of minions. Situated off the primary thoroughfare cutting through Stranglethorn Vale, Jubuwal was once part of the grand Gurubashi civilization. Today, stone carvings and ivy-draped masonry have been overtaken by Zanzil the Outcast, an eccentric witch doctor known for his potent concoctions and foul voodoo. Zanzil has filled the ruins with an unnatural menagerie of followers, including enthralled ghouls, subjugated naga, and renegade trolls. Desperate fugitives also lurk among the stone arches, such as Jon-Jon the Crow and Maury 'Club Foot' Wilkins, both hiding from the ruthless debt collector 'Sea Wolf' MacKinley back in Booty Bay.

subzone:ruins-of-kel-theril.text: Ruins of Kel'Theril. The Ruins of Kel'Theril are the shattered remnants of an ancient night elven city bordering the frozen expanse of Lake Kel'Theril in central Winterspring. Destroyed ten thousand years ago during the Great Sundering, its frostbitten stone pillars and temples remain haunted by the tormented spirits of Highborne who perished in the cataclysm. Long before Winterspring became a frozen highland, Kel'Theril stood as a grand settlement of the ancient night elven empire. When the Well of Eternity collapsed during the Great Sundering, the city was blasted into ruin and buried beneath ice and snow. The disaster caught the residing Highborne unaware, binding their souls to the snowbound stones. Today, the spirits of these former spellcasters linger among the frostbitten arches, endlessly reliving their final, catastrophic moments. Travelers braving central Winterspring encounter restless, spectral Highborne haunting the ruined lakeside colonnades. These phantoms are often hostile, driven mad by millenniums of isolation and the violent magic that tore their civilization apart. However, a few sorrowful apparitions, such as the Remorseful Highborne, seek out travelers willing to hear their lingering laments and make peace with their forgotten past.

subzone:ruins-of-lordaeron.text:
Ruins of Lordaeron. At the Ruins of Lordaeron, the hollowed surface of Capital City guards the way into the Undercity. Once the heart of humanity’s northern empire, the city fell when Prince Arthas murdered his father and unleashed the Scourge. Capital City once united the northern realms under King Terenas Menethil II. Its splendor ended when Prince Arthas returned from Northrend with Frostmourne, the cursed runeblade. Celebration gave way to slaughter. Arthas slew his father on the throne, and the Scourge ruled the city as it rotted.

After civil war tore the Scourge apart, Lady Sylvanas Windrunner claimed the devastated palace. She secured the surface and expanded the crypts and dungeons below into the Undercity. The palace still bears the psychic wound of its violent fall. In the entryway and courtyards, travelers hear celebration bells, the murmurs of adoring crowds, and the chilling exchange between Arthas and his father before the regicide.

Blood still stains the grand throne room floor. Those with magical detection can glimpse spectral citizens reliving the afternoon their prince doomed them all.

subzone:ruins-of-ravenwind.text: Ruins of Ravenwind. The Ruins of Ravenwind are the shattered remnants of an ancient Highborne city nestled in northern Feralas. Today, the crumbling marble structures are heavily infested by the vicious Northspring harpies and guarded by brooding dragonkin. Much like the great city of Dire Maul to the east, the Ruins of Ravenwind stand as a solemn monument to the height and hubris of ancient Highborne civilization before the Great Sundering. Long abandoned by its original kaldorei architects, the site has succumbed to creeping wild foliage, forgotten arcane altars, and the foul roosts of Northspring harpies who prey on anything wandering beneath the shattered arches. Beyond the screeching harpies, Ravenwind is bordered by diverse and territorial threats. Fierce green dragonkin known as the Jaedemir circle the central groves and waterways, guarding ancient arboreal sites. Meanwhile, stray wanderers—from distracted night elf explorers to peculiar, solitary gnolls lingering nearby—frequently find themselves trapped in the crossfire of the ruins' lingering magics and wild predators.

subzone:ruins-of-thaurissan.text: Ruins of Thaurissan. The Ruins of Thaurissan are the scorched remnants of the Dark Iron clan's original surface capital in the Burning Steppes. Once a proud city nestled in the lush northern reaches of the Redridge Mountains, it was blasted to cinders during the War of the Three Hammers when Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan inadvertently summoned the Firelord, Ragnaros. Roughly two centuries ago, following their exile from Ironforge after the death of High King Modimus Anvilmar, the Dark Iron clan journeyed south and established Thaurissan City. At the climax of the War of the Three Hammers, facing total defeat by the combined forces of the Bronzebeard and Wildhammer clans, Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan sought an ultimate weapon to turn the tide. He and seven trusted sorcerers channeled ancient magic deep beneath the earth. Instead of an obedient servant, their ritual ripped open a conduit to the Elemental Plane and summoned Ragnaros the Firelord. The cataclysmic eruption shattered the surrounding mountains, burned the verdant landscape into the ashen Burning Steppes, raised the volcano of Blackrock Mountain, and incinerated the city.

subzone:ruins-of-uldum.text: Ruins of Uldum. Tucked into the jagged cliffs of the Valley of the Watchers in southern Tanaris, the Ruins of Uldum consist of an ancient stone hall guarding a sealed Titan facility. Massive stone doors protect its secrets from grave robbers and curious explorers alike. Carved deep into the bedrock of southern Tanaris, the Ruins of Uldum appear to be an antechamber or grand threshold to a far larger, sealed subterranean complex. Its colossal stone gates stand shut against the outside world, and no mechanism or key known to modern scholars has managed to open them.

subzone:ruins-of-zul-mamwe.text: Ruins of Zul'Mamwe. Tucked away in a mountainous pocket south of the Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound, the Ruins of Zul'Mamwe serve as a heavily fortified stronghold for the Skullsplitter troll tribe. Enclosed by steep cliffs on almost all sides, the ancient stone platforms now teem with fierce jungle trolls under the rule of their ruthless chieftain, Ana'thek the Cruel. The Ruins of Zul'Mamwe represent one of the primary seats of power for the Skullsplitter tribe in central Stranglethorn Vale. Cradled within a natural mountain amphitheater, the site has only a single open approach from the north, making it an exceptional defensive redoubt. From atop its weathered ziggurats and stone terraces, Chief Ana'thek the Cruel directs his warriors and witch doctors, defending their territory fiercely against both intruding adventurers and rival jungle troll tribes. Like many of the stone settlements dotting the jungle, Zul'Mamwe is a relic of the ancient Gurubashi Empire that once held undisputed dominion over the southern reaches of the continent. Although the grand empire splintered long ago into squabbling, hostile factions, modern Skullsplitters fiercely guard these ancestral stones, continuing age-old tribal rituals amid the overgrown masonry and broken monoliths.

subzone:rustmaul-dig-site.text: Rustmaul Dig Site. The Rustmaul Dig Site is a ruined excavation in the southern reaches of the Shimmering Flats. Originally established by the dwarven Explorers' League to unearth ancient ruins, the camp fell into tragedy when a Horde war party slaughtered the miners, after which a subterranean silithid swarm emerged. Now abandoned by mortals, the site crawls with hostile insectoids emerging from the caverns below. Prospectors from the Ironforge Explorers' League set up the Rustmaul Dig Site hoping to uncover forgotten artifacts buried beneath the salt flats. Their efforts were brutally cut short when an aggressive Horde war party, led by Moktar Krin, fell upon the camp and wiped out the dwarven excavators. However, the conquerors enjoyed no triumph. The violent clash apparently disturbed a dormant cave network beneath the site, releasing an endless horde of silithid insects that quickly overwhelmed and drove off the battered survivors. Today, Rustmaul stands entirely lost to the surface races. What remains of the mining equipment and scaffolds is buried under skittering mandibles and alien carapaces. The surviving members of Moktar Krin's war party retreated north to Ironstone Camp, terrified by the unrelenting tide of insectoids that emerged after their attack.

subzone:saltspray-glen.text: Saltspray Glen. Along Baradin Bay, salty spray sweeps across Saltspray Glen, where wild raptors roam the lowland. The glen lies between murloc waters and ancient dwarven ruins. In the Wetlands' far northwest, salty spray blows inland across Saltspray Glen from Baradin Bay. Bluegill Marsh and its murloc-haunted waters lie to the south, while the quiet bluffs of Ironbeard's Tomb rise to the east. Cunning wild raptors nest through the marshy grass and hunt across the brackish flats. Their kin range nearby at Raptor Ridge and Black Channel Marsh, leaving little comfort for travelers passing through.

subzone:salty-sailor-tavern.text: Salty Sailor Tavern. The Salty Sailor Tavern is the beating heart of Booty Bay's social life, serving as the port's primary inn and watering hole. Run by the goblin Innkeeper Skindle, it welcomes scoundrels, mercenaries, and travelers from both factions seeking respite from the perils of the jungle. Perched amidst the wooden tiers of Booty Bay, the Salty Sailor Tavern offers warm beds and strong drinks under the watchful eye of the Blackwater Raiders. Behind the bar stands Innkeeper Skindle, keeping glasses filled while a menagerie of buccaneers, traders, and adventurers mingle on neutral ground. Outside the establishment hangs a massive, curious curio—a Zul'Gurub Protector Stone—serving as a strange trophy in this bustling den of commerce.

subzone:sanctum-stromgarde-keep.text: Sanctum (Stromgarde Keep). The Sanctum is a sacred redoubt tucked behind the chapel within Stromgarde Keep. Sheltered within the crumbling fortress, it guards the entrance to the ancestral Trollbane family crypt and stands as one of the few remaining bastions of the Holy Light amidst Arathi's ruin. While much of Stromgarde Keep has fallen to Syndicate infiltrators and the Boulderfist ogres, the Sanctum and its adjacent chapel have remained under the fierce protection of the surviving Stromgarde defenders. Located behind the house of worship, the Sanctum borders the citadel's graveyard and marks the threshold to the royal crypt where the kings of Stromgarde rest. For the battered loyalists rallying around Prince Galen Trollbane, holding this hallowed ground represents more than a tactical foothold; it is a desperate fight to keep their kingdom's ancestral heritage and faith from being trampled by invaders. Beneath the stone flags of the Sanctum lies the passage into the royal tomb. The ground here is consecrated, intended as a place of peaceful reflection and worship of the Holy Light. In the wake of King Thoras Trollbane's murder and the kingdom's subsequent collapse, the Sanctum has instead become a defensive retreat. Those seeking to breach the inner sanctum must contend not only with the royal guards garrisoned throughout the halls, but with the haunting reality of an ancient human lineage clinging to survival on its sacred threshold.

subzone:sandsorrow-watch.text: Sandsorrow Watch. Sandsorrow Watch is a sprawling desert outpost located just west of Gadgetzan in Tanaris. The surrounding dunes and ruins are overrun by hostile Sandfury trolls and their reanimated dead, who also hold the eastern watch tower overlooking the waste. Situated directly west of the bustling goblin trading hub of Gadgetzan, Sandsorrow Watch is a grim borderland in the Tanaris desert. The broad expanse is dominated by the Sandfury tribe, who aggressively defend the arid territory alongside legions of shambling troll zombies. An elevated watch tower at the eastern edge anchors the position, providing a fortified vantage point amidst the encroaching desert wilderness and the hostile indigenous tribes. Even the watch tower at the eastern edge, within sight of Gadgetzan's walls, is held by the Sandfury. From its heights the Sandfury keep a wary eye on the goblin town, and travelers leaving through Gadgetzan's western gate walk almost directly into their territory, a constant reminder of the volatile frontier tension between Tanaris's opportunistic settlers and the native sand trolls.

subzone:sar-theris-strand.text: Sar'theris Strand. Sar'theris Strand forms the western coastline of Desolace, fronting the Veiled Sea. In stark contrast to the barren, grey inland wastes, the shore is sunny and grassy, though it remains perilous due to prowling naga, sea giants, and makrura. Running the length of western Desolace, Sar'theris Strand offers a bizarre respite from the ash and dust of the inland plains. Here, the clifftops and beaches are bright and green. Yet the strand is far from welcoming: serpentine naga patrol the surf alongside towering sea giants and territorial makrura. Shipwrecks litter the shoals, including the ruined Karnitol vessel to the north and small shattered skiffs beneath the towers of Ethel Rethor, proving the sea is as treacherous as the shore. Beyond the constant threat of naga and giants, the waters off the strand are known among seasoned travelers for their peculiar bounties. The jagged coastal shallows conceal salvage from lost expeditions and merchant ventures, while the deep surf is home to rare marine wildlife, notably the prized Sar'theris Striker fish sought out by master fishermen across Kalimdor.

subzone:sardor-isle.text: Sardor Isle. Sardor Isle is a lush island situated off the western coast of Feralas, north of the perilous Isle of Dread. It serves as the home to Feathermoon Stronghold, the primary night elven military bastion in southern Kalimdor. Despite the heavy sentinel presence, parts of the island remain prowled by wild beasts and hostile naga creeping up from the shallows. Resting across the water from mainland Feralas, Sardor Isle is anchored by Feathermoon Stronghold, an impressive elven garrison commanded by General Shandris Feathermoon. While the fortress itself is heavily fortified and linked to the mainland via regular ferry crossings, the broader island is far from tame. Roaming wolf packs claim the timbered slopes, while encroaching naga lurk along the rocky western and northern beaches, constantly testing the resolve of the night elven sentinels.

subzone:sargeron.text: Sargeron. Sargeron is the crumbled ruin of an ancient night elf city located in northern Desolace. Shattered during the Great Sundering, its former temples of Elune have been defiled and claimed by the Hatefury satyrs, who renamed the grounds in tribute to their master, Sargeras. Before the War of the Ancients broke the continent, this settlement was a flourishing center of worship dedicated to Elune, housing sacred grounds such as Elune's Temple, Sanctuary, and Cathedral. Its true name is lost to antiquity. When the world shattered, the city collapsed into rubble, leaving behind sanctified relics like the Cup of Elune, Elune's Brazier, and Elune's Handmaiden. In the millennia since, corrupted Hatefury satyrs overran the stones, repurposing the sacred Kaldorei architecture into a stronghold honoring the titan Sargeras.

subzone:savage-coast.text: Savage Coast. The Savage Coast is the rugged western shoreline of northern Stranglethorn Vale, stretching from the southern border of Westfall down toward Grom'gol Base Camp. Prowled by river crocolisks, shore basilisks, and hostile troll tribes, the strand earns its brutal name with every tide. Running from the cliffs bordering Westfall south toward Grom'gol Base Camp, the Savage Coast marks the perilous western edge of northern Stranglethorn Vale. The sandy banks offer little hospitality: snapjaws, crocolisks, and stonestalkers roam freely among the tide pools and drift logs. Just inland lie territorial jungle troll encampments, making any casual walk along the beach a fight for survival. Offshore, the waters dip toward the submerged dangers of the Vile Reef, ensuring that danger lurks both on the sand and under the waves.

subzone:scarab-dais.text: Scarab Dais. The Scarab Dais is an ancient raised platform situated northwest of the Scarab Wall in southern Silithus. It holds the legendary Scarab Gong, the ritual instrument tied directly to the magical wards sealing the qiraji empire within Ahn'Qiraj. Overlooking the shifting sands before the colossal barrier of the Scarab Wall, the Scarab Dais serves as the focal point for the seal placed upon Ahn'Qiraj a millennium ago. Upon this stone dais rests the Scarab Gong, a relic forged during the War of the Shifting Sands. According to ancient night elven history and the bronze dragonflight, striking this gong with the reconstructed Scepter of the Shifting Sands is the only means to shatter the magical barrier and breach the gates. Until that fateful moment arrives, the platform remains an ominous vigil over the sealed insectoid horrors slumbering beyond the wall.

subzone:scarab-wall.text: Scarab Wall. The Scarab Wall is a colossal barricade at the southern border of Silithus, before the insectoid empire of Ahn'Qiraj. Conjured at the end of the War of the Shifting Sands, the barrier combined stone and bronze dragonflight sorcery to contain the ancient swarms. It stands as an imposing reminder of the terrible cost of that war. Spanning the desert from east to west, the Scarab Wall was raised a thousand years ago at the conclusion of the catastrophic War of the Shifting Sands. Pushed to the brink of annihilation by the qiraji, the night elf armies and their dragon allies forced the swarms back into their ancient kingdom. To contain them permanently, an immense rampart of desert stone was raised, crowned by a colossal magical barrier woven by the bronze dragonflight. The wall successfully severed the insectoid armies from Kalimdor, though the dread presence locked behind its stone remains palpable.

subzone:scarlet-base-camp.text: Scarlet Base Camp. Scarlet Base Camp is a fortified outpost on the eastern shore of Lake Mereldar in the Eastern Plaguelands, just west of Tyr's Hand. Its barricades mark an outer defensive position of the Scarlet Crusade. Perched on the eastern bank of Lake Mereldar, Scarlet Base Camp is a barricaded fortification just west of Tyr's Hand. It marks an outer position of the Scarlet Crusade in the blighted countryside. Tyr's Hand is one of the Scarlet Crusade's strongholds in Lordaeron. The camp lies along its western approaches, in a region where the Crusade seeks to reclaim the land from the undead and treats outsiders with suspicion.

subzone:scarlet-basilica.text: Scarlet Basilica. The Scarlet Basilica is a grand cathedral standing at the heart of Tyr's Hand in the Eastern Plaguelands. It serves as the high seat of spiritual and military authority for the Scarlet Crusade in the east. Overseen by Crusader Lord Valdelmar, its halls represent the zealots' unyielding bastion against the Scourge. Rising prominently over the fortified enclave of Tyr's Hand, the Scarlet Basilica acts as the central cathedral and command hub for the Scarlet Crusade's operations in the Eastern Plaguelands. While the Scarlet Monastery far to the west in Tirisfal Glades serves as the order's spiritual heart, this basilica anchors their surviving territorial stronghold against the blighted horrors of Lordaeron. Guarded fiercely by elite crusaders, the cathedral houses Crusader Lord Valdelmar, who directs the local defense and zealously purges any outsiders who dare approach.

subzone:scarlet-monastery.text: Scarlet Monastery. Scarlet Monastery now shelters the fanatical Scarlet Crusade in Tirisfal Glades. Once a peaceful center of scholarship and worship for the Church of the Holy Light, it has become a fortified redoubt. Anyone approaching without red colors is treated as a carrier of the plague and executed on sight. Before the Third War, the Scarlet Monastery was a proud center of Lordaeron's priesthood. Its halls held theological studies and sacred archives, and paladins trained there. When the Scourge brought down the kingdom, surviving defenders held the site against the undead. Those survivors became the zealous Scarlet Crusade and fortified the cloister. Libraries, gardens, and the cathedral became parts of an armed stronghold. Four wings make up the Scarlet Monastery: a defiled graveyard, an expansive library, an armory, and a grand cathedral. Scarlet Commander Mograine and High Inquisitor Whitemane command its massive garrison. The Crusaders see every outsider as a plague-bearer, living or undead, Alliance or Horde. The Forsaken seek to destroy the garrison that threatens their doorstep, while Alliance leaders increasingly see the Crusade's violent extremism as a dangerous perversion of the Light.

subzone:scarlet-monastery-armory.text: Scarlet Monastery Armory. The Armory is the fortified martial wing of the Scarlet Monastery, dedicated to manufacturing weapons and training recruits for the Scarlet Crusade. Behind locked iron gates, ranks of zealous footmen and crusaders drill under the fierce command of Herod, the Scarlet Champion. Once part of a peaceful retreat for Lordaeron's priesthood, the monastery was completely overhauled following the Third War. The Armory now serves as the Crusade's primary forge, weapons depot, and combat proving ground. From the open training grounds to the deep weapon halls, ranks of Scarlet footmen, conjurers, and crusaders prepare relentlessly to purge the Scourge and anyone else they deem tainted. The wing remains locked away from the Grand Vestibule, accessible only to those carrying the Scarlet Key found in the neighboring Library. At the heart of the wing lies the Hall of Champions, lined with towering statues dedicated to legendary heroes of the Crusade's past. The hall is overseen by Herod, a brutal warrior whose ferocity and whirlwinds are legendary among the crusaders. Herod trains the next generation of zealots personally; when hard-pressed in battle, his desperate recruits will pour into the chamber to fight and die for their champion.

subzone:scarlet-monastery-cathedral.text: Scarlet Monastery Cathedral. The Cathedral is the spiritual and military heart of the Scarlet Monastery, housing the Crusade's inner sanctum. Once a serene hall of worship for Lordaeron's priesthood, it now serves as the command seat for High Inquisitor Whitemane and Scarlet Commander Mograine, guarded by the Crusade's most devoted zealots. Once a peaceful center of enlightenment and prayer for the priesthood of Lordaeron, the Cathedral fell into madness in the wake of the Third War. Following the fall of the kingdom to the Scourge, surviving zealots transformed the complex into a fortress of unyielding hatred. Beyond the manicured cloister of the Chapel Gardens lies the grand Crusader's Chapel, where priests and warriors gather in devotion to their crusade. They view all outsiders—regardless of race or faction—as carriers of the undead plague who must be cleansed by blade and holy fire.

subzone:scarlet-monastery-graveyard.text: Scarlet Monastery Graveyard. The Scarlet Monastery Graveyard is the burial wing of the grand religious complex in northeastern Tirisfal Glades. Once a serene resting place for Lordaeron's clergy and nobility, it has fallen into chilling neglect, overrun by lingering undead and the corrupted magic of the skeletal Bloodmage Thalnos. Before the Third War, this cloistered cemetery served as the peaceful burial ground for the priesthood of Lordaeron. When the Scarlet Crusade fortified the monastery against the undead, their fanatical vigilance failed to cleanse their own crypts. Today, the Graveyard is neglected and deeply haunted. Lingering spirits, restless corpses, and shambling horrors wander the Chamber of Atonement and the mist-covered Forlorn Cloister. Rather than hallowed rest, the dead have found endless torment beneath the crusade's uncaring gaze. At the rear of the grounds stands Honor's Tomb, where the greatest mockery of the Crusade's dogma festers: Bloodmage Thalnos. No record tells who he was in life, but the plague of undeath claimed him, and he rose as a skeletal horror wielding shadow bolts and fire. The crusaders above preach total extermination of the undead plague, yet they harbor a rotting, fallen sorcerer within their own consecrated soil.

subzone:scarlet-monastery-library.text: Scarlet Monastery Library. The Library is the eastern wing of the Scarlet Monastery in Tirisfal Glades, once dedicated to holy scholarship and Lordaeron's priesthood. Now guarded by battle hounds and zealots, it houses ancient archives and rare tomes fiercely coveted by scholars and mages from both factions. Before the Third War, the monastery served as a center for learning and enlightenment for Lordaeron's priesthood. The eastern cloisters housed vast archives of religious thought, historical records, and arcane treatises. When the Scarlet Crusade fortified the monastery against the Scourge, they retained these repositories, turning the quiet halls into an armed redoubt. Today, beastmasters run tracking hounds through the courtyards while battle-mages patrol the shelves, guarding historic volumes like the Compendium of the Fallen and ancient research on the Titans against outsiders. Breaching the Library requires navigating past Houndmaster Loksey in the Huntsman's Cloister, whose trained hounds sniff out infiltrators seeking passage into the inner chambers. Beyond the Gallery of Treasures lies the Athenaeum, overseen by Arcanist Doan. A formidable mage who wields devastating fire and protective sorcery, Doan studies in isolation, fiercely defending the Crusade's hoarded knowledge from any who venture into the heart of the complex.

subzone:scholomance.text: Scholomance. Hidden deep within the crypts beneath Caer Darrow, Scholomance is the Scourge's premier academy of dark arts and necromancy. Here, mortals and undead alike study the Plague of Undeath and fleshcrafting under the sadistic guidance of Darkmaster Gandling and the watchful gaze of the lich Ras Frostwhisper. Before the Third War, Caer Darrow was the proud seat of House Barov, a wealthy aristocratic dynasty holding vast lands across Lordaeron, including Brill, Tarren Mill, and Southshore. Fearing the loss of their wealth and mortality, the Barovs succumbed to Kel'Thuzad's seductive promises of eternal life. They deeded their fortress and ancestral catacombs to the Cult of the Damned, who promptly repaid the nobles by butchering them and turning the sprawling crypts into a hidden necromantic training ground.

subzone:scholomance-classic.text: Scholomance (Classic). Scholomance is a subterranean academy of necromancy hidden in the crypts beneath Caer Darrow in the Western Plaguelands. Founded by Kel'Thuzad and the Cult of the Damned, it serves as the Scourge's premier training ground for mortal spellcasters seeking to master death. Before the Third War devastated Lordaeron, the rogue archmage Kel'Thuzad sought recruits for his Cult of the Damned. He found willing benefactors in the wealthy Barov family, lords of Caer Darrow, who traded their lands and crypts in exchange for promised immortality. Instead, the cult slaughtered them and raised them as monstrous undead. Beneath the ruined fortress, the Cult renovated the ancient Arathorian catacombs into an academy for the dark arts. Here, mortal acolytes study plaguecraft, soul binding, and flesh shaping away from watchful eyes, honing the foul magics that shattered Lordaeron. Though Kel'Thuzad has moved on to direct Scourge operations from above, the school remains fully operational. The eternal lich Ras Frostwhisper holds vigil over the complex in the Scourge's name, while the mortal necromancer Darkmaster Gandling serves as its headmaster, tutoring ambitious sorcerers in horrific experiments. Those students who display weakness are discarded into the catacombs and fed to the Ravenian, a voracious wight lurking in the lower vaults.

subzone:sea-of-cinders.text: Sea of Cinders. The Sea of Cinders is an expanse of scorched, windblown terrain lying across the southern stretch of the Searing Gorge, directly north of Blackrock Mountain. Ravaged by elemental heat and relentless gusts, the flat ground constantly vents ash and embers, creating a choking wasteland where very little can endure. Stretching between the rocky cliffs of the Searing Gorge and the imposing bulk of Blackrock Mountain, the Sea of Cinders earns its name from the suffocating haze of particulate and burning grit that constantly sweeps its plains. When the Firelord Ragnaros was summoned into the mortal world centuries ago, the violent upheaval fractured the Redridge Mountains and transformed the surrounding landscape into an arid slag heap. The Sea of Cinders is among the most barren remnants of that cataclysm, an uninhabitable plain where the earth itself refuses to cool. Because it borders the north approach to Blackrock Mountain, travelers and scavengers often have no choice but to cross these scorching flats. The winds here kick up dense clouds of blinding ash that hide sudden fissures, elemental horrors, and wandering predators adapted to the searing heat. Between the hostile environment and the looming presence of the Dark Iron dwarves who claim the region, any trek across the cinders demands vigilance and swift passage.

subzone:sentry-point.text: Sentry Point. Sentry Point is a human watchtower stationed on the mainland edge of Dustwallow Marsh, guarding the causeway bridge that leads directly to Theramore Isle. Maintained by Theramore's forces, it monitors traffic entering and exiting Lady Jaina Proudmoore's island citadel. Positioned at the western end of the long bridge linking Theramore Isle to the treacherous wetlands of Dustwallow Marsh, Sentry Point serves as the stronghold's first line of defense on the mainland. The stone scout tower keeps watch over the swamp road, ensuring that hostile marsh beasts or Horde raiders cannot approach the island city unnoticed.

subzone:serpent-s-coil.text: Serpent's Coil. Serpent's Coil is a winding network of caves and burnt-out encampments nestled in the eastern ridges of the Blasted Lands. Littered with scorched orcish architecture left behind from the older wars, it serves as a secluded redoubt for dark cultists. Carved into the jagged eastern cliffs of the Blasted Lands, the winding path and caverns of Serpent's Coil wind past ruined orcish huts that date back to the First and Second Wars. Rather than simple beasts, the tunnels harbor cabals of Shadowsworn cultists and practitioners of dark arts drawn to the residual demonic energies permeating the red wastes. Deep within its twisting hollows, they work far from the watchful eyes of Nethergarde Keep.

subzone:shadow-hold.text: Shadow Hold. Shadow Hold is a sprawling subterranean complex hidden within the blighted canyon of Jaedenar in western Felwood. Once a sacred night elf barrow den, it has been seized and desecrated by the Shadow Council to serve as their primary bastion on Kalimdor. Beneath the corrupted red earth of Jaedenar lies Shadow Hold, a vast underground labyrinth carved out of what was once an ancient night elf barrow den. Where sleeping druids once rested to tend the Emerald Dream, dark warlocks and demonic servitors now stalk twisted corridors illuminated by fel fire. At its deepest tiers, the cult commands a formidable force under the dreadlord Lord Banehollow, Prince Xavalis, and Shadow Lord Fel'dan, making it the supreme seat of demonic influence in the region.

subzone:shadowbreak-ravine.text: Shadowbreak Ravine. Shadowbreak Ravine is a secluded mountain hollow tucked away in southeastern Desolace. Cloaked among jagged crags near Magram Village, this eerie ravine serves as a hidden redoubt for the demonic forces and mortal zealots of the Burning Blade. Tucked deep into the barren mountain ridges southeast of Magram Village, Shadowbreak Ravine provides the Burning Blade with a secluded staging ground away from the eyes of wandering centaur tribes. Amid strange, oversized mushrooms and grim ritual encampments, cultists labor alongside summoned demons. Here, dark practitioners invoke fel energies and tend heavy ritual chains, using the natural isolation of the ravine to marshal reinforcements and maintain a firm demonic foothold within the badlands of Desolace.

subzone:shadowfang-keep.text: Shadowfang Keep. On a rugged bluff above Pyrewood Village, Shadowfang Keep broods over southern Silverpine Forest. Once Silverlaine Keep, it fell to worgen summoned during the Third War and became the lair of the mad Archmage Arugal, haunted by slain nobles and overrun by wolf-beasts. Before the Third War, Baron Silverlaine ruled nearby Pyrewood Village from his ancestral seat, Silverlaine Keep. When the Scourge swept through Lordaeron, desperate wizards sought forbidden means to stem the undead tide. Drawing on Dalaran mage Ur's dimensional research, Archmage Arugal summoned worgen from beyond this world. The savage beasts tore through the Scourge, then escaped control. They rampaged across southern Silverpine and besieged the keep, killing Baron Silverlaine, his family, and the defenders under Commander Springvale. Guilt and grief broke Arugal's sanity. He claimed the fortress, renamed it Shadowfang Keep, and called the monstrous predators his children. Shadowfang Keep is the heart of a growing wolf curse in Silverpine Forest. Arugal dwells in the highest observatory, surrounded by ravenous worgen of the Moonrage and Shadowfang packs. Sinister beasts also prowl the keep, including his massive pet wolf, Fenrus. Below Arugal's sanctum, the restless ghosts of the keep's former lords and household remain trapped in torment. Baron Silverlaine and Commander Springvale are among them, cursed to defend the halls they failed to protect in life. From the walls, Arugal's influence reaches Pyrewood Village and the surrounding woodlands, threatening the neighboring Forsaken who seek to purge the forest of his madness.

subzone:shadowprey-village.text: Shadowprey Village. Shadowprey Village is a remote Horde fishing settlement built along the rocky southern coast of Sar'theris Strand in Desolace. Populated largely by Darkspear troll fishermen and supported by tauren service keepers, it acts as a critical coastal outpost and trade lifeline amidst a barren wasteland. Tucked against the cliffs of southern Desolace, Shadowprey Village offers safe harbor in a region notorious for centaur clans and desolate wastes. The settlement is primarily an encampment of troll fishermen whose hauls sustain not only their own village but also inland outposts like Ghost Walker Post. Despite the rough shoreline, towering wooden piers reach out into the ocean, allowing local anglers to brave deep waters and dive for shellfish among the submerged wreckage dotting Sar'theris Strand. Maintaining a frontier port in Desolace is fraught with danger. Beyond the inland threat of marauding centaur and the demon-summoning Burning Blade, the ocean itself tests the village's survival with rough shoals and hungry sea life. Tauren allies, including Taiga Wisemane and the keepers of the inn and wind rider roost, help shore up defenses and keep trade routes open across Kalimdor.

subzone:shadowsong-shrine.text: Shadowsong Shrine. Shadowsong Shrine is a ruined hillside sanctuary situated in western Azshara, not far from the Ashenvale border. Haunted by the restless spirits of ancient Highborne, the site bears the illustrious name of the Shadowsong bloodline, though its true historical connection to them remains shrouded in mystery. Perched upon a high hill overlooking the shattered lands of Azshara, the Shadowsong Shrine lies in ancient, overgrown ruin. Like much of the surrounding coast, it is plagued by the lingering apparitions of Highborne ghosts who wander among the fallen stonework, seeking to extinguish any mortal life that trespasses upon their domain. The shrine shares its name with Maiev Shadowsong, the unrelenting warden of Illidan Stormrage. Whether this sanctuary honors her family or dates back to before the Sundering is a secret lost to the ages.

subzone:shady-rest-inn.text: Shady Rest Inn. The Shady Rest Inn was once a welcoming human-built waystation sitting just off the road between the Barrens and Theramore Isle. Today, only charred timbers and smoldering ashes remain following a sudden and violent arson attack. The tragedy left the innkeeper shattered and sparked tension across the marsh as investigators sift through the wreckage for clues. Built to serve travelers navigating the treacherous crossing between Dustwallow Marsh and the Barrens, the Shady Rest Inn stood as an outpost of civilized comfort in a harsh wilderness. That ended when the inn was abruptly razed to the ground in a devastating fire. Innkeeper James Hyal managed to survive the inferno, but the blaze claimed the lives of his wife and child. Traumatized and grief-stricken, Hyal was left with nothing as the ruins became an active crime scene, drawing scrutiny from Theramore authorities desperate to identify who ignited the flames.

subzone:shalzaru-s-lair.text: Shalzaru's Lair. Shalzaru's Lair is a sprawling, submerged cavern located at the northern tip of the Isle of Dread in Feralas. It serves as a major stronghold for the Hatecrest naga and shelters their formidable master, Shalzaru. From within these damp tunnels, the serpentine invaders coordinate their aggressive presence just south of Feathermoon Stronghold. Carved into the rugged bluffs at the northern end of the Isle of Dread, Shalzaru's Lair is divided into a massive main cavern and a smaller auxiliary chamber, linked together by submerged subterranean waterways. The interior teems with Hatecrest serpent guards and spell-weaving sorceresses on high alert. Deep within the recesses dwells Lord Shalzaru, the serpentine overlord directing the Hatecrest brood across the island. Its proximity to Sardor Isle poses a direct, constant threat to the night elf Sentinels garrisoned at Feathermoon Stronghold just across the channel.

subzone:shaper-s-terrace.text: Shaper's Terrace. Perched high on the northern bluffs above Marshal's Refuge, the Shaper's Terrace is a mysterious overlook marked by ancient titan architecture. It is named in honor of Khaz'goroth the Shaper and bears quiet witness to the primordial experiments that shaped Un'Goro Crater. Overlooking the lush, prehistoric basin of Un'Goro Crater, the Shaper's Terrace holds monumental stone edifices left behind by the titans. Believed to be dedicated to Khaz'goroth the Shaper, this high plateau stands as a testament to the celestial architects who cultivated the crater as a living laboratory for early life on Azeroth. From these elevated stones, ancient entities once observed and directed the flora and fauna below. Its cold stone arches and massive metallic plinths stand in stark, enigmatic contrast to the untamed wilderness thriving directly beneath them.

subzone:shatter-scar-vale.text: Shatter Scar Vale. Shatter Scar Vale is a scorched basin in central Felwood, located just north of Bloodvenom Falls. It marks the ground zero where demonic infernals crashed into northern Kalimdor during the Third War. Today, the craters still burn with fel fire and host lingering remnants of the Burning Legion. During the Third War, the Burning Legion rained living siege engines down upon northern Kalimdor. Shatter Scar Vale bore the brunt of this celestial assault. Demonic infernals plummeted from the skies, tearing through the ancient canopy and smashing deep craters into the earth. The violent impact shattered the terrain, leaving blackened hollows that smolder with unholy fire to this day. Though the Legion was shattered at Mount Hyjal, the infernals and lingering lesser demons never truly dispersed, maintaining an entrenched foothold in the scarred earth.

subzone:shattered-strand.text: Shattered Strand. The Shattered Strand is a wild, rugged coastline flanking the northern rim of the Bay of Storms in Azshara. Dominated by crashing surf and crumbling ancient ruins, the beach crawls with hazardous marine beasts and tribal aquatic creatures. Stretching along the northern edge of the Bay of Storms, the Shattered Strand is far from a peaceful shoreline. The rocky beaches and tidal shallows are heavily inhabited by aggressive wildlife, including towering sea giants, multi-headed hydras, and snapping makrura, alongside encampments of coastal murlocs. Crumbling elven architecture overlooks the waves, anchored by landmarks such as the ancient Temple of Arkkoran and the solitary Tower of Eldara. For travelers navigating Azshara's treacherous cliffs, descending to this isolated strip of coast means confronting some of the region's deadliest amphibious threats.

subzone:shifting-mire.text: Shifting Mire. The Shifting Mire forms the vast, muddy heart of the Swamp of Sorrows, lying just west of the Pool of Tears. Its name comes from the strange, restless silt beneath the murky water, which seems to drift and gather under the influence of an unseen force. Spanning the central reaches of the marshland, the Shifting Mire is an unsettling expanse where solid footing is hard to come by. The silt along the swamp floor shifts and collects as though moved by a living will, driven by a strange, ambient energy permeating the peat. Amidst the drifting mud prowl predatory swamp jaguars, massive sorrow spinners, and hungry sawtooth crocolisks, while bands of broken draenei known as the Lost Ones stalk the sunken paths.

subzone:slag-pit.text: Slag Pit. The Slag Pit is an extensive subterranean mining excavation nestled inside the Cauldron of Searing Gorge. Overseen by ruthless Dark Iron taskmasters and slavers, these fiery tunnels are driven by forced labor under the shadow of Blackrock Mountain. Trespassers must contend not only with hostile dwarf overseers, but also ravenous incendosaurs prowling the lower levels. Carved into the depths of the Cauldron, the Slag Pit represents the grinding industrial engine of the Dark Iron dwarves in Searing Gorge. Day and night, enslaved workers are driven to extract rich ores and minerals under the lash of brutal overseers and taskmasters. The environment is harsh and suffocating, dominated by scorching heat, choking dust, and the clatter of iron picks. The Dark Irons maintain ruthless discipline over their excavation, violently repelling any outside interference with their supply lines to Blackrock Depths. Beyond the cruelty of the slavers, the physical tunnels themselves pose a deadly hazard to workers and intruders alike. In the lower reaches of the excavation, the earth breaks open into scorching caverns inhabited by incendosaurs—ferocious reptilian beasts native to the fiery underground. Despite the constant danger of being devoured by these subterranean predators, the Dark Iron masters continue to push their labor force deeper into the rock, entirely indifferent to the lives lost in the process.

subzone:slaughter-hollow.text: Slaughter Hollow. In the snowy heights of the Alterac Mountains, Crushridge ogres hold Slaughter Hollow as a secluded camp. Travelers rarely come here except to hunt ogres or cross the frozen passes. Slaughter Hollow shelters the Crushridge ogres high in the peaks between Hillsbrad and Alterac. Makeshift fires, scattered bones, and crude shelters mark the mound. Other ogre dens in the highlands often see fights over territory or stolen supplies, but Slaughter Hollow stays quiet and beyond the reach of major military campaigns. Crushridge ogres sometimes keep prisoners taken along the mountain trails in their secluded mound. Travelers speak of Rizz Loosebolt, an unlucky gnome locked in a crude cage and trying to bargain with anyone who passes. Captives seldom fare well against the clan's appetite.

subzone:slither-rock.text: Slither Rock. Slither Rock is a secluded cave tucked into the far northeastern cliffs of the Burning Steppes, past the perilous Terror Wing Path. It serves as the solitary refuge of Cyrus Therepentous, a sharp-tongued black dragonspawn with his own hidden agenda. Tucked away in the scorched crags beyond the Terror Wing Path, Slither Rock is easy to overlook amid the fiery wastes of the Burning Steppes. Far from the roaring forges and marching orc warbands of Blackrock Spire, this remote hollow houses the solitary black dragonspawn Cyrus Therepentous. While dragonspawn are typically fiercely loyal soldiers of the Black Dragonflight, Cyrus maintains a strange, cantankerous independence here, willing to converse with mortal travelers rather than slaughtering them on sight—though never without a steady stream of insults.

subzone:slithering-scar.text: Slithering Scar. The Slithering Scar is a sprawling silithid hive dominating the southern cliffs of Un'Goro Crater. Home to the aggressive Gorishi swarm, its excavated tunnels and organic spires represent a dangerous insectoid encroachment into the primeval basin. Gouged into the red earth and rock of southern Un'Goro, the Slithering Scar stands as an alien intrusion against the lush prehistoric landscape. The hive is controlled by the Gorishi silithid, an organized strain of insectoids that have honeycombed the cliffs with damp burrows and egg chambers. Within these subterranean warrens, workers and tunnelers nurture vast clutches of eggs and grubs alongside towering wasp broods. More alarmingly, the colony cultivates fledgling silithid colossi, monstrous behemoths intended to carve an uncontested path through the crater's ecology. Strange crystalline formations nestled within the hive pulse with unnatural resonance, acting as focal points for the colony's dark, coordinated will. Scholars and explorers who traverse the perimeter of Un'Goro often notice a disturbing anomaly regarding the hive's location. While ancient crystalline pylons stand sentinel across the northern, eastern, and western boundaries of the basin, the southern reaches possess no such pillar. It is precisely in this unprotected gap that the Gorishi have burrowed inward from the neighboring deserts. Whether the silithid purposefully undermined a forgotten southern ward or simply invaded where the crater's primordial wards were weakest remains an unsettling mystery to those watching their rapid expansion.

subzone:sorrow-hill.text: Sorrow Hill. Sorrow Hill is an expansive graveyard resting south of Andorhal in the Western Plaguelands. Once the final resting place for commoners, soldiers, and nobility alike, it has been corrupted by nearby plague cauldrons into a sprawling haven of restless undead. Before the Third War, Sorrow Hill served as the primary burial ground for the city of Andorhal and its surrounding townships. When the Scourge unleashed the Plague of Undeath, the gravediggers could not keep pace with the dead. Neatly kept crypts were soon surrounded by shallow, poorly marked earthen pits. Eventually, terrified survivors ceased traditional burials entirely, instead resorting to burning the corpses of their loved ones in a mass pyre to the south out of fear they would rise. Before the town fell completely, the remnants of the populace entombed Lord Uther the Lightbringer atop the cemetery's high ground, bestowing upon the hill its tragic name. The Scourge's foul plague cauldrons across the region have long since corrupted Sorrow Hill. The interred soldiers and citizens now wander the mist-shrouded headstones as skeletal flayers and ravenous ghouls, while skeletal mages and a local Scourge commander nest in the southeastern crypts. Because the cemetery sits directly along the road between Chillwind Camp and Andorhal, both the Alliance and the Argent Dawn frequently order patrols to culled the ranks of undead here to maintain a vital foothold in the region.

subzone:sorrowmurk.text: Sorrowmurk. The Sorrowmurk is the treacherous wetland expanse lying directly east of the Pool of Tears in the Swamp of Sorrows. Long dominated by patrolling green dragonkin guarding the approach to the Sunken Temple, it remains one of the most perilous regions in the eastern marshes. Stretching out along the eastern edge of the Pool of Tears, the Sorrowmurk is a dense and murky mire that borders the Forbidding Sea. For years, the waters and tangled boughs have crawled with ferocious green dragonspawn and towering drakes, remnants of the brood sent to watch over the submerged temple of Atal'Hakkar. Their presence ensures that only seasoned travelers dare wander through its sodden reaches.

subzone:south-seas.text: South Seas. The South Seas encompass the vast, sun-drenched waters separating the southern regions of Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. Lapping at the shores of Tanaris and Stranglethorn Vale, these tropical expanses are famed for lucrative trade routes, perilous reefs, and brazen pirate crews. Spanning southward beneath the Great Sea and the Maelstrom, the South Seas wash against the deserts of Tanaris and the lush jungles of Stranglethorn Vale. Since the Great Sundering shattered the primeval continent ten thousand years ago, this ocean has nurtured remote tropical islands, unique oceanic beasts, and independent merchant networks. Goblin shipping cartels, operating out of havens like Steamwheedle Port and Booty Bay, maintain tenuous shipping lanes across the waves. However, the waters remain notoriously lawless, crawling with corsairs, Bloodsail buccaneers, and predatory sea life that prey on any vessel daring to venture far from shore. Beyond the coastal trade lanes lies a patchwork of legendary islands and sunken perils. Notable lands scattered across the South Seas include the ancient troll island of Zandalar and the produce-rich shores of Tel'Abim. Yet merchant sailors must contend with far more than cutthroats; the deeper waters harbor colossal giant squids, primeval sea turtles, and lurking naga who guard ancient ruins swallowed by the waves. Navigating these waters demands seasoned captains, reliable charts, and substantial firepower.

subzone:southern-savage-coast.text: Southern Savage Coast. The Southern Savage Coast encompasses the long strand of beaches and tidal waters hugging southwestern Stranglethorn Vale. Flanked by the treacherous depths of the South Seas, these shores are home to prowling wildlife, hostile naga, and the ever-present threat of coastal raiders. Stretching down the western edge of the southern jungle, the Southern Savage Coast marks where the mainland gives way to the warm currents of the South Seas. Divided from the northern Savage Coast by the submerged ruins and perils of the Vile Reef, this coastline skirts inlets near the Gurubashi Arena and Nek'mani Wellspring before tapering off past Booty Bay and Janeiro's Point. While the beaches offer open ground compared to the suffocating interior jungle, travelers must contend with aggressive reptilian predators, predatory naga hunting the shallows, and passing corsairs scanning the strand for easy prey.

subzone:southfury-river.text: Southfury River. The Southfury River is one of the most prominent waterways on central Kalimdor, carving a swift and wide path southward from the heights of Mount Hyjal. It forms the natural border separating Azshara from Ashenvale, as well as Durotar from the Barrens, before plunging into the Great Sea near Ratchet. Beginning high in Mount Hyjal, the Southfury drops over dramatic cascades before coursing through central Kalimdor. Its roaring waters serve as a clear geographic divide, separating the sacred forests of Ashenvale from ancient Azshara, and dividing the arid hills of Durotar from the savanna of the Barrens. Only a few strategic bridges dare cross its swift currents—most notably the heavy span guarding the rear gates of Orgrimmar and the crossing connecting Durotar to the Barrens. The river eventually empties into the Great Sea via a cascading waterfall just northeast of the neutral port of Ratchet. For the Horde, the Southfury is both a shield and a vital natural highway. It protects the western approaches of Durotar and Orgrimmar from immediate ground assault while supplying fresh mountain runoff through an otherwise scorched, sun-baked landscape. Just north of the western crossing into Orgrimmar lies a singular geographic crossroads where four major territories converge: Ashenvale, Azshara, Durotar, and the Barrens. Control over this churning waterway ensures supply lines between Orgrimmar and the outlying Horde settlements remain intact.

subzone:southmoon-ruins.text: Southmoon Ruins. The Southmoon Ruins are ancient stone remains situated in southern Tanaris, just north of the Valley of the Watchers. Long claimed by the brutish Dunemaul ogres, the crumbling stonework preserves remnants of the ancient troll civilization that dominated the desert before the sands swallowed it. Rising out of the blistering wastes of southern Tanaris, the Southmoon Ruins stand as a weathered testament to the ancient troll empires that once ruled Kalimdor's southern reaches. Like nearby Eastmoon and Noonshade, its stone pillars and altars have weathered thousands of years of wind and abrasive grit. The site has often served as a squalid camp for the Dunemaul ogres, who show little reverence for the craftsmanship of the past, using the ancient structures purely for shelter and territory. The architectural remnants are unmistakably trollish, but little is recorded of the people who raised Southmoon's stones or why they abandoned them. Whatever they left behind lies buried beneath the drifting sand, and the ogres who squat among the pillars care nothing for it.

subzone:southpoint-tower.text: Southpoint Tower. Forsaken scouts watch Alliance movements from Southpoint Tower, near Hillsbrad's western edge. The ruined Lordaeron post overlooks the road into Silverpine Forest. Southpoint Tower overlooks the highway between Silverpine Forest and Hillsbrad Foothills. The Kingdom of Lordaeron built it to guard traffic between the eastern farmlands and the western woods. After the Third War and the Scourge's destruction of the kingdom, the stonework fell into ruin. Now the tower stands roofless and crumbling, a remnant of human rule in fractured lands. Forsaken agents watch Alliance patrols from the ruined tower. Deathstalker Lesh is among those stationed there, keeping an eye on nearby human settlements in Hillsbrad Fields and travelers on the main road. The vantage remains valuable despite the collapsed walls. So close to hostile territory, this lonely post often becomes a flashpoint for skirmishes.

subzone:southridge-beach.text: Southridge Beach. Southridge Beach stretches along the southern shores of the Bay of Storms in central Azshara. Once a grand district of the ancient kaldorei city of Eldarath, its shattered ruins are now overrun by hostile naga, murlocs, and towering sea giants. Southridge Beach forms the southern boundary of the turbulent Bay of Storms. Thousands of years ago, this coast was part of the magnificent Highborne city of Eldarath, but the Great Sundering broke the land and plunged most of its palaces beneath the tides. Today, crumbling marble pillars and weathered stone pavilions dot the sand. Rather than scholars and noble courtiers, the strand is contested by aggressive Spitelash naga, prowling makrura, vicious hydras, and scavenging murloc tribes. Even massive sea giants occasionally wander ashore from the deeps.

subzone:southshore-town-hall.text: Southshore Town Hall. At Southshore Town Hall, Magistrate Henry Maleb directs the town’s affairs and defenses. It remains one of Lordaeron’s last centers of civil authority, while the Alliance struggles to hold ground in the plagued north. Southshore Town Hall keeps human rule alive amid Lordaeron’s ruin.
