Magistrate Henry Maleb governs from his office, working with officials such as Kundric Zanden to secure supplies and preserve order. Undead press from nearby lands, Syndicate rogues threaten the region, and Hillsbrad’s border sees fierce skirmishes. From the hall, town leaders direct Southshore’s survival against these threats.

subzone:southwind-village.text: Southwind Village. Southwind Village is the haunted ruin of a night elf outpost located in the sands of Silithus. Wiped out by the qiraji during the War of the Shifting Sands, its streets are now bound by the restless spirits of fallen defenders and prowling silithid. Southwind Village once served as a primary night elf stronghold during the ancient War of the Shifting Sands a thousand years ago. When the qiraji legions breached the defensive perimeter, Valstann Staghelm—son of Archdruid Fandral Staghelm—led a detachment to hold the village. The defense ended in utter disaster: the night elven defenders were overwhelmed and slaughtered, and Valstann himself was dragged away into captivity by General Rajaxx. The village was completely ruined, leaving its former buildings fractured under the sun. A millennium after its fall, Southwind Village remains an open wound in the desert. The trauma of the assault was so absolute that the spirits of the slain night elf Sentinels and druids could not move on. Driven mad by the horror of their final moments, these restless phantoms—led by the Shade of Ambermoon—endlessly roam the crumbled stone walls, lashing out at any who intrude while predatory silithid swarm the surrounding dunes.

subzone:splinterspear-junction.text: Splinterspear Junction. Splinterspear Junction is a strategic fork in the main road winding through the heart of the Swamp of Sorrows. Dominated by a rugged orc watchtower and regularly patrolled by Horde sentries, it divides the path between northern retreats and southern outposts. Standing near the center of the Swamp of Sorrows, Splinterspear Junction divides travelers between two paths: the northern trail leading toward the Lost One refuge of the Harborage and the Fallow Sanctuary, and the southern road running directly past the fortress of Stonard toward the Blasted Lands. An ancient orcish watchtower oversees the split, garrisoned and patrolled by active Horde troops. For members of the Horde, it serves as a secure landmark in a treacherous marsh; for Alliance travelers, it represents a deadly ambush point along an already unforgiving trail.

subzone:stagalbog.text: Stagalbog. The Stagalbog is a dense, waterlogged marsh stretch across the southern reaches of the Swamp of Sorrows. Bordering the southern mountain range just below the Pool of Tears, it remains an untamed wilderness. Stretching beneath the shadow of the southern crags, the Stagalbog is typical of the Swamp of Sorrows: stagnant water, drooping reeds, and tangled vegetation. It sits immediately south of the sunken ruins of the Temple of Atal'Hakkar, caught between the tainted lake and the rocky boundary of the region. Apart from rough wildlife, civilization has established no foothold here. Because it borders the Pool of Tears, the Stagalbog frequently catches whatever shadows or corruptions seep from the Sunken Temple.

subzone:stagalbog-cave.text: Stagalbog Cave. Stagalbog Cave is a damp subterranean cavern situated in the Stagalbog within the eastern reaches of the Swamp of Sorrows. It serves as a fortified den for the Marsh murlocs and their sinister spiritual leader, the Swamp Talker. Tucked away in the murky eastern wetlands of the Swamp of Sorrows, Stagalbog Cave provides shelter from the relentless swamp rains for the local murlocs. Known as the Marsh tribe, these amphibious creatures aggressively guard the winding cavern chambers alongside their chief mystic, the Swamp Talker. Travelers venturing near the sunken mire of the Stagalbog often hear their gurgling calls echoing out across the mossy banks, warning trespassers away from their nesting grounds.

subzone:staghelm-point.text: Staghelm Point. Staghelm Point is an ancient night elven watchtower perched atop a craggy peak in northeastern Silithus. Overlooking the encroaching dunes and the nearby caverns of Twilight's Run, the tower stands as a vigil against the ancient threats haunting the desert. Rising high above the arid flats of northeastern Silithus, Staghelm Point is crowned by a solitary night elf tower. The outpost serves as a lonely sentinel, keeping watch over the wasteland and the shadowed cultists lurking in nearby caves like Twilight's Run. Watched over by Ralo'shan the Eternal Watcher and accompanied by a bronze drake circling overhead, the tower bears the proud and tragic name of the Staghelm lineage—a reminder of the immense sacrifices made by the Kaldorei during the ancient War of the Shifting Sands.

subzone:starfall-village.text: Starfall Village. Starfall Village is a tranquil night elven sanctuary nestled along the snowy road of Winterspring. As the sole Alliance outpost in the frozen valley, it offers shelter and supplies to travelers braving the bitter northern chill. It also stands watch over the nearby barrow den. Situated northwest of the goblin trading post of Everlook and south of Frostsaber Rock, Starfall Village represents the lone bastion of Alliance civilization in Winterspring. Composed of traditional night elven timber lodges, the settlement serves as a haven for wayfarers, providing critical supplies and a warm hearth amid the harsh mountain elements. Despite its peaceful appearance, the village remains ever vigilant, positioned adjacent to a quiet, unoccupied barrow den.

subzone:steamwheedle-port.text: Steamwheedle Port. Steamwheedle Port is a bustling coastal outpost on the eastern shore of Tanaris, directly connected to Gadgetzan. Operated by the neutral Steamwheedle Cartel, it serves as an essential sea link across the South Seas while constantly warding off encroaching Southsea Pirates. Tucked against the dunes along the South Seas, Steamwheedle Port offers the inland desert city of Gadgetzan a direct lifeline to maritime trade. Run by the Steamwheedle Cartel, the settlement bustles with dockhands, traders, and sea captains braving the treacherous waters. Supply vessels regularly ply the routes between here and distant goblin trading posts, bringing valuable mechanical components, luxuries, and raw materials into southern Kalimdor. Life on the port is far from peaceful. Just south along the coast lies Lost Rigger Cove, home to rampant Southsea Freebooters who regularly raid goblin shipping, steal cargo, and contest control of the coastline. Aside from haggling dockworkers and paranoid merchants trying to recover stolen shipments, the port also shelters unusual travelers, such as the enigmatic troll Yeh'kinya, who studies the ancient and ominous spirits of the world away from prying eyes.

subzone:stonard.text: Stonard. Stonard is a fortified Horde outpost situated in the southern marshes of the Swamp of Sorrows. Originally built during the First War, it serves the modern Horde as an essential foothold in the southern Eastern Kingdoms and an observation post watching the Blasted Lands. Stonard stands as one of the oldest orcish settlements on Azeroth. First established when the Old Horde spilled through the Dark Portal into what was once the Black Morass, Stonard and its sister post, Rockard, anchored the invaders' lines. Though abandoned and damaged during the fallout of the Second War, Thrall's New Horde moved to reconstruct and garrison Stonard. Anchored by a traditional orcish Great Hall and fortified burrows, the outpost is now a vital island of Horde authority in an untamed, perilous mire. Modern Stonard functions as both an expeditionary camp and a staging ground. Cartographers and scouts fan out across the surrounding muck to map the uncharted swamp and monitor hostile native beasts, lost draenei wanderers, and the sunken Temple of Atal'Hakkar to the east. Crucially, Stonard also provides the Horde with an organized staging post just north of the shattered Blasted Lands, ensuring a watchful eye remains near the dormant Dark Portal.

subzone:stonemaul-ruins.text: Stonemaul Ruins. The Stonemaul Ruins are the shattered remnants of Stonemaul Village, once the proud Kalimdor settlement of the Stonemaul ogres. After being driven out by the black dragonflight, the clan fled north, leaving their former home overrun by Firemane dragonspawn. Following their migration to Kalimdor, the Stonemaul ogres founded their settlement amid the murky swamps of Dustwallow Marsh. The village became famous when the beastmaster Rexxar braved the clan's lethal trials, slew their brutal chieftain Kor'gall, and rallied the ogres to defend the nascent Horde against Admiral Proudmoore's forces. After the war, Rexxar left the ogre Mok'Morokk in command. Under Mok'Morokk's selfish rule, the village fell into decline and was ultimately ambushed and shattered by the black dragonflight. The surviving ogres fled north to establish Brackenwall Village, while Onyxia's brood took complete possession of the ruins. Today, the ruins are firmly ensconced within Dragonmurk and crawl with Firemane dragonspawn tending the brood's nearby nesting grounds. While Overlord Mok'Morokk grew cowardly and content to languish in Brackenwall, older and prouder clan members like Tharg and Draz'Zilb refuse to abandon their homeland. Operating out of Brackenwall, they urge Horde champions to slaughter the occupying dragonspawn and smash the dragonflight's eggs in hopes that the Stonemaul may one day march back and reclaim their ancestral village.

subzone:stonewrought-pass.text: Stonewrought Pass. Stonewrought Pass is an underground tunnel cut directly through the southern mountains of Loch Modan into the blighted expanse of the Searing Gorge. Masterfully engineered by the famed architect Franclorn Forgewright, this passage connects the Valley of Kings directly to Dustfire Valley. Heavy iron gates secure both ends to protect peaceful dwarven lands from the volcanic terrors to the south. Carved out of the bedrock by the legendary master architect Franclorn Forgewright—famed also for the massive Stonewrought Dam—the Stonewrought Pass serves as a direct corridor between the pastoral beauty of Loch Modan and the scorched wastes of Searing Gorge. Emerging in Loch Modan near the colossal Valley of Kings, it cuts straight through the mountain ridge down into Dustfire Valley. Because Searing Gorge is infested with Dark Iron dwarves and fiery beasts, the Ironforge mountaineers keep the passage locked tight behind heavy gates to prevent danger from spilling into the north.

subzone:stormrage-barrow-dens.text: Stormrage Barrow Dens. The Stormrage Barrow Dens are an ancient subterranean sanctuary carved beneath the sacred valley of Moonglade. Named for Malfurion Stormrage, these quiet earth-hewn chambers serve as a dedicated resting place where druids enter long, restorative slumbers to wander the Emerald Dream. Barrow dens serve as sacred havens throughout night elven lands, providing druids a safe subterranean refuge where their physical bodies can lie undisturbed during lengthy immersions in the Emerald Dream. The Stormrage Barrow Dens are particularly esteemed within the sacred realm of Moonglade. Named in honor of Archdruid Malfurion Stormrage, these winding earthen halls hold both ancient reverence and quiet vigil. While some druids like Clintar Dreamwalker still slumber safely within its alcoves, the absence of the great Archdruid himself casts a somber shadow over the hollowed roots and peaceful glowing lanterns. During the desperate days of the Third War, these dens stood on the brink of total ruin. The dreadlord Tichondrius and the Burning Legion's forces sought to eradicate the sleeping druids before they could rally. High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind fought her way through invading demons and hostile corrupted wildlife deep into these earthen tunnels to blow the Horn of Cenarius, waking Malfurion Stormrage in the nick of time. Since Archimonde's defeat at Mount Hyjal, Malfurion's spirit has once more drifted into the Dream, leaving his brethren to watch over these sacred earthen depths.

subzone:stormwind-city.text:
Stormwind City. Stormwind City leads the Kingdom of Stormwind and the Alliance from its seat of power. Rebuilt after the First War, it is Azeroth's greatest remaining human stronghold since the northern kingdoms fell. Stormwind City rose over a thousand years ago, founded by Arathi descendants who migrated south. Its coastal ramparts sheltered a flourishing capital, where swift rivermills powered the city. In the First War, the Orcish Horde broke through its defenses and burned Stormwind to the ground.

Sir Anduin Lothar led the surviving refugees across the Great Sea to Lordaeron. After the Alliance won the Second War, the Stonemasons' Guild rebuilt the capital with white stone, canals and towering spires. The fortress now stands north of Elwynn Forest. Stormwind City is mankind's chief refuge and stronghold after the Scourge shattered Lordaeron and the Third War left Dalaran heavily ruined. The disciplined Stormwind City Guard patrols its broad avenues and defensive walls. The Cathedral of Light's spires guide faith across the southern kingdoms.

Yet political troubles linger beneath the orderly districts and ceremonial gates. King Varian Wrynn has mysteriously vanished, and his young son Anduin sits on the throne. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon governs as regent, with the whispered counsel of royal advisor Lady Katrana Prestor.

subzone:stratholme.text: Stratholme. Stratholme was once the jewel of the Eastweald and the second greatest city in the Kingdom of Lordaeron. During the Third War, it became the site of Prince Arthas Menethil's infamous culling after its citizens consumed grain tainted by the Plague of Undeath. Today, the ruined metropolis still burns, serving as the Scourge's primary stronghold in northern Lordaeron. Long before its downfall, Stratholme stood as a cornerstone of northern civilization. Emerging centuries ago from the Arathi expansion into the Eastweald, it flourished into Lordaeron's second-largest settlement, renowned for holy shrines and sacred water capable of resisting dark sorcery. Prior to the Second War, Archbishop Alonsus Faol gathered at the city's chapel to establish the Order of the Knights of the Silver Hand, ordaining legends like Uther the Lightbringer. Throughout that war, Stratholme served as a vital port, supply hub, and northern oil refinery for the Alliance of Lordaeron, enduring an assault by the Old Horde before rebuilding in victory. Stratholme's fate was sealed when the Cult of the Damned funneled shipments of infected grain from Andorhal into the city's markets. Unaware, thousands ate the tainted flour. When Prince Arthas arrived alongside Uther and Jaina Proudmoore, he discovered the infection had spread too far to cure. Deeming slaughter the only way to deny Mal'Ganis an entire army, Arthas ordered the purge of every citizen—an atrocity that drove Uther and Jaina away and began the prince's descent into madness. The city was put to the torch, and in the aftermath, the Scourge moved into the smoking ruins to make it their regional capital.

subzone:stratholme-classic.text: Stratholme (Classic). Stratholme, once northern Lordaeron's proudest jewel and the birthplace of the Silver Hand, is now a burning ruin serving as the Scourge's regional capital. Divided between the fanatical Scarlet Crusade and Baron Rivendare's undead legions, the cursed city remains locked in endless, violent war. Before the Third War, Stratholme was the northern powerhouse of Lordaeron and the sacred birthplace of the Knights of the Silver Hand. Its fate was sealed when Prince Arthas purged the city, slaughtering his own subjects after infected grain brought the plague within its walls. Left smoldering and ruined, Stratholme was claimed by the Scourge. Today, under the overarching authority of the lich Kel'Thuzad and the field command of Baron Rivendare, the city serves as the primary base for undead power in the Plaguelands. Stratholme is split between two vicious factions locked in perpetual bloodshed. To the west, the fanatical Scarlet Crusade has fortified Crusaders' Square and the Scarlet Bastion, commanded by Grand Crusader Saidan Dathrohan. To the east lies the Scourge slaughterhouses and necropolises, defended by towering ziggurats and the death knight Baron Rivendare. Anyone entering the city must navigate this grinding crossfire, surrounded by burning tenements and restless spirits.

subzone:stratholme-main-gate.text: Stratholme Main Gate. The Stratholme Main Gate stands as the grand, burning entrance to Lordaeron's northern metropolis in the northwestern Eastern Plaguelands. It provides direct access through the city's ruined avenues toward King's Square and the crusader fortifications within. Stratholme was once the pride of northern Lordaeron, famed as the birthplace of the Order of the Silver Hand. Today, its colossal arched main gates mark the threshold of an ongoing nightmare. It was here during the Third War that Prince Arthas turned on his mentor, Uther the Lightbringer, and purged his own citizens before the Plague of Undeath could claim them. The city has burned relentlessly ever since, transformed into the primary Scourge stronghold in the region. Approaching through the main gate leads straight into the ruins of King's Square and Market Row, heading toward the fortified district known as the Scarlet Bastion. Zealots of the Scarlet Crusade pushed through this entrance to reclaim the city and purge the dead, carving out an encampment in the ruins. However, the crusaders find themselves surrounded by overwhelming undead monstrosities, fighting an attrition war they cannot win against the dark forces orchestrating Stratholme's defense.

subzone:stratholme-service-entrance.text: Stratholme Service Entrance. The Stratholme Service Entrance is a fortified rear gateway located at Eastwall Gate in the northern Eastern Plaguelands. It provides direct, covert access into the Scourge-controlled eastern quarter of the burning city, bypassing the grand front gates. While the monumental Main Gate of Stratholme opens into King's Square and provides a route toward the Scarlet Bastion, the Service Entrance breaches the city's eastern fortification at Eastwall Gate. Today, it leads directly into the corrupted heart of the metropolis: Elders' Square and the blighted pathways leading toward Baron Rivendare's slaughterhouses. Venturing through the service portal offers a shorter approach to the Scourge's eastern districts. The surrounding alleys crawl with gargoyles, crypt fiends, and cultists guarding the dread ziggurats. For the Argent Dawn and daring adventurers seeking to strike at the ruling death knight directly, this hidden iron gate serves as the primary staging point for surgical strikes against the Lich King's commanders.

subzone:stromgarde-keep.text: Stromgarde Keep. Stromgarde Keep is the battered, divided capital of the fallen human kingdom of Stromgarde in the Arathi Highlands. Once the proud cradle of human civilization known as Strom, the fortress is now partitioned between hostile Syndicate rogues, invading Boulderfist ogres, and a desperate remnant of royal defenders under Prince Galen Trollbane. Long before it bore its current name, this fortress was founded nearly three millennia ago as Strom, the first capital of the unified human empire of Arathor under King Thoradin. It served as the staging ground for humanity's victory against the forest trolls and was the birthplace of human wizardry, where high elven magi tutored the first hundred human spellcasters. Over centuries, as younger sister kingdoms like Dalaran, Lordaeron, and Stormwind rose and prospered, Strom's influence waned. Renamed Stromgarde by the stubborn Trollbane dynasty who stayed behind, it remained a proud warrior bastion throughout the Second War, anchoring the Alliance of Lordaeron against the Orcish Horde. Following the devastation of the Third War, Stromgarde finally buckled under mounting catastrophes and treachery. Today, the majestic stone city sits fractured into three warring sectors. The aristocratic traitors of the Syndicate occupy the grand inner keep, while brutish Boulderfist ogres have overrun the former sanctum of the mage district. Pinned in the remaining quarter, Prince Galen Trollbane and the battered Stromgarde military wage a grueling, bloody war on multiple fronts just to keep their ancestral home from vanishing into memory.

subzone:sundown-marsh.text: Sundown Marsh. In the Wetlands' far west, Sundown Marsh holds deep water, stagnant pools, and dangerous wildlife. An eccentric pair keeps a solitary home along its muddy borders. Sundown Marsh fills the Wetlands' deepest, westernmost reaches, where deep water and thick mud hide a dense population of predators. Giant crocolisks, shifting oozes, roaming raptors, and territorial Mosshide gnolls move through the mist. Most travelers keep to the main cobblestone road between Menethil Harbor and Ironforge, leaving this corner largely untamed. A lonely stone cottage with a churning windmill stands amid the marsh's hazards. The gnome Fradd Swiftgear and the dwarf Wenna Silkbeard make their living scavenging the bog. They sell curiosities and rare trade recipes recovered from the mire to travelers who brave its aggressive denizens.

subzone:sunnyglade.text: Sunnyglade. Sunnyglade was once a wealthy, prosperous human settlement belonging to the kingdom of Stormwind during the First War. Devastated and eventually abandoned as the front lines collapsed, the ruined settlement now languishes under the dark influence of the Twilight's Hammer cult. Before the First War tore southern Azeroth apart, Sunnyglade was celebrated for its wealth and comfortable prosperity. That peace was violently shattered when the Old Horde invaded. Orc raiding parties attacked the town and enslaved its surviving residents, leaving only a lone wizard's tower intact to study the arcane arts of human conjurers. Though Stormwind forces mounted an effort to rescue the captive peasants and rebuild the settlement, the surrounding Riverglades were steadily swallowed by the advancing Horde. Deeming the outer province lost, Stormwind's commanders eventually withdrew their resources to defend the homeland, leaving Sunnyglade to ruin. Today, Sunnyglade lies far beyond the safe borders of Stormwind's reestablished realm. While the iconic stone mage tower remarkably weathered the First War and the years of abandonment that followed, the peaceful township around it is gone. Instead, the secluded ruins have been occupied by zealots of the Twilight's Hammer cult, who turn the once-prosperous valley to their own sinister designs.

subzone:swamplight-manor.text: Swamplight Manor. Swamplight Manor is an ironically named, ramshackle wooden shack nestled deep within Witch Hill in Dustwallow Marsh. It serves as the eccentric home and kitchen of 'Swamp Eye' Jarl, an isolated recluse known across the mire for his strange culinary appetites. Despite its humble, eerie isolation, the surrounding garden conceals intrigue that catches the attention of both Theramore and Brackenwall Village. Despite what its grandiose title suggests, Swamplight Manor is far from a lordly estate. It is merely a crooked, weather-beaten shack tucked into the haunted wetlands of Witch Hill. Its lone resident, the odd recluse known as 'Swamp Eye' Jarl, lives a solitary existence surrounded by fog, muck, and restless marsh ghosts. Jarl spends his days concocting unusual regional delicacies out of local wildlife, frequently recruiting wandering adventurers to hunt down bizarre ingredients like marsh frog legs and creature eyes to satisfy his strange craft.

subzone:swarming-pillar.text: Swarming Pillar. The Swarming Pillar is a towering rock formation in the heart of Silithus, thoroughly infested and reshaped by the silithid. Situated just south of Cenarion Hold, the spire takes its name from the relentless clouds of winged insectoids buzzing around its peaks and subterranean entrances. Rising abruptly from the shifting dunes of central Silithus, the Swarming Pillar serves as a grim monument to the unchecked expansion of the silithid. What began as a natural rock formation has been carved and encrusted with the resinous secretions and burrows of the insectoid swarm. Just south of Cenarion Hold, it constantly churns out broods of winged workers and soldiers, whose dark clouds fill the dry desert air and warn travelers to keep their distance. Though massive and intimidating on the surface, the Swarming Pillar is merely the outward protrusion of a vast underground network. Beneath its stony exterior lie deep tunnels and cavernous breeding chambers that anchor one of the largest hives in the region. The Cenarion Circle views the spire with immense concern, as its active broods directly threaten druidic operations and hint at the terrifying coordination behind the insectoid menace.

subzone:tabetha-s-farm.text: Tabetha's Farm. Deep in the murkiest reaches of the Quagmire lies Tabetha's Farm, an isolated homestead centered around a small wooden hut, a modest garden, and a private dock. Despite the treacherous marsh surroundings, this sanctuary serves as a hidden redoubt for the hermit mage Tabetha. Tucked away in the western wetlands of Dustwallow Marsh, Tabetha's Farm defies its unforgiving environment. Consisting of a weather-worn hut, small vegetable plots, and a dock for navigating the swamp's murky waterways, the homestead offers a quiet refuge far from the political rivalries of Theramore and Brackenwall Village. Here, the reclusive human sorceress Tabetha lives in near-total seclusion, pursuing esoteric studies of arcane and fel power without interference from Dalaran or local authorities. Despite its remote location, the farm attracts practitioners of the magical arts from across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. Mages seeking mastery over raw arcane surges and warlocks seeking aid to cleanse volatile artifacts like the Orb of Orahil are directed to Tabetha's doorstep.

subzone:tahonda-ruins.text: Tahonda Ruins. The Tahonda Ruins are the sun-bleached remnants of an ancient tauren settlement swallowed by the salt and sand of the Shimmering Flats. Little is remembered of the villagers who once lived here, and dangerous Saltstone basilisks now stalk among the decaying tent poles and shredded leather. Situated in the southern reaches of the Shimmering Flats near the pass into Tanaris, the Tahonda Ruins stand as a somber monument to an abandoned tauren past. The village fell long ago, its weathered structures gradually engulfed by shifting white salt crusts. While some suspect the local Saltstone basilisks drove the inhabitants away, odd clues linger on the surviving structures. Two distinct sets of three parallel tears cut through the leather of a ruined lodge, suggesting the village met a violent end at the claws of powerful predators or hostile invaders before the desert claimed what remained.

subzone:tainted-scar.text: Tainted Scar. The Tainted Scar is a demon-infested canyon carved into the southwestern Blasted Lands, saturated with foul fel magic from the nearby Dark Portal. It currently serves as the primary redoubt for the remnants of the Burning Legion on Azeroth, commanded by the doomguard Lord Kazzak. Once lush wetlands belonging to the ancient Black Morass, this desolate trench was utterly drained of life and turned the color of dried blood by chaotic fel energies leaking from the Dark Portal. Following Archimonde's defeat at Mount Hyjal during the Third War, surviving forces of the Burning Legion rallied in the south. The colossal ered'ruin Lord Kazzak claimed the Tainted Scar as his stronghold, stationing elite demons across its blackened rises and dispatching dreadful lieutenants like Razelikh the Defiler to hold dominion over the wasted red soils. While most mortals shun the Scar on pain of agonizing death, practitioners of the dark arts find its saturated fel energies irresistible. An eccentric human warlock named Daio the Decrepit has taken up residence by a ruined demonic altar overlooking the horrors, using the rampant fiends to perform dark rituals and instruct aspiring warlocks in how to summon and bind dread infernals.

subzone:talonbranch-glade.text: Talonbranch Glade. Talonbranch Glade is a quiet night elf redoubt nestled in the blighted hills of northern Felwood. Located just south of Timbermaw Hold, it provides a rare haven of pristine moonlight, sanctuary, and hippogryph transit in an otherwise corrupted wilderness. Perched on high ground near the tunnel to Timbermaw Hold, Talonbranch Glade serves as the northernmost bastion of the Alliance in Felwood. Centered around a sheltered night elf lodge and a functioning moonwell, the outpost offers a crucial refuge from the demonic corruption that has swallowed the surrounding forest. Alliance scouts, Sentinels, and passing adventurers use the glade to rest, recover, and plan their excursions deeper into the tainted woods or onward toward Winterspring and Moonglade. Aside from its natural and spiritual defenses, Talonbranch Glade functions as an essential logistics hub. Hippogryphs stationed here connect travelers to Auberdine in Darkshore and Everlook in the snowy expanse beyond Timbermaw Hold. It remains a lonely, vigilant watchpost holding the line against the encroaching shadows of the Shadow Council and feral beast packs roaming the corrupted vales.

subzone:temple-of-arkkoran.text: Temple of Arkkoran. The Temple of Arkkoran is an ancient night elven ruin resting on the northeastern cliffs of Azshara above the Shattered Strand. Originally built in honor of Elune, the crumbling structure has since been claimed by the towering sea giant Arkkoroc and his aquatic thralls. Like many of the grand ruins dotting Azshara's coast, the Temple of Arkkoran was once a sanctum dedicated to the moon goddess Elune before the Sundering shattered the ancient night elf empire. Today, its weathered marble steps and broken colonnades are overrun by tidal monstrosities. The sea giant Arkkoroc presides over the temple's highest level, surrounded by loyal makrura and vicious murlocs who violently defend the surrounding coastline from any land-dwelling intruders.

subzone:temple-of-atal-hakkar.text: Temple of Atal'Hakkar. The Temple of Atal'Hakkar, widely known as the Sunken Temple, is a submerged fortress built by exiled troll priests dedicated to the blood god Hakkar. Sunk beneath the marshes by the green dragonflight centuries ago, its drowned halls remain a staging ground for forbidden rituals and dark corruption. Over a millennium ago, a catastrophic civil war shattered the Gurubashi Empire when the Atal'ai priesthood attempted to summon Hakkar the Soulflayer. Exiled to the north, the surviving zealots raised a massive stone temple in the Swamp of Sorrows to finish their dark work. Learning of their scheme, the Dragon Aspect Ysera smashed the ziggurat deep into the mire, inundating its chambers beneath the Pool of Tears. Green dragon wardens were left behind to guard the drowned ruins and ensure Hakkar's return was thwarted forever. Instead of burying the cult, the temple's submersion provided the Atal'ai isolation to continue their grisly sacrifices unhindered. Over the centuries, corruption began to rot the guardians from within; the dragon sentinels succumb to madness while the Atal'ai, guided by Jammal'an the Prophet, prepare the way for Hakkar's avatar. Now, both the Horde and Alliance keep an anxious eye on the submerged ziggurat as shadowy rumors slip out from the swamp's depths.

subzone:temple-of-zin-malor.text: Temple of Zin-Malor. The Temple of Zin-Malor is an ancient night elven sanctuary located within the Ruins of Eldarath in Azshara. Originally dedicated to the moon goddess Elune, the crumbling structure is now held by the Spitelash naga under the direct command of Warlord Krellian. Before the Great Sundering, the Temple of Zin-Malor stood as a grand house of worship dedicated to Elune. Its architecture closely mirrors both the nearby Temple of Arkkoran and the modern Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, bearing the graceful, sweeping stonework characteristic of pre-Sundering night elven civilization. Today, however, its moonlit marble is weathered and broken, overtaken by the serpent-bodied Spitelash naga. These invaders have claimed the holy grounds for themselves, turning a place of quiet reflection into a militarized redoubt. The temple once housed the renowned Crystal of Zin-Malor, a potent artifact that was carried away long ago to Kel'Theril in Winterspring.

subzone:terrace-of-repose.text: Terrace of Repose. The Terrace of Repose is a pristine courtyard garden located just outside the entrance to the Scarlet Monastery in Tirisfal Glades. Maintained by the Scarlet Crusade, it stands as one of the few places in northern Lordaeron completely untouched by the Plague of Undeath, complete with green hedges and clean water. Situated just north of the grand entrance into the Scarlet Monastery, the Terrace of Repose offers a surreal contrast to the rotting forests of Tirisfal Glades. While the rest of Lordaeron chokes under grey mist, corrupt soil, and stagnant bogs, this terrace boasts verdant, neatly pruned hedges and a functioning fountain fed by fresh, uncontaminated water. For the zealots of the Scarlet Crusade, the garden serves as physical proof of their divine righteousness and purity, a sacred bastion demonstrating that holy devotion can ward off the Scourge's corruption.

subzone:terror-run.text: Terror Run. Terror Run is a perilous swath of land situated in the southwestern reaches of Un'Goro Crater, directly west of the insectoid hives of the Slithering Scar. True to its fearsome name, the territory is stalked by predatory beasts, ranging from massive devilsaurs to ravenous diemetradons and swooping pterrordax. Stretching across the southwestern shelf of Un'Goro Crater, Terror Run lives up to its ominous reputation. Fierce pterrordax wheel through the humid air above while massive diemetradons, stegodons, and apex devilsaurs roam the low brush below. The territory sits directly in the shadow of the mountainous rim, wedged uncomfortably close to the chittering alien mounds of the Slithering Scar. Along the eastern edge of the flats lie the ruined remnants of a camp left behind by Williden Marshal's expedition, a sobering reminder of researchers who were caught unprepared when the crater's primeval predators closed in. Beyond the sheer concentration of hungry fauna, Terror Run draws naturalists and adventurers alike for a geological rarity: it is the primary ground in the crater where curious Red Power Crystals emerge from the fertile soil. The crimson formations hum with primeval energy akin to the blue, green, and yellow crystals found elsewhere in the basin. Surviving long enough to gather them, however, means contending with the sovereign hunters of the plains—including nesting apex devilsaurs that brook no trespassers in the deep south.

subzone:terror-wing-path.text: Terror Wing Path. Terror Wing Path is a rocky canyon winding through the eastern reaches of the Burning Steppes. Infested by whelps and dragonkin of the black dragonflight, it serves as a perilous approach into the remote northeastern corner of the Steppes. Carved into the craggy, ash-covered foothills of the eastern Burning Steppes, Terror Wing Path earns its name from the aerial predators and wyrmkin that claim it. Broods of the black dragonflight prowl these defiles, fiercely guarding clutches and hunting anything foolish enough to wander into their shadow. Ash and soot blanket the stone trails, making any trek beneath the canyon walls a treacherous venture. Black drakes patrol the length of the valley, and the rare magma giant Volchan is sometimes seen wandering through it. Only the most seasoned adventurers dare the journey, and seldom alone, yet it is the only way to reach the hidden cave of Slither Rock in the far northeastern corner of the Steppes.

subzone:terrordale.text: Terrordale. Terrordale is a ruined, ghost-haunted settlement nestled in the northwestern edge of the Eastern Plaguelands. Bordered by the blighted Plaguewood and the arachnid-infested Terrorweb Tunnel, the ruined town swarms with the Scourge and the restless dead. Once a quiet settlement in northern Lordaeron, Terrordale fell along with the rest of the kingdom to the Scourge. Today, the village stands in grim ruin near the mouth of the Terrorweb Tunnel. Its streets are choked with restless shades and wandering undead, while the surrounding trees of the Plaguewood encroach on its rotten timber. Amidst the desolation, only a handful of eccentric residents dare remain—such as the peculiar merchant Augustus the Touched and the ghost hunter Egan, who attempts to free the tortured spirits caught between worlds. The anguish of Terrordale's demise ran so deep that the physical world literally buckles beneath the torment of the spirit realm. Terrordale spirits linger in perpetual agony, bound to the earth by their tragic ends. Because of this concentrated spiritual corruption, seasoned paladins under the guidance of the Silver Hand and Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker are dispatched here to perform rites of judgment and sacrifice, banishing the torment as a sacred trial of holy discipline.

subzone:terrorweb-tunnel.text: Terrorweb Tunnel. Terrorweb Tunnel is a subterranean passage carving through the mountains between Terrordale and the Thondroril River. Infested with the Scourge's undead nerubian crypt fiends, it forms a hazardous subterranean shortcut across the western border of the Eastern Plaguelands. Bored straight through the mountains flanking the Thondroril River, the Terrorweb Tunnel links the contaminated village of Terrordale with the riverbanks to the south. Rather than typical ghouls or skeletal sentries, this dark subterranean bypass is claimed entirely by crypt fiends—mummified nerubian arachnids raised into servitude by the Lich King. Traveling the length of the passage cuts out long circuits around the mountain slopes, but requires navigating thick webs and avoiding towering nerubian overseers that patrol the dark.

subzone:thalanaar.text: Thalanaar. Thalanaar is a secluded night elf outpost nestled directly on the border between the verdant wilds of Feralas and the arid canyons of Thousand Needles. Serving as the primary eastern gateway into Feralas for the Alliance, it offers tired travelers a vital hippogryph roost and shelter beneath the canopy. Though modest in size, it acts as a critical link between mainland Kalimdor and the remote stronghold of Feathermoon. Perched at the natural choke point where the baked sandstone of Thousand Needles gives way to the dense, misty canopy of Feralas, Thalanaar is the first sign of night elven presence awaiting travelers from the east. It is little more than a fortified grove with a few sturdy pavilions and sentinels on watch, yet its position is vital. The outpost shelters Alliance scouts, couriers, and craftsmen venturing into the untamed forest, providing a secure staging ground against the beasts, ogres, and Horde forces roaming Southern Kalimdor. Because overland travel through southern Kalimdor is fraught with peril, Thalanaar's primary function is logistics. Its hippogryph master links the secluded wilderness of Feralas directly to Theramore Isle in Dustwallow Marsh, Gadgetzan in Tanaris, and the island bastion of Feathermoon Stronghold to the west. Craftsmen also make pilgrimage here to seek out master leatherworkers who teach the ancient art of working wild hides under the woodland boughs.

subzone:thalassian-base-camp.text: Thalassian Base Camp. Tucked onto a high ridge in northern Azshara, the Thalassian Base Camp serves as the staging ground for an expedition of blood elves unearthing ancient arcane relics. Though initially funded under an agreement with the Horde, the camp's leadership quickly broke faith once digging commenced. Now, amidst their red pavilions and pulverized magical artifacts, darker summoning practices hint at their true objectives. The blood elf expedition nestled east of Ursolan was not supposed to be hostile to travelers from Orgrimmar. Their leader, Magus Rimtori, negotiated a formal pact with the Horde: in exchange for supply lines, funding, and armed escort through Azshara's treacherous wildlands, her researchers would share whatever magical riches they uncovered. Instead, as soon as the base camp was fortified and the first relics were pried from the elven ruins, Rimtori reneged entirely, driving away Horde emissaries. While Rimtori searches deeper reaches with an armed retinue, Magister Hawkhelm keeps watch over the ridge, guarding the encampment against retribution.

subzone:thandol-span.text: Thandol Span. The Thandol Span is a pair of colossal dwarven stone bridges connecting the Wetlands of Khaz Modan with the Arathi Highlands of southern Lordaeron. Long celebrated as a marvel of engineering and the vital artery between the northern and southern kingdoms, it is currently in a state of disaster following a sabotage attack by Dark Iron infiltrators. Constructed following the War of the Three Hammers to bridge Ironforge with the Wildhammer clan of the Aerie Peak, the Thandol Span stands among the grandest stonecraft feats of dwarven history. Capable of supporting entire marching armies, it served as the critical land corridor between Lordaeron and Khaz Modan throughout the Second War, notably carrying Sir Anduin Lothar's counter-offensive southward. Today, the crossing is grievously wounded. Dark Iron saboteurs led by Balgaras the Foul and Kam Deepfury mounted a devastating assault from nearby Dun Modr, shattering one span entirely with explosives and threatening to sever overland travel between the allied realms completely. The surviving bridge remains contested and heavily guarded. Mountaineers from Ironforge fight desperately to preserve the remaining roadway and repel Dark Iron sappers, suffering painful losses in the process. The loss of the bridge would leave northern trade and military movements almost entirely reliant on maritime routes, cutting off Alliance forces stationed across the Arathi Highlands from immediate reinforcement.

subzone:thelgen-rock.text: Thelgen Rock. In the southern mountain wall of the Wetlands, Thelgen Rock’s caverns hold volatile Incendicite Ore. Venomous spiders infest the passages. Thelgen Rock cuts deep into the mountains between the Wetlands and Loch Modan. Aggressive spiders fill its web-choked passages, and their venom makes every step dangerous. Miners and adventurers still brave the tunnels for the valuable Incendicite Ore embedded in the rock.

subzone:theramore-isle.text:
Theramore Isle. Theramore Isle shelters refugees from Lordaeron behind the eastern coast of Dustwallow Marsh. Lady Jaina Proudmoore founded the fortified port, now the Alliance's chief stronghold in southern Kalimdor. After the Scourge ravaged Dalaran and Lordaeron in the Third War, Lady Jaina Proudmoore led survivors across the Great Sea to Kalimdor. There, humans, dwarves, and high elves fought beside orcs and night elves to defeat the Burning Legion atop Mount Hyjal.

After the victory, Jaina's coalition withdrew to the misty edge of Dustwallow Marsh. On an island just off the coast, they raised a harbor city with stone ramparts and Jaina's citadel, sheltering what remained of the northern kingdoms.

subzone:thistleshrub-valley.text: Thistleshrub Valley. Tucked away in the southwestern reaches of Tanaris, Thistleshrub Valley is a bizarre oasis of prickly plant life amidst endless dunes. The canyon is known for its strange grove of giant cacti and hostile animated thistleshrubs that attack anything stepping through their thorn-choked territory. While most of Tanaris is an arid wasteland stripped bare of vegetation, Thistleshrub Valley is curiously choked with life. Giant blooming cacti tower over the canyon floor, providing a sharp contrast to the surrounding sea of sand. However, this is no peaceful sanctuary. The valley takes its name from the hostile, living plant creatures that lurk among the brush. These thistleshrubs lash out with razor-sharp spines at any traveler who wanders near, making navigation hazardous for those trying to push past the cliffs toward the mysterious southern gates. The presence of animated flora in such a dry climate has long puzzled wanderers and desert survivalists. Whether awakened by forgotten elemental energies or stubborn adaptation to the harsh Tanaris climate, the thistleshrubs remain violently territorial. Travelers journeying through the canyon must contend not only with these thrashing thickets of thorn and root, but also the desert predators and venomous serpents that nest among the towering cacti.

subzone:thondroril-river.text: Thondroril River. The Thondroril River is a vital natural boundary separating the Western and Eastern Plaguelands. Originating in the mountains of Northern Lordaeron near the Terrorweb Tunnel, its blighted waters flow southward into Darrowmere Lake. Once a vibrant trade and travel waterway of the fallen kingdom, it is now flanked by monstrous Scourge beasts and the humble refuge of a legendary hermit. Before the fall of Lordaeron, the Thondroril served as an important waterway connecting northern holdings toward Stratholme and south to Darrowmere Lake. Today, the river marks the hazardous divide between the Western and Eastern Plaguelands. The waters carry the taint of the plague, and its banks are infested with giant maggots, plaguebats, diseased bears, and predatory snapjaws, turning what was once a scenic riverbed into a deadly crossing for travelers.

subzone:thoradin-s-wall.text: Thoradin's Wall. Thoradin's Wall is a monumental, crumbling stone rampart dividing the Arathi Highlands from the Hillsbrad Foothills. Commissioned millennia ago by King Thoradin during the dawn of the Empire of Arathor, it was built to shield early humanity from the fierce incursions of the Amani trolls. Erected nearly three thousand years ago, Thoradin's Wall marks the western frontier of ancient Strom, the heart of the first unified human empire. King Thoradin recognized that humanity's fledgeling settlements were acutely vulnerable to the predatory raids of the Amani forest trolls. By raising this vast stone barrier across the valley corridor, Arathor secured its heartland and forged a defensible bastion from which humanity could survive and eventually contest troll supremacy in the north. Today, the ancient barrier stands in severe disrepair. Vast breeches gash the stone ramparts, their battlements weathered down by thousands of years of exposure, warfare, and abandonment. Following the splintering of Arathor into rival kingdoms and the eventual fall of neighboring Lordaeron to the Scourge, no central realm maintains the masonry. Now, travelers and roaming bandits slip freely through its broken archways as they journey between Hillsbrad and the untamed Arathi Highlands.

subzone:thorium-point.text: Thorium Point. Perched upon the northern bluffs of the Searing Gorge, Thorium Point serves as the primary staging camp for the Thorium Brotherhood. From this neutral outpost, these rogue Dark Iron dwarves recruit passing adventurers and strike back against their tyrannical kin deeper within the volcanic wastes. Overlooking the scorched slag heaps of the Searing Gorge, Thorium Point is a modest mountain encampment built out of necessity. It is held by the Thorium Brotherhood, a renegade faction of Dark Iron dwarves who have severed ties with their enslaved brethren in Shadowforge City. Unwilling to bow to the Firelord or Emperor Dagran Thaurissan, these outcasts maintain an open-air forge, a busy flight master, and a well-guarded perimeter northeast of Firewatch Ridge. Because of their desperate struggle for survival and master-level smithing aspirations, the Brotherhood keeps the camp open to both the Alliance and the Horde, welcoming anyone willing to dig ores out of the ash or bash Dark Iron skulls. Beyond being a staging ground for the Brotherhood's war against their brethren, Thorium Point is an indispensable crossroads in the heart of the Redridge mountain chain. Perched safely above the ravenous spiders and fire elementals that prowl the volcanic basin, the outpost offers direct flight links to Ironforge, as well as forward camps across the Badlands and the Burning Steppes. For wandering mercenaries, prospectors, and crafters looking to earn the secretive favor of master dwarf smiths, this smoky cliffside is the safest hearth to be found in the Gorge.

subzone:thunder-axe-fortress.text: Thunder Axe Fortress. Thunder Axe Fortress is a fortified compound in northwestern Desolace serving as a stronghold for the demonic Burning Blade cult. Within its stone barracks, watchtowers, and darkened caves, cultists perform dark rituals to summon demonic entities and store stolen artifacts of power. The cult remains an active threat to anyone traversing the desolate wastes. Perched in northwestern Desolace, Thunder Axe Fortress serves as a heavily guarded redoubt for the Burning Blade. Composed of stone barracks, defensive watchtowers, and deep caverns, it allows the cult to maintain a fortified foothold far from the gaze of Kalimdor's major cities. Here, the cultists gather fel energies, summon lesser demons, and concoct schemes to bring far more dangerous entities into the world.

subzone:thunder-bluff.text: Thunder Bluff. On Mulgore’s high mesas, Thunder Bluff shelters the tauren as their capital. Cairne Bloodhoof founded the city after the Third War, bringing a people long scattered across Kalimdor together in a place of refuge and tradition. Thunder Bluff rises above Mulgore, where rope bridges link its stone mesas and wooden elevators carry travelers up from the plains. For generations, the tauren wandered across central Kalimdor, pursued by centaur raiding parties. During the Third War, Cairne Bloodhoof joined with Warchief Thrall and the New Horde. Together, they drove back the centaurs and claimed Mulgore’s fertile grasslands. Cairne gathered the scattered tribes and founded the city atop the mesas, where the heights offered shelter and a place for the tauren to trade and gather in worship. Cairne Bloodhoof’s followers share Thunder Bluff with tauren who hold to other ways. Magatha Grimtotem and her kin dwell on the Elder Rise, while spirit walkers and shaman seek the ancestors’ will at the Pools of Vision beneath the city. Tribal rivalries persist, yet Thunder Bluff remains a spiritual pillar of Kalimdor’s Horde. Hunters return from the Barrens, artisans travel through, and druids come to commune with the Earth Mother.

subzone:tidefury-cove.text: Tidefury Cove. Tidefury Cove is a treacherous stretch of water and rocky shallows along the southeastern coast of Dustwallow Marsh, south of Theramore Isle. Renowned for its hazardous reefs and wrecked vessels, it serves as a secluded haven for roaming makrura and solitary anglers. Tucked away at the far end of Dustwallow Bay between Theramore Isle and the Wyrmbog, Tidefury Cove presents a notorious navigational hazard to passing sailors. Jagged reefs and shifting shoals have claimed multiple vessels over the years, leaving rotting wooden hulks half-submerged in the tideline. Today, the ruined ships are crawled over by opportunistic makrura, turning the cove into a dangerous, isolated stretch of coastline visited mostly by hardy scavengers or quiet hermits seeking distance from Theramore's busy docks. During the invasion of Durotar, the shores of Tidefury Cove became a crucial strategic battleground. Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's Kul Tiran expedition fortified the coast with an imposing coastal fortress and guard towers to command the approaches to Theramore. To break Proudmoore's grip, Thrall marshaled the combined strength of the young Horde—uniting orcs, Darkspear trolls, and tauren alongside Rexxar and the Stonemaul ogres—to storm the shoreline and dismantle the Kul Tiran beachhead before pressing directly toward the island fortress.

subzone:timbermaw-hold.text: Timbermaw Hold. Timbermaw Hold is a fortified subterranean network of tunnels that links Felwood, Moonglade, and Winterspring. It serves as the stronghold for the Timbermaw furbolgs, one of the last tribes to resist the demonic corruption plaguing northern Kalimdor. Carved deep into the mountain roots between Felwood, Moonglade, and Winterspring, Timbermaw Hold stands as a desperately guarded bastion. While neighboring furbolg tribes fell to the foul taint of the Burning Legion during the Third War, the Timbermaw clan weathered the nightmare within these stone corridors. Though safe beneath the earth, they were forced to watch their beloved forests warp into corrupted mockeries. Extremely protective and deeply suspicious of outsiders, the furbolgs guard every tunnel entrance fiercely, expecting violence from anyone wandering in from the infected woods. Beyond its role as a tribal sanctuary, Timbermaw Hold is the only direct mountain highway connecting the tainted lowlands of Felwood, the sacred sanctuary of Moonglade, and the frozen expanse of Winterspring. Outsiders who wish to pass through without being torn apart by tribal sentries must prove their goodwill. Those who demonstrate their opposition to the region's corrupted furbolg clans find the Timbermaw to be steadfast allies willing to share their ancient shamanic knowledge and leathercrafting traditions.

subzone:timbermaw-post.text: Timbermaw Post. Timbermaw Post is a small furbolg camp situated in the snowy expanse of Winterspring, nestled between Frostfire Hot Springs and Lake Kel'Theril. Despite bearing the name of the uncorrupted Timbermaw tribe, the encampment has fallen under the aggressive grip of the corrupted Winterfall furbolgs. Positioned just southeast across the road from Frostfire Hot Springs and west of the frozen Lake Kel'Theril, Timbermaw Post stands as a bitter reminder of the furbolgs' internal strife in Winterspring. Despite its Timbermaw name, travelers approaching the camp will find no friendly welcomes. The outpost is controlled by the hostile Winterfall tribe, driven mad and violent by demonic corruption. Now crowded with savage Winterfall furbolgs, the camp serves as an aggressive staging ground encroaching upon the central road.

subzone:tkashi-ruins.text: Tkashi Ruins. The Tkashi Ruins are ancient stone remnants situated southwest of Nesingwary's Expedition in northern Stranglethorn Vale. Overrun by hostile Bloodscalp trolls, the site remains a stronghold of the tribe. Perched southwest of Hemet Nesingwary's hunting camp, the crumbling stone masonry of the Tkashi Ruins marks the ancient domain of Stranglethorn's jungle trolls. Today, the encampment is heavily occupied by the Bloodscalp tribe, who aggressively defend the territory and practice their shamanistic rituals among the vines and decayed stone. While Hemet Nesingwary noted passing through the ruins without trouble in his hunting memoirs, modern travelers find the trolls far less accommodating, guarding valuable tribal relics buried among the rubble.

subzone:tower-of-arathor.text: Tower of Arathor. The Tower of Arathor is a ruined wizard's tower situated in the former mage district in the southwestern reaches of Stromgarde Keep. Once the workshop of Archmage Trelane, it was overrun during the fall of the city and is currently occupied by Boulderfist ogres. Erected in the heart of Stromgarde Keep's mage district and named after the ancient Empire of Arathor, this spire long served the realm's sorcerers. Its most notable resident, Archmage Trelane, devised a magical defensive grid keyed to enchanted gemstones to protect the sanctum. However, when the Syndicate and the Boulderfist ogre clan assaulted Stromgarde following the Third War, the kingdom fractured. Despite Trelane's desperate attempts to hold the tower using his arcane wards, the sheer brutish force of the ogres overwhelmed him. Forced to flee the city for his life, the archmage left behind his most prized arcane artifacts, leaving the spire in the hands of the Boulderfist brute Ruul Onestone and his followers.

subzone:tower-of-eldara.text: Tower of Eldara. The Tower of Eldara is an ancient, sealed night elven spire situated on the far northeastern promontory overlooking the Bay of Storms in Azshara. Though long abandoned, its sturdy stone architecture has survived the Sundering, standing silent above coasts roamed by aggressive coastal beasts. Perched on a remote cliff edge northeast of the Bay of Storms, the Tower of Eldara stands as a lonely testament to the vast kaldorei empire that once dominated this coastline. Like much of Azshara's ruined architecture, it fell into disuse following the Great Sundering thousands of years ago. Today, the entrance remains firmly closed and barred against the outside world, giving no hint of whatever relics or chambers lie sealed inside. The surrounding shores are fraught with danger, prowled constantly by wandering murlocs, clawing makrura, and predatory hydras that keep all but the most daring travelers away.

subzone:twilight-base-camp.text: Twilight Base Camp. The Twilight Base Camp is a fortified outpost of the Twilight's Hammer cult situated in the arid wastes of Silithus. It serves as an active ritual site where cultists convene to commune with elemental powers and orchestrate their apocalyptic agenda. The camp is characterized by strange wind stones and heavily armed cult zealots. Perched among the desolate sands of Silithus, the Twilight Base Camp is one of several enclaves established by the Twilight's Hammer cult. The outpost brims with zealots, geomancers, and stonecallers dedicated to summoning devastating elemental forces. Surrounded by jagged ritual stones, the camp acts as a staging ground where leaders like Twilight Keeper Havunth and Twilight Lord Everun direct efforts to hasten Azeroth's end, standing in open defiance of the Cenarion Hold forces attempting to restore balance to the region. Scattered throughout the outpost are mysterious monuments known as wind stones, ranging in power from lesser conduits to greater monoliths. Through cryptic incantations and cult regalia, the Twilight's Hammer uses these focal points to pull chaotic elemental spirits directly into the physical realm. Disrupting these rituals remains a top priority for travelers and scouts hoping to prevent the cult's influence from spreading across Kalimdor.

subzone:twilight-outpost.text: Twilight Outpost. The Twilight Outpost is a fortified encampment of the Twilight's Hammer cult nestled in the southwestern sands of Silithus. Located just northwest of the ancient Scarab Wall, it serves as a staging ground where cultists conduct dark rituals to commune with and summon elemental horrors. Tucked away in the southwestern reaches of Silithus, the Twilight Outpost serves as one of several major cultist strongholds dotting the desert wastes. Positioned in the shadow of the colossal Scarab Wall and west of the Bronzebeard Encampment, the outpost teems with fanatical Twilight Avengers, Geolords, and Stonecallers. Under the command of leaders like Twilight Keeper Exeter and the rare Twilight Lord Everun, these zealots toil tirelessly in service of their maddening apocalyptic masters. Scattered throughout the encampment are mysterious Wind Stones, varying in size from Lesser to Greater conduits. Through the use of enchanted cultist regalia and foul incantations, the cult utilizes these monoliths to tear into the elemental planes, dragging forth Abyssal commanders and elemental lords. For adventurers brave enough to infiltrate their ranks, disrupting these summonings remains one of the primary means to strike back against the cult's influence in the desert.

subzone:twilight-post.text: Twilight Post. Twilight Post is a fortified encampment established by the Twilight's Hammer cult in northwestern Silithus. Situated far west of Cenarion Hold and northwest of the Twilight Base Camp, it serves as a critical site for the cultists' elemental summoning rituals. Adventurers venturing here face zealous cultists and the wind stones they use to contact otherworldly forces. Tucked away in the desert sands of northwestern Silithus, Twilight Post serves as an outpost for the Twilight's Hammer cult. The camp is populated by heavily armed defenders and ritualists, including Twilight Avengers, Geolords, and Stonecallers under the leadership of Twilight Keeper Mayna and the rare fanatic Twilight Lord Everun. Like other encampments scattered across the wastes, the post revolves around ancient summoning conduits—Lesser, regular, and Greater Wind Stones. Through dark rites and elemental communion, the cultists utilize these stones to entreat and bind elemental horrors from the realms beyond, threatening the fragile peace maintained by the Cenarion Circle in the region.

subzone:twilight-s-run.text: Twilight's Run. Twilight's Run is a secluded subterranean cavern carved into the northern mountains of Silithus beneath Staghelm Point. Occupied by the fanatical Twilight's Hammer cult, it serves as a secluded sanctuary and ritual redoubt away from the harsh desert winds. Tucked away in the northern cliffside below Staghelm Point, Twilight's Run provides the Twilight's Hammer cultists with a natural bastion amidst the windswept hazards of Silithus. Rather than weathering the dust storms or contending directly with roaming silithid hives across the surface dunes, cultists retreat into these shadowy tunnels to commune with dark forces, guard ritual materials, and marshal their forces. Under the direction of overseers such as Vyral the Vile, cult members within the cave maintain a vigilant, hostile presence, ready to strike down any curious travelers or scouts who draw too close to their subterranean encampment.

subzone:twin-colossals.text: Twin Colossals. The Twin Colossals are a pair of towering, sheer-faced mesas that dominate the northwestern skyline of Feralas. Rising high above the canopy, the narrow passage between their sheer cliffs forms the primary overland route connecting Feralas with the arid wastes of Desolace to the north. Towering over the western reaches of Feralas, the Twin Colossals stand as the highest landforms in the region. Their vertical rock faces cut a striking silhouette against the sky, serving as unmistakable landmarks for travelers venturing south out of Desolace. While the lower slopes merge into the dense jungle and the lands stretching toward the Forgotten Coast, the summits are isolated plateaus far above the forest floor. Scaling the vertical cliffs on foot is impossible, yet the summits are not entirely deserted. An intrepid night elf named Marli Wishrunner assists travelers seeking passage to the eastern peak. Those who ascend find a tranquil pond perched atop the stone mesa—though it is inhabited by an unusually large makrura named Diamond Head. To aid adventurers in returning to earth, Kalin Windflight offers sturdy parachutes to descend back into the jungle canopy below.

subzone:tyr-s-hand.text: Tyr's Hand. Tyr's Hand is a heavily fortified human stronghold situated in the southeastern hills of the Eastern Plaguelands. Long revered as an ancient holy site for the Church of the Holy Light, the city now serves as the primary regional bastion and supply hub for the zealous Scarlet Crusade. Perched defensively in what was once Lordaeron's green Eastweald, Tyr's Hand is one of humanity's most ancient sacred sites. The settlement became known as a 'city of churches' as shrines and holy structures were raised across its grounds. Unlike the blight-rotted ruins that litter the rest of the Plaguelands, Tyr's Hand remains remarkably preserved behind formidable masonry, thick walls, and the towering silhouette of the Scarlet Basilica. When the Scourge swept through Lordaeron during the Third War, Lord Valdelmar kept the city standing through sheer military vigilance and faith. After the Knights of the Silver Hand shattered into rival factions, Tyr's Hand aligned firmly with the Crimson dawn of the Scarlet Crusade. Today, it operates as an impenetrable base of operations led by High General Brigitte Abbendis and Valdelmar. Elite crusaders train within its abbey, heavily guarded couriers maintain communication with scarlet forces holding Stratholme, and the city ruthlessly rebuffs all outsiders who approach its gates.

subzone:tyr-s-hand-abbey.text: Tyr's Hand Abbey. Tyr's Hand Abbey is a well-maintained sanctuary nestled within the fortified bastion of Tyr's Hand in the southeastern Eastern Plaguelands. Controlled by the zealots of the Scarlet Crusade, it serves as an auxiliary house of worship and study alongside the grand Scarlet Basilica. While the imposing Scarlet Basilica dominates the skyline of Tyr's Hand, the abbey provides a quieter, functional center of devotion and martial doctrine for the Scarlet Crusade. Its architecture closely mirrors traditional Holy Light foundations such as Northshire Abbey in Elwynn Forest, featuring a central Main Hall flanked by a Hall of Arms and a dedicated Library Wing. Despite the relentless horrors of the Plaguelands, the Crusade maintains the abbey with meticulous care, fiercely defending its cloisters from all outsiders.

subzone:uldaman.text: Uldaman. Carved deep beneath the northern mountains of the Badlands, Uldaman is an ancient titan vault dating back to the ordering of the world. Recently unsealed by dwarven excavators, its halls contain the buried origins of the dwarven race alongside savage troggs and vigilant stone sentinels. Uldaman was constructed by titan watchers as a subterranean redoubt and research facility. When early experiments in shaping living stone produced the misshapen troggs, the titans sealed their failed creations within the vault's stasis chambers and began anew, culminating in the stone-skinned earthen. Its deepest chambers came to hold vital archives, including the fabled Discs of Norgannon, guarded by the stonekeeper Archaedas and the giantess Ironaya. Dwarven legend holds that in time the stone-skinned earthen gave rise to the dwarven race, and that their cradle lay buried and forgotten beneath the hills.

subzone:uldum.text: Uldum. Uldum is a massive, sealed Titan research installation tucked behind colossal stone gates in the southernmost cliffs of Tanaris. Long hidden away behind ancient wards and forgotten machinery, it remains inaccessible to modern explorers. Carved into the rugged southern mountain range bordering the Tanaris desert, the monumental gateway to Uldum stands silent and impassable. Built during the ordering of ancient Kalimdor, the compound served as an advanced Titan facility tied to their mysterious efforts to shape and oversee the planet's biosphere. Titanic wardens and defensive constructs once maintained the perimeter, leaving modern mortals only monumental stone carved arches and buried secrets that have defied all mundane attempts at entry. The site's unmistakable Titan craftsmanship draws the curiosity of dwarven scholars, yet no mechanism or key has been found that might unlock the ancient complex. Legend claims that true insight into the secrets locked within requires the lost Plates of Uldum, leaving the dwarven scholars peering through the keyhole of an empire they cannot yet breach.

subzone:undercity.text: Undercity. Beneath Capital City, the Forsaken hold their underground stronghold, ruled by Sylvanas Windrunner. Its halls began as Scourge work and now shelter the free-willed undead. Before the Third War, sewers, royal catacombs, and dungeons lay beneath Capital City. As Lordaeron fell, Prince Arthas Menethil ordered the Scourge to enlarge them into an underground seat of power. The Lich King summoned Arthas to Northrend before the work was finished. During the civil war in the Plaguelands, Sylvanas Windrunner rallied undead who had escaped the Lich King's grip. She overthrew the dreadlords and drove out rival forces, and the Forsaken claimed the underground complex. They finished the maze of catacombs the Scourge had begun and fortified it beneath the silent ruins of their former kingdom. Now the Dark Lady rules her people from its poisoned halls.

subzone:undercroft.text: Undercroft. The Undercroft is an ancient burial crypt nestled in the southwestern hills of the Eastern Plaguelands. Once a dignified tomb of Lordaeron, it has been desecrated by a band of undead trolls under the command of Zaeldarr the Outcast. Amid the defiled catacombs lies an ersatz grave dug long ago to feign the death of the exiled paladin Tirion Fordring. Carved into the rugged bluffs southwest of Corin's Crossing, the Undercroft was originally built as a final resting place for the honored dead of Lordaeron. The fall of the kingdom stripped away its sanctity, and the tomb is now infested by a band of savage undead trolls. Led by the hulking monstrosity Zaeldarr the Outcast, these ghoulish marauders use the underground halls as a redoubt from which to stalk the Plaguelands, even daring to raid the grave pits of Light's Hope Chapel to gather raw corpses for their sinister practices.

subzone:uplands.text: Uplands. The Uplands is a rolling, elevated territory in the northeastern Alterac Mountains that once served as the agricultural heartland of the fallen Kingdom of Alterac. Following the kingdom's collapse, the fertile hills fell entirely under the sway of the Syndicate. Today, the criminal organization maintains its strongest base of power here, fortifying multiple encampments across the slopes. Before the Second War broke Alterac apart, the hills of the Uplands were celebrated as the kingdom's breadbasket, providing grain and livestock to feed its mountain fortresses. When the core of the realm fell to ruin and infamy, the farming estates were abandoned by honest folk. In their place rose the Syndicate, led by dispossessed Alterac nobles and cutthroats determined to reclaim their stolen inheritance through force. The Uplands now represents the Syndicate's most heavily concentrated territory in the region, dotted with camps, patrols, and outposts like Dandred's Fold along its western borders. Because the Syndicate commands these hills in force, high-ranking conspirators often oversee operations from the Uplands. Figures such as Baron Vardus, aligned with the shadowy leadership steering the remnants of Alterac's nobility, coordinate brigand movements, raids on neighboring valleys, and resistance against both the Alliance and Horde. Travelers crossing into the northeastern ridges face immediate hostility from entrenched highwaymen who view the entire range as their sovereign soil.

subzone:ursolan.text: Ursolan. Ursolan is a sprawling Timbermaw furbolg settlement situated in western Azshara, just east of Timbermaw Hold. Bisected by a deep ravine, the encampment honors the bear Ancient Ursol and serves as a vital stronghold for uncorrupted furbolgs defending their territory from outside incursions. Perched on the rugged bluffs of western Azshara, Ursolan constitutes the eastern branch of the Timbermaw tribe's domain, connecting directly through Timbermaw Hold to Bear's Head in the south. Named after the revered bear Ancient Ursol, this camp represents a rare haven of sanity among Kalimdor's furbolg populations, which have largely fallen victim to demonic corruption. The village spans both rims of a dramatic earthen chasm, where the Timbermaw vigilantly guard their borders against encroaching interlopers, including intrusive researchers from the night elven camp of Talrendis.

subzone:uther-s-tomb.text: Uther's Tomb. Uther's Tomb is the sacred resting place of Uther the Lightbringer, situated atop Sorrow Hill in the Western Plaguelands. Constructed by his surviving followers after his defeat at nearby Andorhal, this monument stands as one of the few remaining bastions of the Holy Light amidst a blighted and haunted region. Perched south of the ruins of Andorhal at Sorrow Hill, Uther's Tomb marks the final resting place of the legendary paladin who founded the Knights of the Silver Hand. Following the collapse of Lordaeron, Uther made his last stand in Andorhal, defending the royal urn holding the ashes of King Terenas Menethil II against Prince Arthas Menethil and the Scourge. Arthas struck down his former mentor and desecrated the urn to carry Kel'Thuzad's remains. Surviving soldiers salvaged Uther's body, laying him to rest within a stone sanctuary. Despite the relentless corruption engulfing the surrounding lands, the tomb remains miraculously untouched by decay, held under the steadfast vigil of High Priest Thel'danis. Approached via the Path of Uther, the monument centers on a grand stone effigy depicting the paladin with a tome of the Holy Light in one hand and his warhammer in the other. Pilgrims who travel these treacherous roads frequently seek out the tomb to pay homage, pray, or reflect upon the devotion that defined the first paladins.

subzone:valley-of-bones.text: Valley of Bones. The Valley of Bones is a desolate canyon along the crags of Shen'dralas, choked with dust, ancient remains, and restless undead. Haunted by the lingering spirits of the Magram centaur clan and patrolled by dark necromancers, it is dominated by the colossal rib cages of mysterious ancient beasts known as the Dead Goliaths. Tucked away in the southern reaches of the region, the Valley of Bones lives up to its grim name. Skeletal horrors walk the dusty ravines, raised and bound by centaur necromancers who draw upon dark sorceries. The spirits of deceased Magram centaur wander the wastes alongside them, bound to this barren earth long after their violent deaths. Adding to the canyon's ominous nature are the Dead Goliaths—two immense skeletons slumped against the rocky cliffs whose true origin remains a total mystery to scholars and wanderers alike.

subzone:valley-of-fangs.text: Valley of Fangs. The Valley of Fangs is a rugged, narrow pass carved between towering rock pillars in the central Badlands. Known for the vicious predators that prowl its dusty floor, it also shelters a small, isolated encampment of wandering tinkerers and exiles. Situated between two imposing stone formations in the heart of the Badlands, the Valley of Fangs earns its name from both the sharp silhouettes of its surrounding cliffs and the dangerous beasts roaming its floor. Feral crag coyotes, prowling cougars, and vicious wolves stalk the dusty corridor, making transit hazardous for lone travelers. Despite the hostile wildlife, a handful of wayward figures—including the banished orc Martek the Exiled and his goblin associates Rigglefuzz and Jazzrik—have pitched an informal camp here, tinkering away in seclusion far from the regional outposts.

subzone:valley-of-spears.text: Valley of Spears. The Valley of Spears is a rugged canyon nestled in western Desolace, serving as the stronghold of the Maraudine centaur clan. Enclosed by steep cliffs and guarded passes, the valley leads directly to Maraudon, the sacred ancestral burial ground of all centaurkind. Carved into the rugged heights of western Desolace, the Valley of Spears is a stronghold of the Maraudine clan. Accessible on foot only through narrow, easily defended mountain passes from the south and east, this enclosed valley provides the centaur with a natural bastion. Travelers who venture past the rocky chokepoints face dense encampments of hostile nomads guarding the approach to their most revered holy site. Tucked away at the southwestern end of the valley lies the entrance to Maraudon, the sacred cavern housing the tomb of Zaetar, father of the centaur, where Princess Theradras dwells. Because of this proximity, the Maraudine defend the canyon with zealous fury against rival clans and outside interlopers alike. Anyone foolish enough to stumble into the valley unawares—such as careless gnome cartographers or scouts—frequently ends up captured or slain.

subzone:valley-of-the-watchers.text: Valley of the Watchers. Tucked away in the far southern reaches of the Tanaris desert, the Valley of the Watchers is a sun-scorched canyon defined by monumental stonework. At its end stands a colossal, sealed stone gate leading into the mysterious complex of Uldum, guarded by lumbering giants and ancient stone sentinels. The Valley of the Watchers marks the southern boundary where the shifting sands of Tanaris meet the mountainous edge of the continent. Dominating the canyon is a massive gate crafted from ancient stone, locked tight against the outside world. This sealed portal is believed to guard the entrance to Uldum, a subterranean facility of the enigmatic Titans. Massive Dune Smasher mountain giants roam the dusty approach, ensuring that whatever secrets lie buried beneath the sands remain undisturbed by travelers, tomb robbers, and scholars alike.

subzone:valor-s-rest.text: Valor's Rest. Valor's Rest is a small outpost and cemetery perched at the eastern threshold of Silithus. Guarded by members of the Cenarion Circle, it is the first point of shelter seen by travelers emerging from Un'Goro Crater into the windswept wastes. Perched on the eastern border of Silithus along the ramp leading down from Un'Goro Crater, Valor's Rest serves as the threshold into this desolate frontier. Maintained as a neutral staging ground by the Cenarion Circle, the camp hosts members of both the Alliance and the Horde who dare to brave the arid wastes. Its prominent graveyard stands as a somber reminder of the danger lurking throughout the desert, where insectoid horrors and ancient threats test even the hardiest expeditions.

subzone:valormok.text: Valormok. Valormok keeps a Horde foothold in northwest Azshara. North of the Haldarr Encampment, the outpost sends scouts and travelers toward the cursed ancient ruins along the coast. Autumn-colored trees ring Valormok, where the Horde holds a foothold in a hostile and largely forsaken land. Nearby satyrs, nagas, and prowling beasts threaten the lightly fortified camp. Its warriors hold their ground despite the danger. Wind riders connect Valormok with Orgrimmar and the wilder reaches of northern Kalimdor.

subzone:venture-co-base-camp.text: Venture Co. Base Camp. Tucked away in the dense jungles of northern Stranglethorn Vale, the Venture Co. Base Camp serves as a forward foothold for the notoriously greedy goblin syndicate. Here, hired overseers and laborers exploit the lush wilderness, focusing their efforts on harvesting timber, hunting local wildlife, and extracting valuable tumbled crystals from the nearby waterways. The Venture Company is infamous across Azeroth for ruthless profiteering and complete disregard for the natural world. At this jungle base camp, steam-powered equipment and makeshift goblin shacks chew into the ancient canopy. Guarded by armed mercenaries, foremen, and field workers, the camp coordinates resource extraction throughout the surrounding valleys, paying particular interest to valuable tumbled crystals found nearby while clear-cutting any jungle that stands in their way.

subzone:vice.text: Vice. The Vice is a rugged, desolate expanse of Deadwind Pass situated along the road leading toward Karazhan. It serves as the territory of the Deadwind ogres, who maintain rough mounds and scattered camps in defiance of the land's grim isolation. Travelers passing through must navigate both their crude brutality and their surprisingly adept wielders of dark magic.
