Stretching across the southern stretches of Deadwind Pass, the Vice is defined by barren earth, jagged rock faces, and crude mounds erected by the Deadwind ogre clan. While the surrounding canyon is largely abandoned to vengeful ghosts and scavenger vultures, these ogres have carved out a stubborn foothold directly beside the main path approaching Karazhan. Why they chose such a bleak and magically scarred waste remains an enduring mystery, but any traveler passing between Duskwood and the Swamp of Sorrows quickly learns they defend their camps with fierce territorial violence. Unlike mere highwaymen, the ogres dwelling in the Vice possess both heavy martial strength and dangerous arcane talent. Alongside hulking bruisers, Deadwind warlocks practice crude yet lethal fel sorceries among the earthen mounds. Their presence so close to the abandoned seat of Medivh suggests a hunger for residual magical power, making the canyon a lethal gauntlet for wandering scholars and solitary scouts alike.

subzone:vile-reef.text: Vile Reef. The Vile Reef is a submerged, vibrant coral shelf lying off the western coast of Stranglethorn Vale near Grom'gol Base Camp. Beneath its waters, aggressive murlocs make their home among ancient sunken troll ruins, giant clams, and coastal shipwrecks. Stretching beneath the waves of the Great Sea just offshore from Grom'gol Base Camp, the Vile Reef is known for its vivid marine growth and perilous inhabitants. The seabed is dotted with the weathered stonework of submerged troll ruins alongside the enigmatic Altar of the Tides. Flocks of territorial murlocs lurk among the coral shelves and shattered timbers of passing vessels, fiercely defending the shallow waters and preying upon any diver who braves the deep in search of giant clams and rare blue pearls.

subzone:wailing-caverns.text: Wailing Caverns. Steam wails through the bluffs above Lushwater Oasis, where the Wailing Caverns twist beneath the Barrens. Naralex, a night elf druid, entered the springs hoping to restore life to the arid plains, but mutations and agitated wildlife now haunt the caverns.

subzone:warpwood-quarter.text: Warpwood Quarter. The Warpwood Quarter encompasses the eastern district of the ruined Highborne city of Eldre'Thalas, now known as Dire Maul. Once a center of elven nature cultivation and lush gardens, it has devolved into a warped, demon-tainted ruin overrun by frenzied flora and corrupted satyrs. Formerly known for its grand botanical marvels, the Warpwood Quarter has become a choking forest of twisted ancients and lethal lashers. The district fell under the sway of Alzzin the Wildshaper, a satyr who bent his dark magic toward defiling the ancient Fruit of Fertility. Under his malign influence, the plant life grew grotesque and predatory, saturating the halls with vile Felvine shards and drawing demons, rebellious imps, and demonic thralls into the ruined halls. While explorers typically enter the district through the central Broken Commons of Dire Maul, an overgrown subterranean backdoor lies hidden beneath the Lariss Pavilion to the east. Navigating the district requires contending not only with Alzzin's warped guardians, but also with elusive denizens such as the mischievous imp Pusillin, whose thievery leads pursuers on dangerous chases toward the secluded reaches of the ruins.

subzone:waterspring-field.text: Waterspring Field. Waterspring Field is a vital water-pumping operation in northern Tanaris, constructed by the goblins of Gadgetzan to tap underground aquifers. Instead of supplying the boomtown, the field has been overtaken by the ruthless Wastewander bandits, who now hoard the desert's most precious resource. In the searing wastes of Tanaris, nothing carries more value than fresh water. Seeking to support their expanding trade hub, the Steamwheedle Cartel goblins of Gadgetzan erected an array of industrial pumping towers across Waterspring Field to draw from underground reserves. Their plans collapsed when the Wastewanders—a sprawling band of human outlaws and desert marauders—seized the entire field. The bandits now guard the hijacked pumps with their lives, forcing Gadgetzan to look for hired blades willing to reclaim the moisture.

subzone:wavestrider-beach.text: Wavestrider Beach. Wavestrider Beach is the sun-scorched coastal strip lining the eastern edge of Tanaris. Stretching between Steamwheedle Port and the pirate stronghold at Lost Rigger Cove, its sands are inhabited by aggressive crustacean wildlife and overlook distant naval skirmishes out at sea. Running along the ocean border of eastern Tanaris, Wavestrider Beach connects the goblin settlement of Steamwheedle Port in the north to the cliffs guarding Lost Rigger Cove to the south. Rather than a gentle resort, the shoreline is plagued by vicious Steeljaw Snappers and Desert Crawlers scuttling across the baking sand. Out in the deep water just offshore, burning vessels remain locked in a perpetual naval clash, serving as a grim warning of the piratical violence that dominates these coastal waters.

subzone:weazel-s-crater.text: Weazel's Crater. Weazel's Crater is a deep gouge carved into the hard salt of the northern Shimmering Flats. Its origins are mysterious, and Saltstone basilisks inhabit the hollow. Across the blinding white expanse of the Shimmering Flats, experimental goblin and gnome rocket-cars constantly push the boundaries of mechanical sanity. Debris, scorched earth, and impact hollows litter the plains, but Weazel's Crater stands out for its sheer size and depth. The crater's origins are unknown. Today, the mechanical wreckage has largely settled, and the hollow has been claimed as a sunning pit by aggressive Saltstone basilisks.

subzone:weeping-cave.text: Weeping Cave. The Weeping Cave is a foul, subterranean cavern tucked into the hills of the northeastern Western Plaguelands, just west of the Thondroril River. Once a natural cave system, it now seeps with toxic blight and festers with grotesque fungal beasts and oozes. Carved into the rugged bluffs above the Thondroril River, the Weeping Cave earned its name from the continual trickling of moisture through its rocky ceiling—water that has long since turned rank and corrupt. The Scourge's plague has thoroughly permeated the soil above, draining virulent filth down into the dark. Within, rotting horrors, decaying behemoths, and caustic oozes wander the damp tunnels, accompanied by an enigmatic corrupted elemental entity known simply as The Husk.

subzone:whispering-gardens.text: Whispering Gardens. The Whispering Gardens occupy the terraced hillside just south of the Scarlet Monastery in northeastern Tirisfal Glades. Once a place of quiet contemplation, it became the site of a savage clash between early crusade defenders and a massive host of the Scourge. Today, crusaders patrol its overgrown pathways while the faint voices of the fallen linger in the air. Before the Scarlet Crusade fully retreated behind the fortress walls of the Monastery, a fierce battle erupted across these terraced slopes against an encroaching army of undead. The clash claimed countless lives on both sides. In the twilight, travelers through the gardens report hearing strange, soft murmurings on the wind—believed to be the restless echoes of the soldiers and priests who perished defending the holy grounds. Despite the haunting presence, the Scarlet Crusade maintains an active watch over the gardens. Scarlet scouts, magicians, and preservers guard the trails to intercept any intruders approaching from the lower glades. For the zealots within the nearby monastery, these overgrown steps serve as both a defensive bulwark and a solemn reminder of the ceaseless war against the undead.

subzone:wild-shore.text: Wild Shore. The Wild Shore is the southernmost coastline of Stranglethorn Vale, where the jungle meets the waves of the South Seas. It serves as a staging ground and anchorage for the Bloodsail Buccaneers, whose ships lie moored along the shallows. Stretching along the bottom tip of the continent, the Wild Shore marks the border where Stranglethorn Vale plunges into the South Seas. To the northwest lies the fortified inlet of Booty Bay, while a shallow ocean strait separates the mainland beach from Jaguero Isle to the east. The beach continues northeast toward the Crystal Shore. Because of its secluded position away from the Blackwater Raiders' direct cannons, the coast has become a hotbed of piratical activity and wild perils. The shore is heavily occupied by the Bloodsail Buccaneers, who anchor their wooden ships in the surf and pitch camps along the sand. These swashbucklers use the beaches to stage operations, store illicit cargo, and plan strikes against their goblin rivals. Travelers must also contend with natural hazards of the shore, including prowling beasts and Gorlash, a colossal sea giant who stomps through the surf, crushing anyone caught lingering along the tide line.

subzone:windbreak-canyon.text: Windbreak Canyon. Windbreak Canyon is a winding gorge along the northern side of Thousand Needles, situated between Freewind Post and the Shimmering Flats. Famous for its harsh drafts and jagged stone, it is heavily infested with nesting wind serpents. Travelers passing along the main road must tread carefully near its mouth to avoid being hunted from above. Carved into the sheer northern walls of the canyon floor, Windbreak Canyon spans a large stretch of territory east of Freewind Post. Rather than offering shelter, the ravine channels whistling winds between the rock spires, creating ideal perches for feral wind serpents. The predators lay their clutches along the stone ledges and strike at unwary travelers drifting off the main road. Those braving the canyon interior will also find the winding trails that climb upward toward the Weathered Nook.

subzone:winterfall-village.text: Winterfall Village. Winterfall Village is a sprawling furbolg encampment nestled in the snowdrifts of eastern Winterspring, just east of Everlook. Once peaceful kin to the other ursine tribes of Kalimdor, the Winterfall furbolgs living here have descended into madness and violent corruption under the rule of High Chief Winterfall. Sprawled across the terraced snowbanks east of the goblin trading post Everlook, Winterfall Village serves as the primary bastion of the Winterfall furbolgs in Winterspring. Like their cousins scattered across northern Kalimdor, these bear-folk were warped and driven mad by the lingering foulness of the Burning Legion's invasion. Led by High Chief Winterfall from a secluded cavern atop the settlement's highest tier, the tribe has abandoned its ancestral ways. Instead of communing peacefully with the wild spirits of the snow, the enraged furbolgs now aggressively assault travelers, patrol the mountain passes, and threaten any who come near their frost-bitten home.

subzone:witch-hill.text: Witch Hill. Witch Hill is a dreary, mist-shrouded rise in the heart of Dustwallow Marsh along the path toward Theramore. It is best known for the secluded Swamplight Manor, scattered camps of hostile Mirefin murlocs, and sinister rumors of dark hauntings. Rising out of the stagnant waters of Dustwallow Marsh, Witch Hill sits roughly a third of the way along the peninsula leading southeast toward Theramore Isle. The elevated ground provides little refuge from the hazards of the swamp, as aggressive Mirefin murlocs claim the surrounding waters. At its center stands Swamplight Manor, the lonely and unsettling residence of the hermit known as 'Swamp Eye' Jarl. Travelers passing through frequently report eerie phenomena and lingering dark presences across the knoll.

subzone:witherbark-village.text: Witherbark Village. Witherbark Village is a forest troll settlement nestled around a secluded lake in the southeastern hills of the Arathi Highlands. Inhabited by the hostile Witherbark tribe, it serves as a staging ground for troll raiders contesting both the Alliance remnants of Stromgarde and the Horde outpost at Hammerfall. Built along the shores of a quiet mountain lake, Witherbark Village houses the fierce forest trolls of the Witherbark tribe. While fishers, axe throwers, and witch doctors occupy the hut-lined waterfront, tribal leaders such as Zalas Witherbark and deadly shadow hunters oversee operations from a massive cavern cavern tucked behind the settlement. The Witherbark maintain an opportunistic alliance with the Boulderfist ogres of Arathi, working together to carve out territory across the highlands—even establishing a firm foothold amidst the ruins of Stromgarde Keep. Fiercely territorial, they lash out at any outsider venturing into their corner of the basin.

subzone:woodpaw-den.text: Woodpaw Den. Woodpaw Den is a rugged gnoll stronghold nestled in southern Feralas, just north of the ancient Darkmist Ruins. The settlement serves as a major gathering point for the Woodpaw gnolls and their fiercest pack alphas, making it a dangerous pocket of wilderness within the dense canopy. Situated amidst the towering boughs of Feralas, Woodpaw Den stands as the fortified heartland of the local Woodpaw gnolls. Unlike smaller scout camps scattered along the jungle tracks, this encampment is heavily guarded by the pack's seasoned Alphas. The gnolls here defend their territory fiercely against both intruding adventurers and the encroaching wilderness. Located just north of the elven remnants at Darkmist Ruins, the den represents an ever-present predatory threat to travelers attempting to traverse the central wilderness of the region.

subzone:woodpaw-hills.text: Woodpaw Hills. The Woodpaw Hills are a rugged, forested stretch of southeastern Feralas claimed by the Woodpaw gnolls. Once a dominant tribal territory, the hills have become an embattled frontline as insectoid terrors tunnel up from below and ancient stone giants stalk the canopy. The dense forests of the Woodpaw Hills serve as the historical territory of the Woodpaw gnoll clan. While the hyena-folk once roamed unchallenged across these slopes, their dominance has crumbled under pressure from multiple fronts. To their southeast, nightmarish silithid swarmers have breached the earth at the Writhing Deep, forcing the gnolls back and compelling their chieftains to retreat deeper into the Woodpaw Den. Adding to the peril, ancient mountain giants—relics summoned down during the Third War to repel the Burning Legion—now wander the hillside woods, crushing any travelers or Horde interlopers who stray into their path.

subzone:workshop-entrance.text: Workshop Entrance. Past the Train Depot, Workshop Entrance offers another way into Gnomeregan. The passage skirts the front gates and reaches the Engineering Labs in the irradiated city. Past the Train Depot, Workshop Entrance crosses the cavernous workshop floor toward Gnomeregan’s industrial heart. The opening to the Loading Room lies on one side. The passage runs straight to the Engineering Labs, away from the fortified gates near the surface. There, leper gnomes and troggs contest the way. Those seeking to reclaim the underground capital can use this side door to bypass the first perimeter.

subzone:writhing-deep.text: Writhing Deep. The Writhing Deep is a massive, insectoid hive complex carved into southeastern Feralas. Inhabited by the Zukk'ash silithid, this subterranean burrow is a growing danger that threatens nearby wildlife and surrounding encampments alike. The relentless expansion of these subterranean predators has upset the regional balance of the lush forest. Tucked away in the humid lowlands of southeastern Feralas, the Writhing Deep serves as the primary colony for the Zukk'ash silithid. Unlike the typical woodland beasts of the valley, these chittering insects dig labyrinthine tunnels and fiercely guard clutches of resinous eggs. The hive's aggressive encroachment into the nearby territories has destabilized the wild fauna and agitated local gnoll packs, pushing displaced and frenzied predators uncomfortably close to both Horde paths and native sanctuaries.

subzone:writhing-haunt.text: Writhing Haunt. The Writhing Haunt is a blighted farmstead situated east of the Ruins of Andorhal in the Western Plaguelands. Once fertile land that fed Lordaeron, it has been seized by the Scourge and transformed into a toxic spreading ground for plague vapors. Like many of the old human homesteads surrounding Andorhal, the farmstead now called the Writhing Haunt fell swiftly during the Third War. Today, the fields do not grow crops but instead harvest rot. The Scourge planted an enormous plague cauldron squarely in the center of the tilled earth, continuously venting noxious, diseased vapors into the air. Rotting ghouls, freezing ghouls, and fetid zombies wander the overgrown furrows, guarding the machinery under the command of Cauldron Lord Razarch. Despite the omnipresent danger of the Scourge and the choking miasma from the cauldron, the farm is not entirely abandoned. Inside one of the dilapidated farmhouses lingers Mulgris Deepriver, a tauren druid who came to these lands to heal the damage done to nature. Stricken by the plague himself and unable to cure the suffering beasts, he asks capable travelers to grant the diseased wolves and other wildlife a swift and merciful release.

subzone:wyrmbog.text: Wyrmbog. Wyrmbog is the perilous southern expanse of Dustwallow Marsh, lying just south of the Dragonmurk. Dominated by foul mire and jagged spires of stone, it serves as the staging ground and territorial buffer for the black dragonflight. The caves of ancient wyrms, including the broodmother Onyxia and the elder Emberstrife, are carved directly into its surrounding ridges. Wyrmbog represents the most heavily infested black dragon territory in southern Kalimdor. Where the open waters of Dustwallow give way to scorched muck and towering bones, whelps and mature drakes patrol the fetid air. The bog is choked with toxic fumes and predatory beasts driven wild by the draconic presence. Travelers foolish enough to wander into these reaches find themselves directly in the shadow of Onyxia's Lair and Emberstrife's cavernous den.

subzone:yojamba-isle.text: Yojamba Isle. Yojamba Isle is a cluster of small tropical islets off the northwestern coast of Stranglethorn Vale, near the waters leading up to Westfall. It serves as an offshore encampment for the scholarly Zandalar Tribe, who have established a foothold here to observe the growing crisis in the jungle. From these shores, the Zandalari seek willing champions from both the Horde and the Alliance to confront the ancient horrors awakening in Zul'Gurub. While most trolls encountered across Stranglethorn Vale are hostile to outsiders, the Zandalar tribe dwelling on Yojamba Isle maintain an uneasy neutrality. As the ancient priests and lorekeepers of troll civilization, the Zandalari have watched with mounting dread as the Gurubashi trolls within Zul'Gurub turned to Hakkar the Soulflayer. Knowing the world-ending danger a fully summoned blood god represents, the Zandalari have ventured far from their ancestral home to establish this staging ground, calling upon any capable adventurer—regardless of faction—to aid in curbing the threat. The island rests quietly along the coastline northwest of the Vile Reef and the ruins that haunt the mainland beaches. To the north lies the massive hidden sea-gate of Ironclad Cove, while the surrounding shallows are frequented by wandering sea beasts. Despite its precarious location, the Zandalari camp functions as a tranquil sanctuary where exotic rituals, sacred altars, and ancient knowledge provide solace and power to those preparing to march deep into the jungle's darkest ruins.

subzone:zalashji-s-den.text: Zalashji's Den. Zalashji's Den is a secluded cave tucked along the eastern coast of Tanaris. It serves as the solitary lair of Zalashji, an enigmatic naga who dwells far from the typical gathering grounds of his serpentine kin. Carved into the rugged bluffs along the eastern shoreline of Tanaris, this coastal cavern provides shelter to a single inhabitant: Zalashji. Naga are known across Kalimdor to gather in disciplined war parties or coastal outposts, yet Zalashji resides here entirely alone. Little is known about why he made this isolated cave his domain, far removed from the primary settlements and desert ruins of the region, but any traveler venturing along the surf should approach the cave mouth with caution.

subzone:zul-farrak.text: Zul'Farrak. Zul'Farrak is a sprawling, sun-baked sandstone city tucked into the northwestern cliffs of Tanaris. Long isolated from the rest of their kind, the Sandfury trolls defend this ancient stronghold with fanatic zeal, dark voodoo, and a hoard of undead risen from their sandy graves. Little of Zul'Farrak's distant past survives beyond troll legend, but the Sandfury trolls who hold it have long endured the searing, arid wastes of Tanaris. Known across the desert for their particular ruthlessness, their priests now practice a brutal brand of dark mysticism, exhuming their own dead to build a shambling army within their sun-bleached walls. Whispers throughout Gadgetzan tell of treasures and terrors hidden behind Zul'Farrak's guarded gates. Troll lore speaks of Sul'thraze the Lasher, a legendary broadsword broken into two separate blades that remain hidden somewhere in the city. More alarming are the tales of a band of mercenaries led by Sergeant Bly who wandered into the city and were captured, as well as rumors of Gahz'rilla, an ancient hydra demigod slumbering within a sacred pool at the city's heart.

subzone:zul-gurub.text: Zul'Gurub. Zul'Gurub is an ancient temple city nestled deep in the jungles of northeastern Stranglethorn Vale. Once the glorious heart of the sprawling Gurubashi Empire, it now stands as a perilous stronghold where jungle trolls scheme to summon an ancient, terrible entity into the world. Thousands of years ago, Zul'Gurub reigned supreme as the vibrant capital of the entire Gurubashi Empire, uniting the jungle troll tribes under its grand stone ziggurats. That golden age shattered roughly fifteen hundred years before the opening of the Dark Portal when a vicious civil war tore the empire apart. A radical sect of priests, the Atal'ai, sought to summon Hakkar the Soulflayer—a bloodthirsty ancient god—to seize absolute power. Though loyalist tribes banded together to defeat and banish the Atal'ai northward into the Swamp of Sorrows, the devastation broke the empire's spine, leaving Zul'Gurub a violent shadow of its former grandeur.

subzone:zul-mashar.text: Zul'Mashar. Zul'Mashar is an ancient forest troll settlement tucked into the northeastern corner of the Eastern Plaguelands. Formerly the proud capital of the Mossflayer tribe, it has deteriorated into a desolate ruin following continuous wars with human kingdoms and the devastation of the Plague of Undeath. Today, its remaining defenders face an insidious collapse as the Scourge works from within to turn them into undead thralls. Long before the Scourge swept across northern Lordaeron, Zul'Mashar served as the seat of power for the Mossflayer forest trolls. Constant border skirmishes against the humans of Lordaeron chipped away at their dominance, leaving their territories fractured. When the Plague of Undeath blanketed the region, it struck the Mossflayers just as mercilessly as it did their mortal enemies. While the great stepped ziggurat of Mazra'Alor still stands, Zul'Mashar is a hollow shell of its former glory. Commanded by Warlord Thresh'jin and Zul'Brin Warpbranch, the remaining trolls cling stubbornly to their ancient home, largely blind to the reality that Scourge influence is already seeping into their ranks and quietly transforming their kin into rotting monstrosities.

zone:alteracvalley.text:
Alterac Valley. In Alterac Valley, the Frostwolves and Stormpike dwarves fight for control of the snow. The dwarves seek riches and relics they believe link them to their ancestors, while the Frostwolves fight to drive them out. Each side presses through towers and graveyards toward the other's general: Vanndar Stormpike in Dun Baldar or Drek'Thar in Frostwolf Keep. Gul'dan exiled Durotan's Frostwolf clan for defying him, and the orcs found refuge in this cold valley. They made it their home. Long afterward, young Thrall found his father's people here and learned shaman ways from Drek'Thar, the elder.

Thrall now leads the Horde in Kalimdor. Many Frostwolves remain in the valley under Drek'Thar's guidance, guarding their homeland fiercely. Led by Vanndar Stormpike, the Stormpike Guard is an expedition of Ironforge dwarves based at the northern fortress of Dun Baldar. They came for the valley's mines and for relics they believe link them to their ancestors.

They have dug in with bunkers and towers, holding fast with stubborn pride. The Frostwolves call them invaders; the dwarves claim the valley's secrets by right of discovery. The battle for Alterac Valley pits one army against another. Fighters storm towers and bunkers, seize graveyards, and claim the valley's mines for their side.

Each side must break through to the enemy general and bring them down. The Horde faces Vanndar Stormpike in Dun Baldar; the Alliance faces Drek'Thar in Frostwolf Keep.

zone:arathibasin.text:
Arathi Basin. In Arathi Basin, the League of Arathor and the Defilers fight over the valley's wealth. The League seeks to reclaim Arathor's lost lands for Stormwind, while the Forsaken aim to cut the humans off from their dwarven allies to the south. Its farm, stables, lumber mill, blacksmith and gold mine feed the war. Long before the Third War, Arathi Basin's fields, mills and mines fed Stromgarde, heir to ancient Arathor. When Lordaeron fell and Stromgarde crumbled, the valley was left almost undefended, though its farmsteads and workshops still stood.

Whoever holds them now commands grain, timber, iron and gold. Those stores keep an army in the field, and make this quiet valley one of the most fought-over places in the highlands. The League of Arathor is an Alliance company formed from Stromgarde's survivors and their friends. Backed by Stormwind, they work from Refuge Pointe and have sworn to reclaim the lands their forebears built.

The Defilers are the Forsaken's answer: hardened troops of the Undercity under Varimathras's watchful eye. They fight alongside the Horde at Hammerfall. Their aim is to take the basin's riches and sever the road joining the northern humans to the dwarves of the south. Five strongpoints decide the battle: the farm, the stables, the lumber mill, the blacksmith and the gold mine. Each side races to raise its banner over them and defend what it claims. Every strongpoint held adds to its store of resources.

Raiders slip between the points to seize one while the enemy is busy elsewhere. The side that gathers enough resources first wins the basin, for a time.

zone:darkspearislands.text:
Darkspear Islands. The Horde and Alliance fight across the Darkspear Islands off Kalimdor's coast. The ceremonial isles are sacred to Vol'jin's trolls, while the Alliance seeks a foothold on the shore and a chance to strike at the Horde's pride. Victory goes to the side that holds the strongpoints, seizes the Darkspear Islands flag and gathers 2000 resources first. The Darkspear are an island people. Driven from Stranglethorn Vale by larger, crueler rivals, they made their lives among the islands of the southern seas. They keep these isles off Kalimdor's coast for their rites and the loa they honor.

On islands like these, Thrall's storm-wrecked fleet found Sen'jin's people beset by Kul Tiran sailors, murlocs and a sea witch. There, the trolls first swore themselves to the Horde. To a Darkspear, an enemy banner over the ceremonial grounds means desecration as well as defeat. For the Horde, holding the isles is a debt of honor. The Darkspear stood with Thrall when the Horde had little else, so orcs, tauren and Forsaken fight beside them to keep the trolls' holy ground. For the Alliance, these islands are a foothold off Kalimdor's coast and a way to strike where Horde pride runs deepest. Neither side speaks of peace. Every landing is answered, and every fallen camp is fought over again. Numbers alone cannot hold the islands. The fighting runs from the Camp and the old Ruins to the Abandoned Tower and Shipwreck Cove. Each side builds up its store of resources by capturing and holding the strongpoints. Seizing the Darkspear Islands flag can turn the tide. The first side to gather 2000 resources wins the day and drives its enemies back to their ships, until the next landing.

zone:hyjal.text:
Mount Hyjal. On Mount Hyjal, Nordrassil still crowns the sacred mountain above the second Well of Eternity. In the last battle of the Third War, night elves, humans and orcs held the slopes against the Burning Legion until Archimonde fell at the World Tree's roots. The battle scarred the mountain, and the wounded tree still stands over the Well. Ten thousand years ago, after the Great Sundering, Illidan Stormrage poured stolen waters from the first Well of Eternity into a lake atop Mount Hyjal. There he made a second Well. The Dragon Aspects raised the World Tree Nordrassil over its waters to guard it. Their blessings gave the night elves immortality and bound them deeply to the Emerald Dream. For millennia, the kaldorei watched over the mountain while their druids slept in the barrow deeps beneath it. During the Third War, Archimonde led the Scourge and the Burning Legion up Mount Hyjal to drain the Well and destroy the World Tree. Jaina Proudmoore's humans and Thrall's Horde set aside old hatreds to stand with Tyrande Whisperwind and Malfurion Stormrage.

They held the slopes while Malfurion prepared a trap. When Archimonde reached Nordrassil, Malfurion sounded the Horn of Cenarius. Thousands of wisps swarmed the demon, and the tree's stored power tore him apart. The night elves lost their immortality, and Nordrassil was scorched. Beneath Mount Hyjal lie the barrow deeps, where the Druids of the Claw slept in bear form for thousands of years. Malfurion woke them with the Horn of Cenarius to fight the Legion. Today, the barrow deeps and hyjal summit, high on the mountain, rank among Kalimdor's most perilous places. Only great war bands of seasoned heroes can face them.

zone:warsonggulch.text:
Warsong Gulch. At the border of Ashenvale and the Barrens, Warsong Gulch is where the Horde and Alliance fight without pause. Warsong orcs cut timber for the Horde, while the night elves of Silverwing Hold defend their sacred forest. Fighters of many races raid the opposing stronghold to seize its banner. The Horde builds its home in Kalimdor with wood, much of it cut in Ashenvale. The Warsong clan, Grom Hellscream's warriors, have felled trees here since the Horde first landed. Their Warsong Mill at the gulch's end supplies the Horde's camps and walls. The night elves see each fallen tree as a wound to a forest they have guarded for ten thousand years. They also remember that Grom's warriors slew Cenarius in these woods. The Horde's fighters are the Warsong Outriders, supplied from Mor'shan Base Camp on the northern edge of the Barrens. There, Kelm Hargunth keeps them armed and fed. The Silverwing Sentinels of Silverwing Hold stand against them.

These night elf warriors are sworn to drive every invader from Ashenvale, and Illiyana Moonblaze supplies them at Silverwing Grove. Allies also flock to the gulch: dwarves and humans beside the Sentinels, and tauren, trolls and Forsaken beside the Outriders. The Warsong Mill stands at one end of the gulch, and Silverwing Hold at the other. Each stronghold keeps its side's banner. Fighters raid the enemy's hold, seize its flag and race back as defenders hunt them down. Every banner carried home strikes at the enemy's pride. The side that captures the most wins the day.
